For example, the Pset_WallCommon, that should be attached to walls, contains properties that define if the wall is load-bearing or is exterior or interior.
BIM_IfcProperties.m: Manage → IFC Management → Manage IFC Properties

BIM_IfcQuantities.d:
The IFC Quantities Manager allows you to check the explicit quantities attached to objects, to be exported to IFC.

The IFC format allows to include, for any object, explicit quantities, that can be things like "Width" or "Height" or "Area". There is no standard that defines which object type must include which kind of quantity, and there is also no guarantee that such explicit quantities actually reflect the geometry of the object. In other words, these quantities could have wrong values or even lie. A wall could have its geometry as a cube with a length of 10 meters, but have an attached "Length" quantity of 8 meters.
BIM_IfcQuantities.m: Manage → IFC Management → Manage IFC Quantities

BIM_ImagePlane.d: The BIM ImagePlane tool creates a planar object from an image file. The image is mapped onto a rectangular plane in the 3D View, allowing you to use reference images (such as floor plans, elevations, or sketches) as visual guides during BIM modeling.
u: A file dialog opens.
Select an image file (PNG, JPG, or BMP).
Click two points in the 3D View to define the diagonal corners of the Image Plane.
An Image Plane is created, fitted to the aspect ratio of the original image.

BIM_Layers.d: The Layers Manager allows you to manage layers. Layers are a special kind of group that controls the visual properties of objects placed inside of it. By changing the properties of the layer, such as line width, line color, shape color and transparency, the changes are propagated to its child objects. Layers don't interfere with any other FreeCAD structure such as groups or Building parts, so any object can be part of a layer and part of a group at the same time.
u: Set options and press OK.

BIM_Leader.d: The BIM Leader tool creates a leader line, a Wire object with an arrow symbol at the last selected point. The tool is supposed to be used in conjunction with the BIM Text tool to create annotations in BIM projects.
u: The Leader task panel opens.
Pick the first point in the 3D View, or type coordinates and press the Enter Point button.
Pick additional points in the 3D View, or type coordinates and press the Enter Point button.
Press Esc or the Close button to finish the tool.

BIM_Library.d:
The BIM Library tool allows you to place an object from the Parts Library in the current model.

The library can be accessed offline by downloading the whole workbench via the Addon Manager, or browsed directly from within FreeCAD: in that case, on-demand downloads will be pulled from the Parts Library Git repository.
u: The Library Browser task panel opens
Click a file from the Library Browser
Double-click it or press the Insert button
Click a point in the 3D View or enter a coordinate manually to place the object

BIM_Link.d: The BIM Link command is a shortcut to Std LinkMake, but starts a Draft Move operation immediately after, allowing a link to be created and placed in one go.
u: Select an object.
A link is created from the selected object.
The Draft Move command starts automatically.
Click in the 3D View to place the new link.

BIM_Material.d:
Shows the BIM Material dialog. The dialog allows to quickly and easily perform material-related operations, with extra focus on efficient working with many objects and many materials.

  • Create new material or multi-material.
  • Attribute an existing material or multi-material to selected object(s).
u: Optionally select one or more BIM objects whose DataMaterial property you want to change. Objects without this property can also be selected, but will be ignored.
One of the following happens:

BIM_Preflight.d:
The BIM Preflight tool allows you to perform several tests on your model to verify its compatibility with IFC standards and best practices, and help you to detect possible issues you might want to fix.

As FreeCAD is a very loose and free-style modelling platform, the requirements are very low. You can basically model and organize your BIM model the way you like, using all the tools that FreeCAD offers, both from the BIM Workbench and other workbenches. The IFC format, however, has some strict requirements, and other BIM applications that can read IFC files often bring additional limitations as they more than often have difficulties with certain entities or the way certain objects are modeled.

BIM_Project.d:
The BIM Project tool creates a native IFC project in the current document. In IFC, a project (IfcProject) is the root object of all the contents of the model. It is mandatory to have one in each IFC file.

It is not necessary to create a project to export a FreeCAD model to IFC, as a default one will be added each time you export an IFC file. However, when working with native IFC, an IFC file is attached to the model, and all the geometry and properties of that model and its components come from the attached IFC file. The project is where the IFC file is attached to the document.
u: Make sure you have a FreeCAD document open.
Optionally, lock the document by pressing the IFC Lock button.

BIM_ProjectManager.d: The BIM Project Setup dialog allows you to create a basic set of guide objects in the current document or in a new document, that will help you to start modeling a BIM project.

BIM_Reextrude.d:
The BIM Reextrude tool recreates an extruded solid from the selected face of an existing object. This is useful when you have a face (for example, from a wall or slab) and want to create a new extruded solid based on that face's profile.

The tool takes the selected face, determines its extrusion direction and length based on the original object, and creates a new parametric extrusion.
u: Select a single face of an existing object in the 3D View.
A new extruded object is created based on the selected face. The original object is deleted.

BIM_Report.d:
The BIM Report is a tool for generating schedules and data reports from a FreeCAD model. It uses an SQL-like query language to select, filter, and aggregate data, offering a declarative alternative to other scheduling tools. Ultimately, it enables users to create and automatically populate a spreadsheet with data gathered from the model.

You might choose the BIM Report tool when you need to perform:

  • Complex filtering: Select objects based on a combination of properties, including nested data (e.g., an object's placement coordinates).
  • Data aggregation: Calculate totals, counts, minimums, or maximums across many objects (e.g., find the total area of all "Space" objects).
  • Hierarchical queries: Select objects based on their relationship to other objects (e.g., find all windows hosted in walls on a specific floor).
u: Open or create a FreeCAD document which contains some objects.

The new Report will open its Task Panel automatically. Create one or more statements for the report. You can optionally use the provided statement editor to see a preview of executing those statements.
Press OK to save the report and refresh the associated spreadsheet with the query results.

BIM_Rewire.d: The BIM Rewire tool takes selected objects and attempts to connect their edges into continuous wires. This is useful when you have fragmented line work that should form connected polylines, for example after importing geometry from other applications or after splitting operations.
u: Select two or more objects that contain only straight edges (lines, wires, or shapes with edges).
One or more Draft Wire objects are created from connected edge sequences. The original objects are deleted.

BIM_SetWPFront.d: The BIM SetWPFront tool places the working plane on the global XZ-plane (front).

BIM_SetWPSide.d: The BIM SetWPSide tool places the working plane on the global YZ-plane (side).

BIM_SetWPTop.d: The BIM SetWPTop tool places the working plane on the global XY-plane (ground).

BIM_Setup.d: The preferences system of FreeCAD, located under menu Edit → Preferences, is very complex. The BIM Setup dialog offers a simplified version of it, by gathering the settings most commonly used for BIM work in one simple screen. Changing anything there has the same effect as changing the corresponding setting in the Preferences.

BIM_Shape2DCut.d:
The BIM Shape2DCut tool creates a 2D projection of only the intersecting faces of selected objects on the XY-plane.

This tool is a specialized variant of the BIM Shape2DView tool. It performs the exact same operation, but explicitly sets the resulting object's DataProjection Mode property to Cutfaces.

When used in combination with an Arch SectionPlane, it produces solid filled shapes where the plane physically slices through the 3D geometry. It is typically used alongside BIM Shape2DView to build standard architectural drawings with background lines and solid cut fills.

BIM_Shape2DView.d:
The BIM Shape2DView tool creates a 2D projection of the selected objects on the XY-plane.

It is a specialized wrapper around the Draft Shape2DView tool, tailored for architectural workflows. While the Draft tool keeps the 2D projection in its original 3D position by default, the BIM tool explicitly forces the DataInPlace property to false. This strips the projection of its 3D spatial context, flattening it onto the global XY-plane (at Z=0).
u: Select an existing Arch SectionPlane in the Tree View or the 3D View.
A 2D projection of the objects seen by the section plane is created on the XY-plane. The 3D camera orientation is ignored; the projection relies entirely on the section plane's direction.

BIM_Sketch.d:
The BIM Sketch tool creates a new sketch on the current Working Plane and opens the Sketcher Dialog to edit it.

While the standard Sketcher NewSketch tool opens a dialog to select a base plane or maps to a selected face, the BIM Sketch tool is optimized for quicker BIM workflows. It ignores current selections and directly places the new sketch on the orientation and origin of the current Working Plane.
u: Ensure the Working Plane is set to the desired orientation and position (e.g., set to a face or a level).
The interface switches to the Sketcher Workbench and the Sketcher Dialog (task panel) opens.
Create the desired geometry using the Sketcher tools.
When finished, press the Close button in the task panel.

BIM_Slab.d:
The BIM Slab tool creates a Slab object, a horizontal structure element, from a planar shape. Slabs are specialized Arch Structure objects with their DataIfc Type preset to "Slab".

While it behaves like a standard Arch Structure, the BIM tool specifically initializes the slab with a default height (thickness) of 200 mm and an extrusion direction pointing downwards.
u: Optionally select a planar object.
If you have not yet selected a planar object: select one (as prompted in the Report View).
A new Slab object is created and the tool is finished.
Optionally change some properties in the Property View.

BIM_TDPage.d: The BIM TDPage tool creates a new TechDraw page from a template.

BIM_TDView.d: The BIM TDView tool creates a new TechDraw view from a section plane or 2D objects.

BIM_Text.d: The BIM Text tool creates a text, either a Text object, in the current 3D View, or an Annotation object on the current TechDraw page.

BIM_TogglePanels.d: The BIM TogglePanels tool toggles the display of bottom panels (Report View and Python Console) on or off.

BIM_Trash.d: The BIM Trash tool moves the selected objects to the "Trash" group. The Trash group will be created if not already present in the document. The Trash group is simply a hidden group, that allows you to not permanently delete objects, but still retain them in the document. This is useful when you are unsure if you'll need objects later, or if an object cannot be deleted because other objects depend on it.

BIM_Unclone.d: The BIM Unclone tool converts a Clone object into an independent copy of the original object. The resulting object is no longer linked to the original obejct. Changes to the original object will not affect the uncloned copy, and vice versa.
u: Select a single clone object in the 3D View or the Tree View.
The clone is replaced with an independent copy of its original object.

BIM_Views.d:
The BIM Views Manager is a dockable window that opens below the normal Tree View, that contains all the Building Parts and Working Plane Proxies of your model in the top part. Drawing Views and TechDraw Pages are listed in the bottom part.

The aim of this window is to allow you to quickly access your levels and working plane configurations, without the need to navigate the tree to find them. It also enables accessing existing pages and drawings.

BIM_WPView.d: The BIM WPView tool centers the view on the current working plane.

BIM_Windows.d: The BIM Windows Manager dialog allows you to browse and modify all the windows and doors of your project together. This is often more convenient than editing them one by one, and allows you to make sure that they all have the parameters you require correctly set, such as tag, dimensions, description or material.

CAM_Adaptive.d: The CAM Adaptive command creates clearing and profiling paths. The operation varies cutter engagement so that the material removal never exceeds a maximum value.
u: Select the tool controller for the Operation from the Tool controller dialogue pop up window, if prompted.
Adjust the operation depths as needed in the Depths tab: Start Depth, Finish Depth, Step Down.
Make adjustments in Heights tab if needed.
Configure settings in the Operations tab:
If you wish to preview the result before accepting the settings, click Apply
Click OK button to confirm and generate paths.

CAM_Array.d: The CAM Array command creates a new path by duplicating another path several times at a certain interval distance.
u: Select the operation you want to repeat
Press Apply
Adjust the desired properties at the data box

CAM_Comment.d: The CAM Comment command inserts a comment. When exporting a project to G-code, the comments will be inserted in the G-code program, and can be read by people reading the file. Some machine controllers will also display comments on their display screens.
u: Write your comment in the Comment property

CAM_Copy.d: The CAM Copy command creates a copy of a selected path.
u: Select a CAM object

CAM_Custom.d:
The CAM Custom command inserts a path object which is built from hand coded custom G-code.

Because the Custom G-code command provides no link to a Tool Controller, if a Tool is used by the custom G-code, the Tool index must be written, along with the Spindle Start M-code, in order that it is passed to the Postprocessor. This ensures that Tool changes and starts will be properly generated.

For example, to convey to the Postprocessor that the Tool used in the Custom G-code operation has Tool index 6, and a Spindle Speed of 10,000, insert the following code at the beginning of the Custom G-code Operation:
u: Write custom G-code in the G Code property of the newly created object. Refer to the CAM scripting page for supported G-code commands.

CAM_Deburr.d: The CAM Deburr command is primarily for deburring an edge.
u: The Deburr task panel opens. See Options.
Select Base Geometry.
Specify the required parameters.

CAM_DressupDogbone.d: The CAM DressupDogbone command dresses up an existing path to overcut corners on inside angles of a profile or contour operation. A cylindrical cutter cannot cut all the way into an acute corner without colliding with the model. In certain cases, it may be preferable to violate the model and ensure that the material at the corner is removed. This is especially necessary if parts are going to intersect/interlock with each other.
u: Select a contour or profile path CAM objects.

CAM_DressupDragKnife.d: The CAM DressupDragKnife command uses a cutting edge on a pivot to cut sheet material like vinyl, cardboard, and leather. The cutting point is not aligned with the center of the spindle but rather follows it as the spindle moves. Because the cutting point is offset, the path must be modified to extend past the endpoint of each segment. Also, the dragknife is incapable of making extremely tight turns. To compensate, a pivot 'corner action' is inserted which momentarily lifts the blade slightly and then pivots into the new position.
u: Select a contour or profile path object.

CAM_DressupLeadInOut.d: The CAM DressupLeadInOut command dresses up an existing path by adding lead-in and lead-out moves at the beginning and end of the toolpath.
u: Select an existing path object.
Adjust the lead-in and lead-out settings in the task panel.
Confirm the dressup.

CAM_DressupPathBoundary.d: The CAM DressupPathBoundary command allows restricting the extent of a path to a smaller part of the object. For example, restricting a profile path to just one face or part of the model.
u: Select a path such as contour, profile or pocket operation.

CAM_DressupRampEntry.d: The CAM DressupRampEntry command dresses up an existing path to add a ramp entry.
u: Select a contour or profile path objects.

CAM_DressupTag.d:
The CAM DressupTag command dresses up an existing path (usually a 2D contour cutting path) to leave tags that hold the part in place. Without them a part (which is not fixed to the base) is liable to fly off the machine uncontrollably as the final cut is made. The tags are intended to be broken off by hand (or using a chisel) and then filed flat to finish the part.

A video explanation of this feature is given at: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JZ4prlR6sps
u: Select a contour or profile path objects.

CAM_Drilling.d: The CAM Drilling command generates a drilling Operation in the Job.
u: In the Operation section:

In the Base Geometry section confirm that the list matches the holes that are intended for processing, and adjust add, enable, or disable, as necessary. Holes can be added by selecting the wall faces of the Holes.
In the Depths section check, and if required adjust, the Start Depth and Final Depth.
In the Heights section check, and if required adjust, the Safe Height and the Clearance Height.

CAM_Engrave.d: The CAM Engrave command is primarily for engraving a Draft ShapeString onto a part. It can also be used with other flat 2D geometry, for example imported SVG-based shapes.
u: In the Base Geometry section, select the geometry to engrave and press Add.
In the Depths section, check and adjust the depth settings as required.
Confirm the operation.

CAM_ExportTemplate.d:
The CAM ExportTemplate tool provides a convenient mechanism to save commonly used Job definitions from within an existing Job. This facilitates the setup of future Jobs, that are largely similar, by allowing Job template import during the Job creation process.

The Edit → Preferences → CAM → Job Preferences → Defaults → Template sets the default template.
u: Select elements for inclusion from the Export Template configuration dialog.
The template must be saved in the Macro directory or the CAM directory, as configured in the CAM Preferences.
The template name must follow the pattern of job_<template name>.json. When shown in the selection combobox, the job_ prefix and the extension are left out.

CAM_Fixture.d:
The tool Fixture sets the Work Offset Coordinate Fixture of the machine CNC controller.

Target Work Offset Coordinates typically include: Fixtures G53 to G59. The G-code is simply the Fixture (G53, G54, etc...). The coordinate offset fixtures represent:

  • G53 → Machine coordinate system.
  • G54 → Scratchpad coordinate system.
  • G55 to G59.9 → Coordinate fixtures allowing work offsets, relative to Homing switches located on the CNC machine, to be used.
u: Select the desired Work Offset Fixture from the drop-menu.

CAM_Helix.d: The CAM Helix command appends a helical clearing operation to the Job. Clockwise Helix outputs (G2) G-Code commands. Counterclockwise outputs (G3) G-Code commands. Step Over percentage specifies the concentric step-over as a percentage of the Tool diameter. One or more helical paths will be created at progressively different diameters, to clear the hole.

CAM_Inspect.d: The CAM Inspect command allows inspection of the internal FreeCAD G-code dialect contents of a CAM Operation object.
u: Select a CAM object.

CAM_Job.d:
The CAM Job command creates a new Job object in the active document. The Job object contains the following information:

  • A list of Tool-Controller definitions, specifying the geometry, Feeds, and Speeds for the Path Operations Tools.
  • A Workflow sequential list of Path Operations.
  • A Base Body—a clone used for offset.
  • A Stock, representing the raw material that will be milled to CAM Workbench.
  • A SetupSheet, containing inputs used by the Path Operations, including static values and formulas.
  • Configuration parameters specifying the output G-Code job's destination path, file name, and extension, and the postprocessor (used to generate the appropriate dialect for the target CNC Controller, and customize Units, Tool Changes, Parking, etc.).

CAM_MillFace.d:
The CAM MillFace command creates a path to perform a facing operation on a horizontal surface. This operation is generally used:

  • to smooth out a rough stock surface,
  • to mill selected face(s) to desired depth in preparation for performing subsequent clearing operations within the boundary of the regions affected by this operation,
  • or to apply a finishing surface to the selected face(s).

This operation contains a DataBoundaryShape property that allows for a modified selection area based upon the selected face(s).
u: Select one or more faces to be surfaced. Note: If selected faces exist at different heights, then all will be milled to the Final Depth setting.
Select the correct DataBoundaryShape setting to modify the milling area based on the face(s) selected as Base Geometry.
Adjust the other properties as needed. They are listed further below.

CAM_OpActiveToggle.d:
The CAM OpActiveToggle command toggles the DataActive property of a selected CAM operation.

If this property is set to false, the operation is treated as inactive. Its path is not shown in the 3D View, and it is ignored by commands such as CAM Inspect and CAM Post.
u: Select an operation in the Operations group belonging to a Job. A deactivated operation can be recognized by its grayed out label and icon.
The result depends on the selected operation:

CAM_Pocket3D.d: The CAM Pocket3D command inserts a 3D Pocket object into the Job. This operation takes into account the bottom surface of the pocket, as well as selected walls that are not vertical. In its current state, this operation is used to rough out a pocket with non-vertical walls and/or non-horizontal bottom. A common finishing technique is to use a ball end mill with the experimental 3D Surface operation.
u: From within a Job, select one or more Faces from the Job Model to include as the Base Geometry.
Choose a Tool controller from the pop up selection dialogue window.
Add or subtract Base Geometry elements as needed to configure the Operation.
Check the Depths tab to ensure the Start Depth, Finish Depth, and Step Down percentage are correct. The Final Depth is determined by the Body Geometry selection and is not modifiable.
Check the Heights tab to ensure the Safe and Clearance Heights are appropriate.

Check the Operation tab where the Tool controller can be re-selected, the Cut mode can be configured for Climb or Conventional milling, the Pattern can be set, the Step Over percentage can be adjusted, and Pass Extension can…

CAM_Pocket_Shape.d:
The CAM Pocket Shape command creates a pocketing operation from selected bottom faces, or walls, of one or more pockets of the jobs base object.

The CAM Pocket Shape object is made to be part of a CAM Job.
u: Select the bottom or the wall(s) of a pocket. While it is usually easier to select the bottom, the walls have to be selected when a pocket goes through all.
(v26.3): Horizontal edges can also be selected. Edges are combined into wires, and a closed horizontal wire is converted into a pocket face.
Adjust the desired properties.

CAM_Post.d:
The CAM Post command exports the selected CAM Job to a G-code file.

Each CNC Controller speaks a specific G-code dialect, requiring a Dialect-correct Postprocessor to translate the final output from the agnostic internal FreeCAD G-code dialect.

  • Using a correct Job output G-code file extension.
  • Selecting the G-code commands. CNC controllers typically support a subset of available G-code commands. The super-set of G-code commands contains powerful and specialized commands that otherwise must be processed using multiple simpler commands. Postprocessors are written to select the best G-code for an Operation, available on the target.
  • Formatting the G-code syntax by reordering the Feed, X, Y, Z, A, and B inputs, and the precision.
  • Inserting a Pre-amble to set units, units format, Work plane, coordinate system, etc...
  • Inserting a Post-amble to park the machine, stop it, process any arguments.
  • Inserting Tool changes, or suppressing them between subsequent operations using the same tool.
u: Select a CAM Job in the Tree View.
Confirm the Output File name and directory

CAM_Profile.d:
The CAM Profile command creates a contour operation based on selected features of the model. It offers three operations that were handled by separate tools in previous versions.

All operations create objects that are made to be part of a CAM Job.

These are the available operations:

A Contour operation is the default. It creates a simple external contour cut of complex 3D Part-based objects. The entire Job Model serves as the input for the Operation, regardless of whether any Body Geometry is selected when the Contour command is invoked.
u: Activate the Base Geometry section by clicking its tab, and select features from the Job model.
Activate the Operation section by clicking on its tab, and adjust the operation's settings as desired.
Optionally press the Apply button to preview the operation with the current settings.
Click the OK button or the Cancel button to create or cancel the operation.

CAM_Sanity.d:
Many CAM users are hobbyists and DIYers. As such, they use their CNC machines to run G-code that they configured and generated themselves. That isn't the case for most professional and commercial users. In professional shops, different people are responsible for creating the G-code and for running it on the machine.

Hobbyists usually run the G-code shortly after post-processing it and probably only once or twice. In a professional shop, proven G-code may be run many times over a long period.
u: Select a CAM Job in the Tree View.
If necessary, set the DataOutputFile property of the Job before running the command.
FreeCAD generates a standalone HTML report for the selected Job.
The report is written to the same location as the configured Job output file.
The generated report is opened in the system's default web browser.

CAM_SelectLoop.d: The CAM SelectLoop command completes a selection of edges that form a loop.
u: Select an edge.
The remaining edges of the loop are added to the selection.

CAM_Shape.d:
The CAM Shape command doesn't match the current CAM workflow. For that reason it's moved to the experimental features.

This tool generates tool-paths from CAM Object edges.

Tool-paths are uncompensated for tool radius. There is no Tool controller associated with the generated tool-paths.
u: Select edges by selecting the entire object from the 3D View or Tree View, or by selecting individual edges, or by Faces from the 3D View.
CAM_Shape.m: CAM → Supplemental Commands → Path From Shape TC

CAM_SimpleCopy.d:
The CAM SimpleCopy command creates a non-parametric copy of a given path.

(v26.3): The command can combine multiple selected operations into one simple copy.
u: Select one or more CAM objects.

CAM_Simulator.d: The CAM Simulator command allows Simulation of the CAM Job by sweeping 3D Models of the Tools used in each Operation, along the G-Code paths, subtracting material from the Stock, where the stock and tool overlap, providing visualization of the Job. This allows detection and isolation of errors prior to running the Job on a mill.
u: De-select any Operations that are not to be simulated
Tune the Speed and Accuracy settings.
Select the Job for simulation from the drop menu.
Use the Path Simulator toolbar to invoke different actions:

CAM_SimulatorGL.d: The CAM SimulatorGL command is a new alternative to Legacy CAM Simulator. It's based on low-level OpenGL functions. To eliminate interference with the 3D View of FreeCAD, it works in a separate window with a separate OpenGL context. It's meant to be faster and more precise than the old simulator.
u: De-select any Operations that are not to be simulated
Tune the Accuracy setting.
Select the Job for simulation from the drop menu.

CAM_Slot.d:
The CAM Slot command creates a simple slotting operation using various methods of input.

Inputs include:

  • selecting one or more faces or edges.
  • selecting two vertices.
  • entering two custom points.

The CAM Slot object is made to be part of a CAM Job.
u: Select the reference geometry on the model:
Invoke the Slot command using several methods:
Adjust the desired properties. Descriptions of available properties are found below.

CAM_Stop.d:
The CAM Stop command inserts a Stop command (M1). This command will Pause a running program on the CNC controller, waiting for user interaction to continue.

Note: this does not stop the spindle.

CAM_Surface.d: The CAM Surface command creates a new 3D Surface operation which is capable of generating G-code paths for the entire top surface of a 3D model (or is able to work with selected faces) and allows for faces to be avoided. This operation offers multiple cut patterns: Line, Zigzag, Circular, Circular Zigzag, Offset, and Spiral (similar to an adaptive pattern). As of version 0.19, this operation offers many customizations to allow for greater productivity.
u: Select the tool controller for the Operation from the Tool controller dialogue pop up window, if presented.
In the Base Geometry tab, select any specific faces you wish to focus on and/or avoid for the operation.
Adjust the operation depths as needed in the Depths tab: Start Depth, Finish Depth, Step Down.
Make adjustments in Heights tab if needed.
Configure settings in the Operations tab as needed:
If you wish to preview the result before accepting the settings, click Apply

CAM_ToolBitDock.d:
The CAM ToolBitDock command opens the Toolbit Selector.

The purpose of the selector is to display the currently selected library and allow the user to quickly add tool controllers to the CAM Job(s).

Double-clicking on a toolbit will create a single tool controller for the toolbit. Multi-selecting toolbits and pressing the 'Add to Job' button will create tool controllers for all toolbits in the library.

The user may also select multiple tools and use the 'add...' button at the bottom to add tool controllers for the selection.
u: There are several ways to open the Toolbit Selector:
Use the selector to add tool controllers to a CAM Job.

CAM_ToolBitLibraryOpen.d:
The CAM ToolBitLibraryOpen command is for creating, managing, and organize toolbits. Launching the library manager will display the manager as a modal dialog.

From here the user can perform all task related to toolbit management:

  • Select a default library
  • Create/edit/delete Toolbits
  • Create libraries
  • Modify libraries by adding and removing toolbits
  • Save a library to a new name
  • Export a library to the LinuxCNC tooltable (.tbl) format
u: There are several ways to open the Toolbit Library Manager:
Select a library from the list.
Create/Add/Remove toolbits from the library.
Double-click a row to edit the toolbit.
Close the manager.
The selected library will become the default library for the dock.

CAM_Vcarve.d:
The CAM Vcarve command is primarily for center-line engraving a Draft ShapeString onto a part. However, it may be useful for other kinds of 2D.

Unlike engraving which follows the lines in the shapestring, V-carving uses a V-shaped cutter and attempts to clear the area by moving the cutter down the center of the region and varying the depth of cut. Since a v-cutter radius varies with the depth, the width of cut varies as well. The result is a more natural looking cut, particularly for serif fonts.

CAM_Waterline.d:
The CAM Waterline command creates a new Waterline operation. As of 0.19_pre, the operation works on the entire model to generate G-code for the Job. Currently, within the operation's settings there is no functionality to select specific areas, faces, or regions of the model.

The Waterline operation has three algorithms: OCL Dropcutter, OCL Adaptive, and Experimental.

  • The OCL Dropcutter and OCL Adaptive algorithms interface to OCL.pyd, a 3rd party Open Source module titled OpenCamLib, that generates tool paths from a 3D Model. OpenCamLib is not integrated directly into FreeCAD.
  • (v26.3): The OCL Adaptive algorithm is available. It can generate smoother paths more quickly for suitable models. It is not restricted by Waterline boundaries; use a Boundary Dressup if required.
  • The Experimental algorithm makes use of the built-in Path.Area() class.
u: Select the tool controller for the Operation from the Tool controller dialogue pop up window.
Adjust the operation depths as needed in the Depths tab: Start Depth, Final Depth, Step Down.
Make adjustments in Heights tab if needed.
Configure settings in the Operations tab based on the Algorithm selected:
If you wish to preview the result before accepting the settings, click Apply
Click OK button to confirm and generate paths.

Cables_AddVertex.d: The Add Vertex adds a new vertex to the WireFlex object. It preserves proper assignment of existing attachments of wire vertexes. It can be used interchangeably with the "Add point" command from Cables Edit, see the WireFlex Description.
u: Select one edge of an existing WireFlex object in the 3D View.
Create a new vertex of WireFlex by one of these methods:

Cables_AttachInPlace.d:
The Attach In Place makes an attachment of an object without changing its global position. The Map Mode property of an attached object is set to Object XY, the Attacher Engine is set to Engine 3D. The Attachment Offset property is calculated automatically.

This is useful when, for example, there are two objects that already have final distance and rotation between them and one of them has to be moved to a new place. This tool allows to build attachment keeping the distance and rotation between these objects untouched. Once the connection is established, moving the base object will not change the relative position of the attached object.
u: Select two or more objects in the 3D View or Tree View holding the CTRL key. The last selected object will be the Attachment Support for other selected objects.
Create an Attach In Place attachment by one of these methods:

Cables_AttachVertex.d:
The Attach Vertex attaches an existing vertex of WireFlex to external vertex or object. Attachments of vertexes are kept in special properties of WireFlex, for details see WireFlex Properties.

It can be used interchangeably with the "Attach point" command from Cables Edit, see the WireFlex Description.

Once attached the wire vertex keeps the same position in 3D space as the external vertex to which it is attached to. When the external vertex is moved, the attached wire vertex moves together with it. When the wire is edited in the Cables Edit the attached vertex can not be moved. It jumps back to its attached position.
u: Select one vertex of an existing WireFlex object in the 3D View.
Select one external vertex in the 3D View holding the CTRL key.
Create a new WireFlex vertex attachment by one of these methods:

Cables_AttachWireToTerminal.d:
The Attach Wire To Terminal attaches two initial or two final vertices of WireFlex to existing CableTerminal. Attachments of vertices are kept in special properties of WireFlex, for details see WireFlex Properties.

The electrical connection between terminal and wire is established. The terminal properties from the Net group are updated accordingly.

Once attached the connected wire vertices keep the same position in 3D space as the CableTerminal to which they are attached to. When the CableTerminal is moved, the attached wire vertices move together with it. When the wire is edited in the Cables Edit the attached vertices can not be moved. They jump back to their attached position.
u: Use one of the WireFlex selection methods:
Use one of the CableTerminal selection methods holding the CTRL:
Run an Attach Wire To Terminal command by one of these methods:
Cables_AttachWireToTerminal.m: Cable Wires → Attach Wire To Terminal

Cables_Cable.d:
The Cable creates a Cable object based on selected Cables WireFlex and Cables Profile. The CompoundPath can also be selected as a base wire (v0.2.0). The Cable is fully parametric and is derived from Arch Pipe and inherits all of its properties. Some properties specific for Arch Pipe are hidden and not used by Cable.

The Cable automatically creates several subcomponents based on a given Profile. These are:
u: Select the existing WireFlex or CompoundPath in the 3D View.
Optionally select the existing Cable Profile in the 3D View or Tree View holding the CTRL key.If the profile is not selected, a single-wire cable will be created.
Create cable by one of these methods:

Cables_CableBox.d:
New concept of Cable Box Preset and SnapLines child object: (v0.3.0)

The Cable Box creates a parametric cable box object. It has default size upon creation, but some parameters, like Diameter, Height or Thickness can be changed later. The Cable Box belongs to the Arch Component class and inherits all of its properties. The Cable Box has inlet holes equipped with SnapLines crosses. Each SnapLines cross has five vertices which can be used as attachment supports for up to five cables entering single hole. SnapLines object is not a part of Cable Box shape, it is a separate child object also visible in the Tree View.
u: Select the vertex, point on surface or object in the 3D View or select nothing.
Create Cable Box by one of these methods:
The Cable Box task panel opens. See Options for more information.

Cables_CableConduit.d:
The Cables CableConduit tool creates a CableConduit object based on selected Cables WireFlex or Cables CompoundPath and optionally a profile. The CableConduit is fully parametric and is derived from Arch Pipe and inherits all of its properties.

This element is designed to model additional layers used to build cable conduits, harnesses or cable assemblies. It can group other conduits or cables as its children under Tree View and take a shape which is a compound of its own parametric shape and shapes of its children.
u: Select at least one existing wire object (see Note 1) in the 3D View or Tree View.
Create CableConduit by one of these methods:

Cables_CableConnector.d:
New concept of Cable Connector Preset with CableTerminal and SnapLines as child objects: (v0.3.0)

The Cable Connector represents a model of an electrical connector. Its shape can be selected from DataPreset list upon creation. There are two shape types available: first one fully parametric called 'ParametricTerminal' and second one called 'Fixed'.

The 'ParametricTerminal' type creates a parametric connector object. The connector is a model of electrically conductive metal block (for simplicity without external insulation). From an electrical point of view, all wires connected to a connector form one electrical node. The connector has default size upon creation, but some parameters, like Height, Hole Size, Hole Diameter or Number of Holes can be changed during creation after selection 'Customized' preset or later by changing properties. In this mode the single CableTerminal is created, split to segments passing through each connector hole.
u: Select the vertex, point on surface or object in the 3D View or select nothing.
Create Cable Connector by one of these methods:
The Cable Connector task panel opens. See Options for more information.

Cables_CableLightPoint.d:
New concept of Cable Light Point Preset and SnapLines child object: (v0.3.0)

The Cable Light Point creates a parametric light point object. The light point is a simple ring symbolizing the point where a cable exits from e.g. the wall to connect a light source (e.g. a lamp). It has default size upon creation, but some parameters, like Diameter, Height or Thickness can be changed later. The Cable Light Point belongs to the Arch Component class and inherits all of its properties. The Cable Light Point has SnapLines child object with two crosses. Each SnapLines cross can be used as attachment supports for cable passing through the ring. SnapLines object is not a part of Cable Light Point shape, it is a separate child object also visible in the Tree View.
u: Select the vertex, point on surface or object in the 3D View or select nothing.
Create Cable Light Point by one of these methods:

Cables_CableTerminal.d:
The CableTerminal is a dependent object and cannot be created directly.

It represents electrical connection point for Cable. It can be created as a child object during creation of: CableConnector, ElectricalDevice. Its main purpose is to indicate position for cable end inside connector or electrical device. If more cable wires have to be connected to single terminal it can be split into segments allowing more items to connect to them. The CableTerminal is fully parametric, which means it has configurable length, number of allowed connections and placement relative to its parent.

Cables_CompoundPath.d:
The CompoundPath command is designed to create a wire object based on a group of other wire objects. Its topological shape is a compound of wire shapes or a single wire shape.

It is possible to use CompoundPath as a base for Cable or CableConduit. Proper combination of WireFlex and CompoundPath can be used to simplify process of creation complex cable bundles or cables inside cable conduits avoiding unnecessary redundant base wires. Single WireFlex object can be a part of a few different CompoundPath objects influencing their shapes.
u: Select at least two existing wire objects (see Note 1) in the 3D View or Tree View.
Create CompoundPath by one of these methods:

Cables_DeactivateAttachment.d:
The Deactivate Attachment disables current attachment of an object. The Map Mode property of an object is set to Deactivated, other attachment properties remain untouched.

This is useful when the attachment is not needed temporary. Deactivated Map Mode enables precise object movement e.g. with TransformManip tool. After placement correction the AttachInPlace tool can be used to apply corrected Attachment Offset property.
u: Select one or more objects in the 3D View or Tree View holding the CTRL key.
Deactivate Attachment of all selected objects by one of these methods:

Cables_DelVertex.d: The Delete Vertex deletes an existing vertex from WireFlex object. It preserves proper assignment of existing attachments of wire vertexes. It can be used interchangeably with the "Delete point" command from Cables Edit, see the WireFlex Description.
u: Select one mid vertex of an existing WireFlex object in the 3D View.
Delete selected vertex of WireFlex by one of these methods:

Cables_DetachWireFromTerminal.d:
The Detach Wire From Terminal detaches previously attached vertices of WireFlex from existing CableTerminal. Attachments of vertices are removed from special properties of WireFlex, for details see WireFlex Properties.

Detachment does not change existing terminal or wire positions. The electrical connection between terminal and wire no longer exists. The terminal properties from the Net group are updated accordingly.
u: Select WireFlex object in the 3D View or in the Tree View.
Select CableTerminal in the 3D View or in the Tree View holding the CTRL.
Run an Detach Wire From Terminal command by one of these methods:
Cables_DetachWireFromTerminal.m: Cable Wires → Detach Wire From Terminal

Cables_Edit.d: The Cables Edit command is an extended version of the Draft Edit command which is compatible with the WireFlex objects. It preserves all properties of WireFlex (especially points attachments) while adding or removing vertexes. Editing can be performed with non zero Fillet Radius property and with any value of Path Type property. While in Cables Edit mode, all WireFlex editing commands can be executed using node or edge context menu: Add Vertex, Delete Vertex, Attach Vertex, Remove Vertex Attachment.
u: Optionally select one or more WireFlex objects. Note that although multiple objects can be in Cables Edit mode, objects can only be edited one at a time.

Cables_ElectricalDevice.d:
The Electrical Device represents a model of any electrical device that has the possibility of direct cable connection. Its shape can be selected from DataPreset list upon creation. There is only non parametric shape type available. It is called 'Fixed'.

The 'Fixed' shape type creates non parametric device object with a shape taken from external STEP file. There are a few predefined STEP device models shipped together with Cables Workbench. Moreover, the user can create their own device library, this is described in Electrical Device presets. In addition to the shape the certain number of CableTerminals are created with predefined size and position corresponding to connection points. Additionally one or more SnapLines objects can be created forming the basis for the cable entering the device.
u: Select the vertex, point on surface or object in the 3D View or select nothing.
Create Electrical Device by one of these methods:
The Electrical Device task panel opens. See Options for more information.

Cables_LayersExtended.d:
The Layers Extended are a predefined set of layers, each of which is an extended version of a Draft Layer. The extended layer in addition to the standard properties of a Draft Layer, allows to define the color and size of the points of elements belonging to the layer. Each extended layer has also Auto Member Type property which is designed to automatically collect layer elements.

Extended layers were created to make it easier to organize WireFlex lines, SupportLines, SupportPoints, SnapLines, CableTerminals. These layers allow you to quickly and easily assign ungrouped objects of a specific type to the appropriate layer, and then hide or show them, as well as apply bulk changes to their view properties.
u: Create default set of extended layers by one of these methods:

Cables_Material.d: The Material creates a series of Arch Materials and Arch Multimaterials ready to use with Cable or Cable Box. The following default multimaterials are suitable for Cable: cableMultiMat3w, cableMultiMat5w, cableMultiMat8w. They have proper naming of their composition which corresponds to default names in Sub Colors property of a Cable. The ((v0.3.0)) boxMultiMat2m multimaterial can be used by CableBox equipped with DIN rails.
u: Create default set of multimaterials by one of these methods:

Cables_Profile.d:
The Cable Profile creates a Sketch object which represents the base profile (cross-section) of a cable. The profile is fully parametric and is created by choosing different cable properties in a dialog box (see Usage). The profile contains all the cross-section information needed for a Cable creation.

There are few predefined cable profile types, e.g. YDYp (flat power cable), YDY (round power cable). Additional custom profile types can be defined by the user (see Adding custom profile types).
u: Create cable profile by one of these methods:
The Add a new cable profile task panel opens.
Select the Preset ((v0.3.1)).
Optionally select the Profile type or any of its parameters (after selecting the option Show details).
Select the Number of wires.
Select the Standard gauge [mm2] from the list or leave custom.

Cables_RemoveVertexAttachment.d:
The Remove Vertex Attachment removes an existing vertex attachment of WireFlex from external vertex or object. Attachments of vertexes are kept in special properties of WireFlex, for details see WireFlex Properties.

It can be used interchangeably with the "Remove point attachment" command from Cables Edit, see the WireFlex Description.

Once attachment is removed the wire vertex can be moved freely in 3D space using Cables Edit command.
u: Select one vertex of an existing WireFlex object in the 3D View.
Remove selected vertex attachment by one of these methods:

Cables_SnapLines.d:
NOTE: Starting with version 0.3.6, the object's name has been changed from SuppLines to SnapLines, which, in the author’s opinion, better reflects the object’s function and is hopefuly more suitable for translation. This change is backward compatible. All models created previously using the old name will continue to function properly.

The SnapLines is a dependent object and cannot be created directly.

Cables_SupportLine.d: The Support Line creates a simple Draft Line in bright color and with enlarged vertexes. It serves as support for creating WireFlex. Its Attachment properties can be used e.g. to group cables around a Cable Box or other objects, for attaching cables to walls or ceilings etc.
u: Select the vertex, point on surface or object in the 3D View or select nothing.
Create Support Line by one of these methods:

Cables_SupportPoint.d: The Support Point creates a Draft Point in bright color. It serves as support for creating WireFlex. Its has additional Attachment properties which can be used e.g. for attaching cables to walls or ceilings etc. The Support Point has the same purpose as Support Line and can serve as its complement.

Cables_WireFlex.d: The WireFlex object is derived from Draft Wire and inherits all its properties. The main difference is that WireFlex is able to attach every of its vertexes to external vertex or object (attachment to object is understood as an attachment to its Placement.Base). Not every vertex has to be attached, some of them can be left to move freely depending on current needs. Another difference is that the WireFlex can take on three different shapes (see Path Type Proterty).
u: Select the first external existing vertex in the 3D View
Select additional vertexes (one or more) in the 3D View holding the CTRL key.
It is also acceptable to select nothing, then the default wire with 5cm length will be created ((v0.3.0)).
Create WireFlex by one of these methods:

CfdOF_Analysis.d: The CfdOF Analysis command creates an Analysis container to hold all objects of a Computational Fluid Dynamic Analysis. This container is mandatory. A document can contain multiple Analysis containers.
u: A CfdAnalysis container is created and set to active.
The following objects are automatically created inside the container:
Several commands can add objects to the container.

CfdOF_FluidMaterial.d: The CfdOF FluidMaterial command opens a task panel to edit a Fluid Properties‏‎ object. This object holds the properties of a fluid used in a simulation. These can be entered manually, or selected from a fluid library. One Fluid Properties‏‎ object is automatically added when an Analysis container is created. In case of a multi-phase Physics Model, additional fluids can be defined by adding more Fluid Properties‏‎ objects.
u: If required: activate the correct Analysis container by double-clicking it in the Tree View.
Ensure the DataPhase property of the Physics Model in the container is set to FreeSurface.
A FluidProperties data object is added to the container.
The task panel opens. See Options for more information.

CfdOF_MeshFromShape.d: The CfdOF MeshFromShape command creates an object that holds data to build a mesh from geometry. The data can be edited in a task panel.
u: If required: activate the correct Analysis container by double-clicking it in the Tree View.
Select the geometry to be meshed.
A [GeometryName]_Mesh data object is added to the container.
The task panel opens. See Options for more information.

CfdOF_MeshRegion.d: The CfdOF MeshRegion command creates an object that holds data to add surface, volume and extrusion refinements to a background mesh. The data can be edited in a task panel.
u: Select a [GeometryName]_Mesh data object in the Tree View.
A MeshRefinement data object is added to the [GeometryName]_Mesh data object.
The task panel opens. See Options for more information.
Optionally repeat the command to add more refinement data objects to the [GeometryName]_Mesh data object.

CfdOF_SolverControl.d: The CfdOF SolverControl command opens a task panel to solve the analysis using OpenFOAM and open the results in Paraview.

CurvedShapes_CurvedArray.d: Creates an array and resizes the items in the bounds of one or more hull curves. In this example, the orange base shape is rescaled in the bounds of the red and violet hullcurves. The curves do not have to be connected. The hullcurves should lie on or parallel to the XY- XZ- or YZ- plane.
u: Select the input curves.
In the Property View, adjust the number of items, as well as the offset end and start parameters, to create the desired shape.
In the Property View, select the checkbox for 'Surface' or 'Solid' depending on the desired result

CurvedShapes_CurvedSegment.d: Interpolates between two 2D curves. The interpolated curves can be resized in the bounds of some hullcurves.
u: Select two sketches that shall be start and end of the interpolation.

CurvedShapes_InterpolatedMiddle.d: Interpolates a shape between two 2D curves. The interpolation can be used to form a surface or a solid.
u: Select two sketches that shall be used.

CurvedShapes_SurfaceCut.d:
Cuts through a surface and makes the crossection available. Normal vector and position can be freely chosen to get the desired cut.

This command is similar to Part CrossSections, but it is fully parametric and has an option to reduce the complexity of the output curve. It tries to remove overlapping edges.
u: Select the surface to cut through

Curves_AdjacentFaces.d: The Curves AdjacentFaces tool selects the adjacent faces of the selected sub shape.
u: Select one or more vertices, edges, and/or faces.
The selection is extended around each selected element.

Curves_Approximate.d:
The Curves Approximate tool approximates points to NURBS curve or surface.

Unlike the Curves Interpolate tool, which aims to generate a curve passing through all points, it aims to create a smoother curve by passing within a specified approximation distance of the points.
u: Select one or more objects that contain at least two vertices each.
An Approximation_Curve object is created for each selected object.
Optionally edit the values in the Property View to choose a different approximation method and parametrization type and also adjust the related properties.

Curves_BSplineToConsole.d: The Curves BSplineToConsole tool creates a Python script to (re-)create the selected B-spline or Bézier geometries.
u: Select one or more Bezier or BSpline curves or surfaces in the 3D View.

A BSplineCurve object is created for each selected curve, and a BSplineSurface object for each selected surface, and a related Python script to (re)create each curve or surface can be found in the Python Console.

Curves_BlendSolid.d: The Curves BlendSolid tool creates a solid between two edges with some continuity with their support shapes.
u: Select two faces of different solids.
A Blend_Solid object is created.
Optionally edit the values in the Property View to choose a different auto scale method and adjust the related properties.

Curves_BlendSurf2.d: The Curves BlendSurf2 tool creates a surface between two edges with some continuity with their support faces.
u: Select four sub shapes:
A Blend_Surface object is created.
Optionally edit the values in the Property View to choose a different auto scale method and adjust the related properties.

Curves_CompressionSpring.d: The Curves CompressionSpring tool creates a compression spring.
u: A CompSpring object is created showing the spine (wire) only.
Optionally edit the values in the Property View to display the solid shape and adjust the related properties.

Curves_CurveOnSurface.d: The Curves CurveOnSurface tool projects a curve on a face and optionally creates a normal or binormal face.
u: Select a curve and a support face.
A CurveOnSurface object is created.
Optionally edit the values in the Property View to add a normal or binormal face and adjust the related properties.

Curves_Discretize.d: The Curves Discretize tool discretizes an edge or a wire and therefore creates a set of points along the edge/wire according to a chosen discretization method.
u: Select one or more edges in the 3D View.
A Discretized_Edge object is created for each selected edge.
Optionally edit the values in the Property View to choose a different discretization method and adjust the related properties.

Curves_DraftAnalysis.d: The Curves DraftAnalysis tool creates a colored overlay on an object to visualize draft angles.
u: Select one or more shapes.
A DraftAnalysis object is created for each selected shape.

Curves_EditableSpline.d: The Curves EditableSpline tool creates a freehand B-spline curve.
u: Optionally select vertices, edges and/or faces:
A Freehand_BSpline object is created and set in a special edit mode.
Drag the spline into the desired shape. for details
Press Q, or right-click the spline in the Tree View and select the Finish editing option in the context menu to exit the edit mode and finish the command.

Curves_ExtendCurve.d: The Curves ExtendCurve tool extends selected edges at both ends by a given distance.
u: Select one or more edges in the 3D View.
An ExtendedCurve object is created for each selected edge.
Optionally edit the values in the Property View to adjust extension lengths and types as well as the output shape.

Curves_ExtractSubshape.d: The Curves ExtractSubshape tool creates non-parametric copies of selected sub shapes.
u: Select one or more sub shapes (Faces, edges, vertices).
A copy of each selected sub shape is created.

Curves_FlattenFace.d: The Curves FlattenFace tool creates a flat developed face from conical or cylindrical faces.
u: Select one or more conical or cylindrical faces.
A Flatten object is created for each selected face.

Curves_GeomInfo.d: The Curves GeomInfo tool toggles the display of information about selected shapes.
u: The state of the button changes and information is shown or hidden accordingly.

Curves_GordonSurface.d:
The Curves GordonSurface tool spans a surface on a grid of guide curves and profile curves.

At least a frame of 2 guide curves and 2 profile curves is needed for a Gordon surface, additional curves in between allow for a more detailed control of its curvature.
u: Select the lines that define the grid of the surface in the appropriate order:
A Gordon object is created.
Optionally edit the values in the Property View to choose a different output type and adjust the related properties.

Curves_Interpolate.d:
The Curves Interpolate tool interpolates points with a B-spline curve.

Unlike the Curves Approximate tool, which aims to create as smooth a curve as possible by deviating from the points up to an approximation distance, it aims to generate a curve passing through all points.
u: Select several vertices or one object containing at least 2 vertices.
An Interpolation_Curve object is created.

Curves_IsoCurve.d: The Curves IsoCurve tool applies a UV oriented lattice onto selected surfaces.
u: Select one or more faces in the 3D View.
A IsoCurve object is created for each selected face, applying a UV oriented lattice on each face.
Optionally edit the values in the Property View to change the numbers of iso curves along U and V directions and adjust the related properties.

Curves_JoinCurve.d: The Curves JoinCurve tool joins selected edges into a B-spline curve.
u: Select one or more edges in 3D View.
A JoinCurve object is created.
Optionally edit the values in the Property View to select a different parametrization method and adjust the related properties.

Curves_Line.d: The Curves Line tool creates a parametric line between two vertices.
u: Select two vertices in the 3D View.
A Line object is created.

Curves_MixedCurve.d: The Curves MixedCurve tool creates a 3D intersection curve, a Mixed_curve object, of two projected curves. Optionally it can connect each source curve and the intersection curve with a ruled surface.
u: Select two curves.
A Mixed_Curve object is created.
In the Property View edit the DataDirection1 and DataDirection2 properties to set the projection directions.This is optional if both selected curves were made with the Sketcher Workbench.

Curves_MultiLoft.d: The Curves MultiLoft tool lofts profile objects made of multiple faces in parallel.
u: A MultiLoft object is created.

Curves_ParametricBlendCurve.d: The Curves ParametricBlendCurve tool creates a Blend curve between two edges.
u: Select two curves.
A Blend_Curve object is created.
Optionally adjust values in the Property View:

Curves_ParametricComb.d:
The Curves ParametricComb tool can help to visualize the regularity or smoothness of a curve as well as the continuity between two curves.

Note: A comb is only for visualization.

A 3D comb will be created for 3D curves. Sample and scale can be changed.
u: Select one or more shapes (sketch, wire, face, etc.).
A Comb object is created, showing the curvature of the select shapes (sketches, wires), or their sub elements (borders and iso-curves in case of faces).
Optionally edit the values in the Property View:

Curves_ParametricSolid.d: The Curves ParametricSolid tool creates a parametric solid from selected faces.
u: Select some faces in the 3D view, or some objects in the Tree View.
A Solid object is created, its status and according icon describe the result:
Optionally edit the values in the Property View to add more surface elements or to display the open edges of surface shapes only.

Curves_PasteSVG.d: The Curves PasteSVG tool pastes the SVG content of the clipboard into the 3D View.
u: Copy the desired SVG content (code) to the clipboard.
For each recognized SVG element a separate object is created.

Curves_PipeShell.d: The Curves Pipeshell creates a Pipeshell sweep object. This tool is part of the external workbench called Curves.
u: Switch to the Curves workbench (install from Addon Manager is necessary, if not previously installed)
Select the edge that builds the sweep path in the 3D view
Select one or more required profiles in the Tree view
To invoke the command, do one of the following:
Change the Pipeshell parameter to the required conditions

Curves_Pipeshell.d: The Curves Pipeshell tool creates a Pipeshell sweep object.
u: Select the edge that builds the sweep path in the 3D View.
Select one or more required profiles in the Tree View.
A PipeShell object is created.
Optionally edit the values in the Property View to choose a different sweeping algorithm, or a different output shape and adjust the related properties.

Curves_PipeshellProfile.d: The Curves PipeshellProfile tool creates a Profile object for Pipeshell.
u: A Profile object is created.

Curves_ProfileSupport.d: The Curves ProfileSupport tool creates a support plane for sketches.
u: A Profile object is created.

Curves_ReflectLines.d: The Curves ReflectLines tool creates the reflect lines on a shape, according to a view direction.
u: Select an object.
If the selected object is not a ReflectLines object a ReflectLines object is created.
The view direction of the ReflectLines object will be set according to the current camera direction.
Optionally edit the values in the Property View to choose the lines to be created, and where they are placed and also adjust the related properties.

Curves_RotationSweep.d: The Curves RotationSweep tool sweeps profiles along a spine (sweep path) or a point.
u: Select a spine and some profiles in the 3D View.
A Rotation_Sweep object is created.

Curves_SegmentSurface.d: The Curves SegmentSurface tool allows to segment a surface on isocurves.
u: Select a face in the 3D View.
A Segment_Surface object is created.
Optionally edit the values in the Property View to adjust the related properties.

Curves_SketchOnSurface.d: The Curves SketchOnSurface tool maps a sketch onto an arbitrary curved face, like a label on a bottle. The sketch must be actually attached to a face (see Sketch.Support). The Map mode of the sketch has no effect on the result.
u: Select the target face in the 3D View.
A Sketch_On_Surface object is created including a Mapped_Sketch object.
Expand this object in the Tree View to make the Mapped_Sketch appear below.
Edit the sketch and add geometries inside the blue construction bounds.

Optionally edit the values in the Property View to create extruded faces, or fill faces and equidistant faces from closed sketch wires, which in combination result in a solid shape, and adjust the related properties.
Select one or more edges in the 3D View.
A SplitCurve object is created for each selected edge. The edge is split by Number in 2 equally long curve segments by default.
Optionally edit the values in the Property View to activate different splitting methods by setting the related properties:

Curves_SurfaceAnalysis.d: The Curves SurfaceAnalysis tool creates visual analysis maps on selected shapes.
u: Select one or more sub shapes.
A SurfaceAnalysis object is created and a zebra texture is mapped on the selected objects.
Optionally edit the values in the Property View to choose a different mode and adjust the related properties.

Curves_Sweep2Rails.d: The Curves Sweep2Rails tool creates a sweep either with a ruled surface and a list of profile edges or with two rails and at least two profiles.
u: Do one of the following:
A Sweep_2_rails object is created.

Curves_ToConsole.d: The Curves ToConsole tool gives access to the selected objects in the Python Console.
u: Select one or more objects in the 3D View or in the Tree View.
A list of commands that give access to the objects in the selection, and their actually selected sub-objects is displayed in the Python Console.

Curves_TrimFace.d: The Curves TrimFace tool trims a face with a projected curve.
u: Select a face and a curve.
A TrimmedFace object is created.

Curves_TruncateExtend.d: The Curves TruncateExtend tool cuts a shape and truncates or extends it by a given distance.
u: Select a shape and a plane or only a plane in a PartDesign body.
A Truncated_Extend object is created.

Curves_WaterlineCurves.d: The Curves WaterlineCurves tool creates waterline curves on selected faces.
u: Select one or more faces and/or objects.
One collective Waterline object is created.
Optionally edit the values in the Property View to change the number of waterlines and adjust their orientation.

Curves_ZebraTool.d: The Curves ZebraTool tool creates a Zebra texture for surface inspection.
u: Select the surface to be tested
Optionally change parameters in the Zebra Stripes Tool Task Panel.
Press any button OK, Cancel, or Quit to finish and exit the tool.
