Optionally change the screw diameter of individual edges in the Edges to chamfer list by double-clicking their Diameter field, and selecting a new value from the dropdown list that appears.

Fasteners_ChangeParameters.d: The Fasteners ChangeParameters command can be used to change the parameters of fasteners.
u: Select one or more fasteners. If multiple fasteners are selected they must be either only screws, only washers or only nuts.
The Change fastener parameters task panel opens.
Optionally change the Fastener type.
Optionally change the diameter by doing one of the following:
Optionally check the Set length checkbox and enter a new length. The length must be valid for the fastener.

Fasteners_Flip.d: The Fasteners Flip command inverts the orientation of attached fasteners by changing their DataInvert property.
u: Select one or more attached fasteners. The selection may include unattached fasteners, but these will not be flipped. See Notes.
The orientation of the selected attached fasteners is inverted.

Fasteners_MatchTypeInner.d: The Fasteners MatchTypeInner command behaves as a toggle with the Fasteners MatchTypeOuter command. When Fasteners MatchTypeInner is selected, circular edges are considered to be tap holes when new fasteners are attached to them. This determines the default dimensions of those fasteners. This setting is not used for countersunk screws.
u: The button stays depressed to indicate the selected option.

Fasteners_MatchTypeOuter.d: The Fasteners MatchTypeOuter command behaves as a toggle with the Fasteners MatchTypeInner command. When Fasteners MatchTypeOuter is selected, circular edges are considered to be pass holes when new fasteners are attached to them. This determines the default dimensions of those fasteners. This setting is not used for countersunk screws.
u: The button stays depressed to indicate the selected option.

Fasteners_Move.d: The Fasteners Move command moves and attaches a fastener to a circular edge. It can also be used to detach a fastener. An attached fastener has a DataBase Object and its DataPlacement is dynamically linked to that object.
u: Select a single fastener and a single circular edge.
The fastener moves to the selected edge and is attached to it.

Fasteners_RestoreProperties.d: The Fasteners RestoreProperties command restores fastener objects saved without the Fasteners Workbench.
u: All fasteners in the document are checked and restored if required.

Fasteners_ScrewCalculator.d: The Fasteners ScrewCalculator command shows a calculator to determine the tap hole size of screws.
u: The Screw hole calculator dialog box opens.
Specify the Fastener type and the Screw diameter.
The Suggested hole diameter is displayed.
The dialog box is modeless, meaning it can stay open while you continue working in FreeCAD.

Fasteners_Search.d: The Fasteners Search command shows a dialog box to search and insert fasteners by name or description.
u: The Search Fasteners dialog box opens.
Enter a search term in the input box at the top. At least 2 characters are required.
The list of search results updates as more characters are entered.
Select a fastener from the list.
The dialog is modeless, meaning it can stay open while you continue working in FreeCAD.
Optionally press the Close button to close the dialog box.

Fasteners_Simplify.d: The Fasteners Simplify command creates non-parametric copies of fasteners. This can be useful if you want to share a document containing fasteners with users who do not have the Fasteners Workbench installed.
u: Select one or more fasteners.
For each fastener a simplified copy is created.
The ViewVisibility property of the original fasteners is set to false.
Optionally delete the original fasteners.

FreeGrid_BitCartridgeHolder.d:
The FreeGrid BitCartridgeHolder tool creates a bit cartridge holder.

This tool is part of the FreeGrid Workbench, an external workbench that can be installed with the Addon Manager.
u: A bit cartridge holder is created with properties based on the current preferences.
Optionally select the object and change its properties in the Property editor.

FreeGrid_Sketch.d:
The FreeGrid Sketch tool generates an inner box profile sketch.

This tool is part of the FreeGrid Workbench, an external workbench that can be installed with the Addon Manager.
u: Optionally select an existing storage box.
If no box has been selected:
A sketch is created.

FreeGrid_StorageBox.d:
The FreeGrid StorageBox tool creates a storage box.

This tool is part of the FreeGrid Workbench, an external workbench that can be installed with the Addon Manager.
u: A storage box is created with properties based on the current preferences.
Optionally select the object and change its properties in the Property editor.

FreeGrid_StorageGrid.d:
The FreeGrid StorageGrid tool creates a storage grid.

This tool is part of the FreeGrid Workbench, an external workbench that can be installed with the Addon Manager.
u: A storage grid is created with properties based on the current preferences.
Optionally select the object and change its properties in the Property editor.

GuiCommand_model.d:
While the page is under construction, add the Template:UnfinishedDocu template at the top of the page by simply typing: {{UnfinishedDocu}}

In this first paragraph give a short description of what the command does. The description can refer to other workbenches such as the Sketcher Workbench. (Editor note: The image is 24px, not 16px)

Remember to use Template:Version, Template:VersionMinus, Template:VersionPlus and Template:Obsolete, or their superscript variants Template:VersionNote, Template:VersionNoteMinus, Template:VersionNotePlus and Template:VersionNoteObsolete (to avoid brackets), when applicable.
u: Detailed steps as needed. Some steps may need Keyboard presses while others may require using the mouse to click on a Button.
Set options and press OK.
GuiCommand_model.m: Menu → Submenu → Menu text for the command

Image_CreateImagePlane.d: The CreateImagePlane tool imports a bitmap image and places it on one of the XY, YZ or XZ planes.
u: Select the desired image in your system.
Choose the plane where the image will be placed, give an offset value, and press OK.

Image_Open.d: The Image Open tool simply opens an image from your system in a new tab in the viewport.
u: Select the image file that you want.

Image_Scaling.d: The Image Scaling tool scales an image that was imported with the Image CreateImagePlane tool.
u: Click a first point on the 3D view.
Click a second point on the 3D view.
Select an existing image plane from the Model tree, created with the Image CreateImagePlane tool.
Add a distance in millimeters and press OK.

Lattice2_AttachablePlacement.d: The Lattice2 AttachablePlacement command assigns a placement or handle to an object so it can later be referred to by a location.
u: Switch to the Lattice2 external workbench
Invoke the Attached Placement command several ways:
Choose the options from the dialog menu

Material_Edit.d: The Material Edit tool provides access to the Material Editor which is part of the material system of FreeCAD. The material system can be used by all workbenches. It handles the material properties and also the appearance properties of objects.
u: There are several ways to launch the editor:
Select a material from the multilevel list in the left panel. The following categories are available:
Use the three tabs in the right panel of the editor to edit the properties of the selected material:
Optionally use the buttons on the General tab:
If material properties have been edited: press the Save button to save them.
Do one of the following:
Material_Edit.m: Materials → Edit Model → Materials → Material Editor

MeshPart_CreateFlatFace.d: The MeshPart CreateFlatFace command creates a flat representation of a face of a shape object. The created outline is a Part Feature. At this time the command almost always creates a rectangular outline.
u: Select a single face of a shape object in the 3D View.

MeshPart_CreateFlatMesh.d: The MeshPart CreateFlatMesh command creates a flat representation of a mesh object by unwrapping, unfolding, it. The created outline is a Part Feature.
u: Select a single mesh object. The mesh must be 'unwrappable'. For example, to unwrap a cylindrical mesh it must have open ends and an open seam. Also curved surfaces must have a relatively fine mesh. Use the Mesh RemeshGmsh…

Mesh_AddFacet.d: The Mesh AddFacet command adds faces along a boundary of an open mesh object. It can be used to fill holes.
u: During the command edit mode will be active. In this mode it is impossible to rotate or pan the 3D View, although zooming still works. But you can temporarily switch out of edit mode with the Std ToggleNavigation command…
Select a single open mesh object.
If you hover over a vertex along a boundary of the mesh a yellow marker will appear and a left-click will select it.
Select two additional points to define a triangular face. The order of the three points, clockwise or counterclockwise, determines the direction of the normal of the face.
A menu pops up with the following options:
Optionally add more faces.

Mesh_BoundingBox.d: The Mesh BoundingBox command shows the bounding box coordinates of a mesh object.
u: Select a single mesh object.
The Boundings dialog box opens showing the coordinates of the object's bounding box.
The same information is also displayed in the Report View.

Mesh_BuildRegularSolid.d: The Mesh BuildRegularSolid command creates a regular parametric solid mesh object.
u: The Regular Solid dialog box opens.
First select a mesh object type from the dropdown list:
Specify the required settings. The available settings depend on the mesh object type. See Properties.
For meshes with curved surfaces: a higher Sampling value results in a finer mesh.
Optionally create more mesh objects.

Mesh_CrossSections.d: The Mesh CrossSections command creates multiple cross sections across mesh objects. The cross sections are taken parallel to one of the main global planes (XY, XZ or YZ). For each set of cross sections a single Part Feature is created.
u: Select one or more mesh objects.
The Cross Sections task panel opens.
The planes that will be used to create the cross sections are indicated in the 3D View, and will be updated based on the task panel inputs.
Select the Guiding Plane:

Specify the Position of the guiding plane from the origin. The default position is based on the center of the bounding box of the selected mesh objects. Choosing a different guiding plane or toggling the Sections checkbox will…
Optionally check the Sections checkbox to create multiple cross sections:

Mesh_CurvatureInfo.d: The Mesh CurvatureInfo command shows the absolute curvature of curvature objects at selected points.
u: During the command the 3D View cannot be changed.
Make sure the mesh objects whose curvature objects you want to analyze are invisible.
The cursor changes to a pipette icon.
Select a point on a curvature object.
Optionally toggle the Annotation option from the 3D View context menu to switch from temporary to permanent labels.
Optionally pick more points on curvature objects.

Mesh_Decimating.d: The Mesh Decimating command reduces the number of faces in mesh objects.
u: Select one or more mesh objects.
The Decimating task panel opens.
Specify the Reduction:

Mesh_Difference.d:
The Mesh Difference command creates a new non-parametric mesh object, a Mesh Feature, that is the difference of two mesh objects: one mesh object is cut from the other.

OpenSCAD must be installed to use this command, and the path to its executable must be set in the OpenSCAD preferences.
u: Select the main mesh object.
Add the mesh object you want to cut from the main object to the selection. The mesh objects must overlap.

Mesh_EvaluateFacet.d: The Mesh EvaluateFacet command shows information about faces of mesh objects.
u: It is advisable to enable the Report View. The command will display detailed information there.
The cursor changes to a pipette icon.
Select a face of a mesh object.
Its index is displayed in the 3D View.
Additional information is shown in the Report View:
Optionally select more faces.

Mesh_EvaluateSolid.d: The Mesh EvaluateSolid command checks if a mesh object is solid. A solid mesh object does not have any holes.
u: Select a single mesh object.
The Solid Mesh dialog box opens informing that the selected mesh object is solid or not.

Mesh_Evaluation.d: The Mesh Evaluation command evaluates and repairs a mesh object.
u: Optionally select a single mesh object.
A dockable dialog box opens.
Optionally press the Settings button to change the following settings:
If you have not yet selected a mesh object: select one from the dropdown list at the top of the dialog box.
The dialog contains 7 or 8 (if the Folds on surface option is enabled) test options.
Do not use the checkboxes, they will be checked automatically if errors are found.

Mesh_Export.d: The Mesh Export command exports a mesh object to a mesh file format. Several file formats are supported.
u: Select a single mesh object.
Select the correct file format in the dialog box.
Enter a filename. If you have selected the All files (*.*) option in the previous step, and do not specify a file extension here, the.stl extension will be used.

Mesh_FillInteractiveHole.d: The Mesh FillInteractiveHole command fills selected holes in mesh objects.
u: The cursor changes to a triangle icon.
Select a face that shares an edge with the hole you wish to close.
The hole is closed.
Optionally repeat this to close additional holes.
If required you can use Std Undo to undo the last action of the command.
Select the Leave Hole-Filling Mode option from the 3D View context menu to finish the command.

Mesh_FillupHoles.d: The Mesh FillupHoles command fills holes in mesh objects.
u: Select one or more mesh objects.
The Fill Holes dialog box opens.
Specify the Fill holes with maximum number of edges value.

Mesh_FlipNormals.d: The Mesh FlipNormals command reverses, flips, the normals of mesh objects.
u: Select one or more mesh objects.

Mesh_FromPartShape.d:
The Mesh_FromPartShape command creates non-parametric mesh objects (Mesh Features) from shape objects (Part Features).

This command is the counterpart of the Part ShapeFromMesh command.
u: Optionally select one or more objects.
The Tessellation task panel opens.
While the task panel is open you can create a new selection or change an existing selection.
Select the tab for the mesher you wish to use.
Specify the required settings. See Meshers.

Mesh_HarmonizeNormals.d: The Mesh HarmonizeNormals command harmonizes the normals of mesh objects.
u: Select one or more mesh objects.

Mesh_Import.d: The Mesh Import command imports geometry from a mesh file format into the active document. Several file formats are supported. The command creates a non-parametric mesh object, a Mesh Feature.
u: Optionally select the correct file format in the dialog box.
Select a file.

Mesh_Intersection.d:
The Mesh Intersection command creates a new non-parametric mesh object, a Mesh Feature, that is the intersection (common) of two mesh objects.

OpenSCAD must be installed to use this command, and the path to its executable must be set in the OpenSCAD preferences.
u: Select two mesh objects that partially overlap.

Mesh_Merge.d: The Mesh Merge command creates a new non-parametric mesh object, a Mesh Feature, by combining the meshes of two or more mesh objects. The command does not perform a Boolean union, the new object will contain separate mesh components. For a Boolean union use the Mesh Union command instead. This command is the counterpart of the Mesh SplitComponents command.
u: Select two or more mesh objects.

Mesh_PolyCut.d: The Mesh PolyCut command cuts whole faces from mesh objects.
u: During the command the 3D View cannot be changed. It is advisable to properly line up the 3d View first.
Select one or more mesh objects.
Define a polygon by picking points in the 3D View.
Select an option from the 3D View context menu:

Mesh_PolyTrim.d: The Mesh PolyTrim command trims faces and parts of faces from mesh objects.
u: During the command the 3D View cannot be changed. It is advisable to properly line up the 3d View first.
Select one or more mesh objects.
Define a polygon by picking points in the 3D View.
Select an option from the 3D View context menu:

Mesh_RemeshGmsh.d: The Mesh RemeshGmsh command remeshes a mesh object using the Gmsh mesher. The new mesh can be finer or coarser.
u: Select a single mesh object.
The Remesh by Gmsh task panel opens.
Specify the required settings. See the Gmsh mesher settings of the Mesh FromPartShape command.
Optionally change one or more settings and again press the Apply button until the new mesh is to your liking.

Mesh_RemoveCompByHand.d: The Mesh RemoveCompByHand command removes components from mesh objects.
u: A component refers to a complete group of connected faces. Usually a mesh object contains a single component. But, for example after using the Mesh Merge command, a mesh object can contain multiple components.
The command uses the color red to mark selected components. To see them properly:
The cursor changes to a hand icon.
Select the components you wish to delete in the 3D View.
Optionally select Clear Selected Faces from the 3D View context menu to deselect all components.
Select Delete Selected Faces from the 3D View context menu to delete the selected components.

Mesh_RemoveComponents.d: The Mesh RemoveComponents command removes faces from mesh objects.
u: The command uses the color red to mark selected faces. To see them properly:
The Remove Components task panel opens.
Use one or more of the Select options to select faces:
Optionally use one or more of the Deselect options to deselect faces. These options are identical to the Select options, except that the number of faces for the Components button is a minimum number.
Optionally press the Invert button to invert the selection.
Select one or more mesh objects.
The Scaling dialog box opens.
Specify a scaling factor, the value must be larger than 0.

Mesh_SectionByPlane.d: The Mesh SectionByPlane command creates a cross section across a mesh object with the selected plane. The cross section is a Part Feature.
u: Select a single mesh object and a single Part plane. The (extended) plane should intersect the mesh object.

Mesh_Segmentation.d: The Mesh Segmentation command creates separate mesh segments for specified surface types of a mesh object.
u: Select a single mesh object.
The Mesh Segmentation task panel opens.

Optionally check the Smooth mesh option and specify a value for the smoothness of the mesh. The higher the value the smoother the mesh is assumed to be. Specifying 0 has the same effect as unchecking this option. Do not select…
Select the surface type you wish to create mesh segments for. You can select more than one type, but this can lead to poorer results. The available surface types are:
Specify the required settings. Make sure the Tolerance values are not too low, and the Minimum number of faces values not too high.
The command will create a group containing separate mesh objects, each a segment of the original mesh object.

Mesh_SegmentationBestFit.d: The Mesh SegmentationBestFit command creates separate mesh segments for specified surface types of a mesh object. The command can also identify their parameters which can be useful when re-engineering a mesh object.
u: If you plan to identify the parameters of a surface type, note that the command uses the color red to mark the faces selected for this option. To see them properly:
Select a single mesh object.
The Mesh Segmentation task panel opens.
Optionally press one of the Parameters buttons to identify the parameters of a surface:
Select the surface type(s) you wish to create mesh segments for:
Specify the Tolerance values.

Mesh_Smoothing.d: The Mesh Smoothing command smooths mesh objects by changing the position of their vertices.
u: If you plan to smooth only certain areas, note that the command uses the color red to mark the faces selected for this option. To see them properly:
Select one or more mesh objects.
The Smoothing task panel opens.
If you only want to smooth selected areas: choose the Only selection option:
Select the smoothing Method:
Specify the Parameters:

Mesh_SplitComponents.d: The Mesh SplitComponents command splits a mesh object into its components. A mesh component is a complete group of connected faces. For each component a new non-parametric mesh object, a Mesh Feature, is created. If the original mesh object contains only one component, and this is usually the case, a single new mesh object, effectively a copy, is created. This command is the counterpart of the Mesh Merge command.
u: Select a single mesh object.

Mesh_TrimByPlane.d: The Mesh TrimByPlane command trims faces and parts of faces on one side of a plane from a mesh object.
u: Select a single mesh object and a single Part plane. The (extended) plane should intersect the mesh object.
The Trim With Plane dialog box opens.
Select the side you want to keep by pressing one of the buttons:

Mesh_Union.d:
The Mesh Union command creates a new non-parametric mesh object, a Mesh Feature, that is the union (fusion) of two mesh objects.

OpenSCAD must be installed to use this command, and the path to its executable must be set in the OpenSCAD preferences.
u: Select two mesh objects that partially overlap.

Mesh_VertexCurvature.d: The Mesh VertexCurvature command creates Mesh Curvature objects for mesh objects. A curvature object displays the curvature of a mesh using different colors for the convex, flat and concave parts.
u: Select one or more mesh objects.

OpenSCAD_AddOpenSCADElement.d:
Add an OpenSCAD element by entering OpenSCAD code into the task panel and executing the OpenSCAD binary (requires OpenSCAD)

When as Mesh is selected, OpenSCAD renders a mesh.

Each time Add is pressed the OpenSCAD code is executed and elements are imported.

If OpenSCAD returns successfully, its messages are displayed as warnings in the report window. This will be the case if the path to imported, included and used files is broken. In case of undesired results it is highly recommend to have a look at the report windows, as there might be a lot of other output, created by the importer. If OpenSCAD fails, its messages will be logged as errors.

OpenSCAD_Edgestofaces.d: Converts edges to faces. Useful to prepare imported DXF geometry for extrusion.
u: Select edges to be converted in the 3D view.

OpenSCAD_ExpandPlacements.d: Expand all placements downwards in the Tree View.
u: Select object in the Tree View.

OpenSCAD_ExplodeGroup.d: This feature explodes a fusion or a compound back to single parts applying random colors to these parts.
u: Select fusion/compound to be exploded

OpenSCAD_Hull.d:
Applies a hull to selected shapes.

Example of a hull operation performed on two cylinders
u: Select shapes in Tree view or in 3D view

OpenSCAD_IncreaseToleranceFeature.d: Increases tolerance of edges/faces/vertex of selected object(s).
u: Select object in the tree view
Select Tolerance object in the Tree View.
Select Data tab in Property View or Combo View.
Change values for Edges/Faces/Vertex to your liking.

OpenSCAD_MeshBoolean.d: Creates new Mesh object by boolean operation from shapes.
u: Select shapes in Tree view.
Select Perform.
A new mesh object is created.

OpenSCAD_Minkowski.d:
Applies a Minkowski sum to selected shapes.

Add each element of subset A to each element of subset B to get Minkowski sum.

Sweep element A along all boundaries of element B. Resulting space which is occupied by both elements is Minkowski sum.

Example of Minkowski sum applied to cylinder and cube. Note: that the height of Minkowski sum is height of cylinder plus height of cube.
u: Select shapes in Tree view or in 3D view

OpenSCAD_MirrorMeshFeature.d: Creates a new mirrored Mesh object, mirrored about the selected axis.
u: Select the Mesh object to be mirrored.
Select the desired axis in the dialog, or enter your own custom axis to use and click OK.
A new Mesh object is created and mirrored, the original object is rendered hidden.

OpenSCAD_RefineShapeFeature.d: Cleans unnecessary lines. After a Boolean operation, some lines defining the previous form remain visible, this tool creates a copy of the totally cleaned.
u: Select the shape to be cleaned.
A parent-object is created and totally cleaned, the original object is rendered hidden.

OpenSCAD_RemoveSubtree.d: Removes the selected objects and all children that are not referenced from other objects.
u: Select object(s) to remove.

OpenSCAD_ReplaceObject.d: Replace an object in the Tree View.
u: Multi-select in correct order old, new and parent object in the Tree View.

OpenSCAD_ResizeMeshFeature.d: Creates a new resized Mesh object with independent sizing for each axis.
u: Select the Mesh object to be resized.
Enter the resizing value.
A new Mesh object is created and resized, the original object is rendered hidden.

OpenSCAD_ScaleMeshFeature.d: Creates a new scaled Mesh object with independent scaling for each axis.
u: Select the Mesh object to be scaled.
Enter scaling value.
A new Mesh object is created and scaled, the original object is rendered hidden.

PartDesign_AdditiveBox.d: Inserts a primitive box in the active Body as the first feature, or fuses it to the existing feature(s).
u: The task panel opens.
Set the parameters. (v26.3): If the Show interactive draggers when editing features preference is selected (default), parameters can be adjusted with interactive gizmos in the 3D View.
Optionally set the Attachment.
Click OK.
A Box feature appears under the active Body.
PartDesign_AdditiveBox.m: Part Design → Additive Primitive → Additive Box

PartDesign_AdditiveCone.d: Inserts a primitive cone in the active Body as the first feature, or fuses it to the existing feature(s).
u: Set the Primitive Parameters (for a complete cone, set one of the radii to zero) and the Attachment.
Click OK.
A Cone feature appears under the active Body.
PartDesign_AdditiveCone.m: Part Design → Additive Primitive → Additive Cone

PartDesign_AdditiveCylinder.d: Inserts a primitive cylinder in the active Body as the first feature, or fuses it to the existing feature(s).
u: The task panel opens.
Set the parameters. (v26.3): If the Show interactive draggers when editing features preference is selected (default), some parameters can be adjusted with interactive gizmos in the 3D View.
Optionally set the Attachment.
Click OK.
A Cylinder feature appears under the active Body.
PartDesign_AdditiveCylinder.m: Part Design → Additive Primitive → Additive Cylinder

PartDesign_AdditiveEllipsoid.d: Inserts a primitive ellipsoid in the active Body as the first feature, or fuses it to the existing feature(s).
u: Set the Primitive Parameters and Attachment.
Click OK.
An Ellipsoid feature appears under the active Body.
PartDesign_AdditiveEllipsoid.m: Part Design → Additive Primitive → Additive Ellipsoid

PartDesign_AdditiveHelix.d: The Additive Helix tool creates a solid by sweeping a selected sketch or 2D object along a helix path.
u: Select the sketch to be swept into a helix. A face on the existing solid can alternatively be used.
Set the Helix parameters (see next section).
Inspect the Helix in the view window, to ensure that the parameters do not result in a self intersecting helix.
Press OK.
PartDesign_AdditiveHelix.m: Part Design → Additive Features → Additive Helix

PartDesign_AdditiveLoft.d: The Additive Loft tool creates a solid in the active Body by making a transition between two or more sketches (also referred to as cross-sections). If the Body already contains features, the additive loft will be merged to them.
u: In the Select Attachment dialog select a sketch to be used as base profile object and click OK.
In the Loft Parameters, press the Add Section button.

Select the next sketch in the 3D View. Repeat to select more sketches in the order you want them to be lofted through. You can change the section order any time later in the loft dialog by dragging sections in the list to the…
Set options if needed and click OK.
PartDesign_AdditiveLoft.m: Part Design → Additive Features → Additive Loft

PartDesign_AdditivePipe.d: The Additive Pipe tool creates a solid in the active Body by sweeping one or more sketches (also referred to as cross-sections) along an open or closed path. If the Body already contains features, the additive pipe will be merged to them.
u: Create two separate sketches;

Arrange the two shapes in 3D correctly. It is recommended to place the origin of the cross-section onto the line of the path. The two sketches should in most cases be orthogonal. This can be done with the 'Map Mode' function…
In the Select Attachment dialog select a sketch to be used as a cross-section and click OK.
In the Pipe Parameters under Path to Sweep Along, press the Object button.
Select the sketch to be used as a path in the 3D View. In this case, the whole sketch will be used as a path.
The other settings should work with the default settings in most cases.
PartDesign_AdditivePipe.m: Part Design → Additive Features → Additive Pipe

PartDesign_AdditivePrism.d: Inserts a primitive prism in the active Body as the first feature, or fuses it to the existing feature(s).
u: Set the Primitive Parameters and Attachment.
Click OK.
A Prism feature appears under the active Body.
PartDesign_AdditivePrism.m: Part Design → Additive Primitive → Additive Prism

PartDesign_AdditiveSphere.d: Inserts a primitive sphere in the active Body as the first feature, or fuses it to the existing feature(s).
u: The task panel opens.
Set the parameters. (v26.3): If the Show interactive draggers when editing features preference is selected (default), the radius can be adjusted with an interactive gizmo in the 3D View.
Optionally set the Attachment.
Click OK.
A Sphere feature appears under the active Body.
PartDesign_AdditiveSphere.m: Part Design → Additive Primitive → Additive Sphere

PartDesign_AdditiveTorus.d: Inserts a primitive torus in the active Body as the first feature, or fuses it to the existing feature(s).
u: Set the Primitive Parameters and Attachment.
Click OK.
A Torus feature appears under the active Body.
PartDesign_AdditiveTorus.m: Part Design → Additive Primitive → Additive Torus

PartDesign_AdditiveWedge.d: Inserts a primitive wedge in the active Body as the first feature, or fuses it to the existing feature(s).
u: Set the Primitive Parameters and Attachment.
Click OK.
A Wedge feature appears under the active Body.
PartDesign_AdditiveWedge.m: Part Design → Additive Primitive → Additive Wedge

PartDesign_Body.d:
A PartDesign Body is the base element to create solids shapes with the PartDesign Workbench. It can contain sketches, datum objects, and PartDesign Features that help in building a solid object. A Body is intended to hold a single contiguous solid, but in FreeCAD version 1.0 an experimental property (DataAllow Compound) has been introduced to allow non-contiguous Bodies.

The Body provides an Origin object which includes local X-, Y- and Z-axes, standard planes and an origin point. These elements can be used as references to attach sketches and primitive objects.
u: An empty Body is created and automatically becomes active.
Now you can press New Sketch to create a sketch in the Body that can be used with Pad.
Alternatively, add a primitive PartDesign Feature, for example, Additive Box.

PartDesign_Boolean.d: PartDesign Boolean imports one or more PartDesign Bodies or PartDesign Clones (designated as "tool bodies") into the active PartDesign Body and applies a Boolean operation (fuse, cut or common). Tool bodies can be placed anywhere in the document relative to the active Body; their placement is correctly respected during the operation (v26.3).
u: Activate the Body which is to receive the Boolean feature. Note: It is important that neither the active Body nor any of the features it contains be selected!
In Boolean Parameters, click on the Add Body button. The active body temporarily disappears from the 3D View to facilitate tool body selection.
In the 3D View, select the Body to use in the Boolean feature. Repeat to add more Bodies.
Select the type of Boolean operation in the drop down menu (Fuse, Cut or Common)
Click OK.

PartDesign_Chamfer.d: The PartDesign Chamfer tool creates chamfers on the selected edges of an object. It adds a Chamfer object to the document with its corresponding representation in the Tree View.
u: Optionally activate the Body to chamfer.
There are several ways to select edges to chamfer:
For a chain of tangentially connected edges only a single edge needs to be selected, the chamfer will propagate along the chain.

If there is no active Body, and there are two or more Bodies in the document, the Active Body Required dialog will open and prompt you to activate one. If there is a single Body it will be activated automatically.
The Chamfer Parameters task panel opens. See Options for more information.

PartDesign_CircularPattern.d: The PartDesign CircularPattern tool duplicates selected features or the active body in concentric circular patterns. This tool allows to disable individual pattern elements.
u: Optionally activate the correct Body.
Optionally select one or more features in the Tree View or the 3D View.

If there is no active Body, and there are two or more Bodies in the document, the Active Body Required dialog will open and prompt you to activate one. If there is a single Body it will be activated automatically.
The Circular Pattern Parameters task panel opens. See Options for more information.
PartDesign_CircularPattern.m: Part Design → Transformation Features → Circular Pattern

PartDesign_Clone.d: The Clone tool creates a linked copy of a selected object which will follow any future edits to the original object (except placement). For example, one use case is when you want to do PartDesign Boolean on an object created in another workbench. Most types of objects are accepted, as long as they are solids. If you need to clone multiple objects (i.e., bodies) or a Part Container, you may use Draft Workbench's clone. One caveat is that the Part Design Workbench's clone sets the current placement of the clone as zero (both Cartesian translation and spatial orientations). While the Draft's workbenches clone calculates and sets the numerical values of the current placement and orientation of the cloned objects with respect to the cloned object container.
u: In the Tree View, select the object to be cloned.

PartDesign_CoordinateSystem.d: Creates a local coordinate system which can be used as reference for other datum geometry. It also helps identify the orientation of the referenced datum geometry in 3D space.
u: Define Coordinate System parameters. Select a first reference in the 3D view to filter the available attachment modes.

Depending on the selected reference, there may be one or more attachment modes available in the the list. The most likely one will automatically be selected and shown in bold in the list. The text Attached with mode along with…
To add an additional reference, press the next Reference button. Once pressed its label changes to Selecting... until a selection is made.
Select an attachment mode in the list.
Define Attachment Offset values.
Press OK.
PartDesign_CoordinateSystem.m: Part Design → Create a local coordinate system

PartDesign_Defeaturing.d:
The PartDesign Defeaturing tool is a parametric dress-up feature that removes one or more selected faces from a PartDesign Feature and heals resulting gaps by extending adjacent faces. Unlike the non-parametric Part Defeaturing tool, this feature stays linked to the base feature and updates automatically when it changes.

This is useful for simplifying imported or heavily featured models, for example removing fillets, chamfers, holes, bosses, or other local details that are not needed for a given purpose, such as FEM analysis, 3D printing, or sharing a simplified model.
u: Select one or more faces of a PartDesign Feature to remove.
The Defeaturing Parameters task panel opens, listing the selected faces.
Optionally press the Select toggle button to add more faces to the list, or select one or more entries and press Delete (or use the context menu) to remove them.

A live preview highlights the changed geometry: material removed from the base shape (e.g. filling in a defeatured hole) and material added compared to the base shape (e.g. the filled volume of a removed fillet) are shown…

PartDesign_Draft.d: The PartDesign Draft tool creates angular draft on the selected faces of an object. It adds a Draft object to the document with its corresponding representation in the Tree View.
u: Optionally activate the Body to apply the Draft to.
Select one or more faces of the Body.

If there is no active Body, and there are two or more Bodies in the document, the Active Body Required dialog will open and prompt you to activate one. If there is a single Body it will be activated automatically.
The Draft Parameters task panel opens. See Options for more information.

PartDesign_Fillet.d: The PartDesign Fillet tool creates fillets (rounds) on the selected edges of an object. It adds a Fillet object to the document with its corresponding representation in the Tree View.
u: Optionally activate the Body to fillet.
There are several ways to select edges to fillet:
For a chain of tangentially connected edges only a single edge needs to be selected, the fillet will propagate along the chain.

If there is no active Body, and there are two or more Bodies in the document, the Active Body Required dialog will open and prompt you to activate one. If there is a single Body it will be activated automatically.
The Fillet Parameters task panel opens. See Options for more information.

PartDesign_Groove.d: The Groove tool revolves a selected sketch or profile about a given axis, cutting out material from the support.
u: Select a single sketch or one or more faces from the Body.
Set the Groove Parameters.

PartDesign_Hole.d:
The Hole feature creates one or more holes from a selected sketch's circles and arcs. If arcs are present they must be part of closed contours. All non arc/circle entities are ignored but they still must form closed contours. Many parameters can be set such as threading and size, fit, hole type (countersink, counterbore, straight) and more.

The centers of the circles and arcs are used to position the holes, but please note that their radii are not taken into account. The generated holes will be identical even if the radii vary.
u: If an existing unused sketch is found, it will be used automatically. If more than one sketch is found, a Select Attachment panel appears to make a selection. Alternatively, a sketch can be selected before launching the Hole…
Define the Hole Parameters, that are described in section Options.
Press OK.

PartDesign_InvoluteGear.d:
This tool allows you to create a 2D profile of an involute gear or spline. This 2D profile is fully parametric, and can be padded with the PartDesign Pad or PartDesign AdditiveHelix feature.

For more detailed information see Wikipedia's entries for: Gear and Involute Gear
u: Optionally activate the correct body.
Set the Involute Parameters.
Click OK.
If there was no active body: drag and drop the gear into a body for the application of further features like padding.

PartDesign_Line.d: Creates a datum line which can be used as reference for sketches, other datum geometry or features. For example it can be used as revolution axis for Revolution and Groove features.
u: Define Line parameters. Select a first reference in the 3D view to filter the available attachment modes.

Depending on the selected reference, there may be one or more attachment modes available in the the list. The most likely one will automatically be selected and shown in bold in the list. The text Attached with mode along with…
To add an additional reference, press the next Reference button. Once pressed its label changes to Selecting... until a selection is made.
Select an attachment mode in the list.
Define Attachment Offset values.
Press OK.
PartDesign_Line.m: Part Design → Create a datum → Create a datum line

PartDesign_LinearPattern.d:
The PartDesign LinearPattern tool creates a linear pattern of selected features or the active body (v1.0).

(v26.3): This tool allows to disable individual pattern elements and to edit each offset individually.
u: Optionally activate the correct Body.
Optionally select one or more features in the Tree View or the 3D View.

If there is no active Body, and there are two or more Bodies in the document, the Active Body Required dialog will open and prompt you to activate one. If there is a single Body it will be activated automatically.
The Linear Pattern Parameters task panel opens. See Options for more information.
PartDesign_LinearPattern.m: Part Design → Transformation Features → Linear Pattern

PartDesign_Migrate.d: The PartDesign workbench in FreeCAD v0.17 introduces new tools and elements that are not recognized by older FreeCAD versions (0.16 and older). FreeCAD documents created in older versions can still be opened and edited. To benefit from the new features, they must be migrated via the menu PartDesign → Migrate.
u: Open a FreeCAD document that was created with FreeCAD 0.16 and below
Switch to the PartDesign workbench.
Go to the Part Design → Migrate menu.
If the migration works, a Part container will be created which will hold one or more Bodies, each hosting a chain of features.

PartDesign_Mirrored.d: The PartDesign Mirrored tool mirrors selected features or the active body (v1.0).
u: Optionally activate the correct Body.
Optionally select one or more features.

If there is no active Body, and there are two or more Bodies in the document, the Active Body Required dialog will open and prompt you to activate one. If there is a single Body it will be activated automatically.
The Mirror Parameters task panel opens. See Options for more information.

PartDesign_MoveFeature.d: Move Object To…, as this command is labeled in the context menu, allows moving objects under a Body to another Body. The moved object is placed right below the other Body's tip. Sketches, datum geometry and features are supported.
u: In the Tree View, right-click the object to be moved.
Select the Move Object To… option from the context menu.
In the Select Body dialog, select the Body to move the object to from the drop-down menu.
Press OK.

PartDesign_MoveFeatureInTree.d: Move Feature After…, as this command is labeled in the context menu, allows reordering of objects under a Body. Sketches, datum geometry and features are supported.
u: In the Tree View, select the object(s) to be moved then right-click to open the context menu.
Select the Move Feature After… option from the context menu.
In the Move Feature After… dialog, select the object under which to move the object(s).
Press OK.

PartDesign_MoveTip.d:
Set Tip, as this command is labeled in the context menu, redefines the tip, which is the feature exposed outside of the Body. By default, the tip is the last feature added to the Body; but sometimes it can be useful to temporarily set the tip to a feature earlier in the tree. This may be done to add a sketch, datum geometry or a feature which in retrospect should have been created earlier in the Body's history.

The tip is visually distinguished in the Tree View by an overlay icon consisting of a white arrow inside a green circle. For example, the following feature is the tip:
u: In the Tree View, right-click the feature to set as tip.
Select the Set Tip option from the context menu.
The new tip is set to visible, and all elements below the tip are hidden from view. Elements newly created from that point will be placed under the tip, and above the other existing elements.

PartDesign_MultiTransform.d:
The PartDesign MultiTransform tool creates a pattern of one or more features. The pattern can include multiple transformations where each subsequent transformation is applied to the result of the previous transformation.

The available transformations are: Mirror, Linear Pattern, Polar Pattern, Circular Pattern (v26.3), Path Pattern (v26.3), Point Pattern (v26.3), and Scale. All except the last one are also available as separate tools.
u: Optionally activate the correct Body.
Optionally select one or more features in the Tree View or the 3D View.

If there is no active Body, and there are two or more Bodies in the document, the Active Body Required dialog will open and prompt you to activate one. If there is a single Body it will be activated automatically.
The Multi-Transform Parameters task panel opens. See Options for more information.

PartDesign_NewSketch.d:
This tool creates a new sketch, creates a new PartDesign Body to contain the sketch if one does not exist and automatically opens the Sketcher workbench after creation.

When creating models using the PartDesign workbench, this tool should be preferred to the Sketcher NewSketch tool found in the Sketcher workbench.
u: In the Tasks panel, the Select Attachment dialog is brought up. Select one of the planes in the list or in the 3D View which can be reoriented for better visibility.
Press OK.

The interface automatically switches to the Sketcher workbench and the sketch can be edited. Once the sketch is exited, the interface is brought back to the PartDesign workbench and the 3D View is restored to the view…
Alternatively, a plane or a face on the existing active body can be selected before creating the sketch, in which case the sketch is instantly created.

PartDesign_Pad.d: The Pad tool extrudes a sketch or a face along a straight path.
u: Select a single sketch or one or more faces from the Body.
Set the Pad parameters.

PartDesign_PathPattern.d: The PartDesign PathPattern tool duplicates selected features or the active body along a path. This tool allows to disable individual pattern elements.
u: Optionally activate the correct Body.
Optionally select one or more features in the Tree View or the 3D View.

If there is no active Body, and there are two or more Bodies in the document, the Active Body Required dialog will open and prompt you to activate one. If there is a single Body it will be activated automatically.
The Path Pattern Parameters task panel opens. See Options for more information.
PartDesign_PathPattern.m: Part Design → Transformation Features → Path Pattern

PartDesign_Plane.d:
Creates a datum plane which can be used as reference for sketches or other datum geometry. Sketches can be attached to datum planes.

Datum Plane crossing 3 corners of the Cube with a Cylinder sketched on it using the Datum Plane as its X-Y Plane.
u: Define Plane parameters. Select a first reference in the 3D view to filter the available attachment modes.

Depending on the selected reference, there may be one or more attachment modes available in the the list. The most likely one will automatically be selected and shown in bold in the list. The text Attached with mode along with…
To add an additional reference, press the next Reference button. Once pressed its label changes to Selecting... until a selection is made.
Select an attachment mode in the list.

Offsets: Define Attachment Offset values. Note that the x, y and z offset represent the local coordinate system of the datum plane, not the world coordinate system. Therefore the z-offset is always the offset along the datum…

Rotation: Changing "Around x-axis" makes the plane rotate around its local X-axis. Changing "Around y-axis" makes the plane rotate around its local Y-axis. Changing "Around z-axis" makes the plane rotate around its local Z-axis.
PartDesign_Plane.m: Part Design → Create a datum → Create a datum plane

PartDesign_Pocket.d:
1.1 and below: The Pocket tool cuts solids by extruding a sketch or a face of a solid along a straight path.

(v26.3): The Pocket tool extrudes a sketch or a face along a straight path to create a Pocket feature that is either the result of a Cut or an optional Common operation.

Cuts the overlapping portion of the extruded shape from the base feature.

Keeps the overlapping portion of base feature and extruded shape.
u: Select a single sketch or one or more faces from the Body.
The Pocket Parameters Task Panel opens.

PartDesign_Point.d: Creates a datum point which can be used as reference for sketches or other datum geometry.
u: Define Point parameters. Select a first reference in the 3D view to filter the available attachment modes.

Depending on the selected reference, there may be one or more attachment modes available in the the list. The most likely one will automatically be selected and shown in bold in the list. The text Attached with mode along with…
To add an additional reference, press the next Reference button. Once pressed its label changes to Selecting... until a selection is made.
Select an attachment mode in the list.
Define Attachment Offset values.
Press OK.
PartDesign_Point.m: Part Design → Create a datum → Create a datum point

PartDesign_PointPattern.d: The PartDesign PointPattern tool duplicates selected features or the active body at points from a shape.
u: Optionally activate the correct Body.
Optionally select one or more features in the Tree View or the 3D View.

If there is no active Body, and there are two or more Bodies in the document, the Active Body Required dialog will open and prompt you to activate one. If there is a single Body it will be activated automatically.
The Circular Pattern Parameters task panel opens. See Options for more information.
PartDesign_PointPattern.m: Part Design → Transformation Features → Point Pattern

PartDesign_PolarPattern.d:
The PartDesign PolarPattern tool creates a polar pattern of selected features or the active body (v1.0).

(v26.3): This tool allows to disable individual pattern elements and to edit each angle individually.
u: Optionally activate the correct Body.
Optionally select one or more features in the Tree View or the 3D View.

If there is no active Body, and there are two or more Bodies in the document, the Active Body Required dialog will open and prompt you to activate one. If there is a single Body it will be activated automatically.
The Polar Pattern Parameters task panel opens. See Options for more information.
PartDesign_PolarPattern.m: Part Design → Transformation Features → Polar Pattern

PartDesign_Revolution.d: The Revolution tool creates a solid by revolving a selected sketch or 2D object about a given axis.
u: Select a single sketch or one or more faces from the Body.
Set the Revolution Parameters.

PartDesign_Scaled.d:
PartDesign Scaled is one of the transformation options of Multi-Transform. Contrary to the other options it is not available as a separate tool. It turns a transformation result into a sequence of scaled objects with evenly distributed scale factors. Starting with the unscaled base feature of the previous transformation the scale factor increases or decreases until reaching the given value at the last item.

If there is no previous transformation within the Multi-Transform feature, scaled items will be placed at the same position as the base feature. This may result in unexpected shapes if the base feature isn't covered completely by the scaled object. And thus it is not recommended to use Scale as the first transformation of a Multi-Transform feature.
u: Do one of the following:
The Multi-Transform Parameters task panel opens.
Right-click in the Transformations list and select Add Scale Transformation from the context menu.
A Scale item is added to the list and the task panel is extended at the bottom to allow to set the Factor and Occurrences. See Options for more information.
Press the OK bar at the bottom.

PartDesign_ShapeBinder.d:
The PartDesign ShapeBinder tool creates a shape binder referencing geometry from a single parent object. A ShapeBinder is used inside a PartDesign Body to reference geometry outside the Body. Using external geometry directly in a Body is not allowed and will lead to out of scope errors.

A ShapeBinder will track the relative placement of the referenced geometry, which is useful in the context of creating assemblies, if its DataTrace Support property is set to true. to understand how this works.
u: Activate the Body the ShapeBinder should be nested in.
Optionally select a single object, or one or more subelements belonging to the same parent object. Subelements can only be selected in the 3D View.
The Shape Binder Parameters task panel opens.
Optionally select an object, this is not required if you want the select subelements:
Optionally select subelements:
Optionally remove subelements:

PartDesign_Sprocket.d: This tool allows you to create a 2D profile of a sprocket (or chainwheel). It can be padded with the PartDesign Pad feature.
u: Optionally activate the correct body.
Set the DataNumber Of Teeth and the DataSprocket Reference.
Click OK.
If there was no active body: drag and drop the sprocket into a body for the application of further features like padding.

PartDesign_SubShapeBinder.d:
The PartDesign SubShapeBinder tool creates a shape binder referencing geometry from one or more parent objects. A SubShapeBinder is typically used inside a PartDesign Body to reference geometry outside the Body. Using external geometry directly in a Body is not allowed and will lead to out of scope errors. But a SubShapeBinder can also be used without being nested in a Body.

A SubShapeBinder will track the relative placement of the referenced geometry, which is useful in the context of creating assemblies, but on top of that also has its own placement.
u: If there are multiple Bodies in the document: optionally activate the Body the SubShapeBinder should be nested in.
Select the required geometry. Subelements can only be selected in the 3D View.
The SubShapeBinder is created.

If there is only one Body in the document the SubShapeBinder is automatically added to it and the Body is activated. If this is the case and the SubShapeBinder should not be nested, it can be dragged out of the Body and…

PartDesign_SubtractiveBox.d:
Inserts a subtractive box in the active Body. Its shape is subtracted from the existing solid.

On the left: active body (A) shown in grey and subtractive box (B) shown in transparent red; result on the right.
u: The task panel opens.
Set the parameters. (v26.3): If the Show interactive draggers when editing features preference is selected (default), parameters can be adjusted with interactive gizmos in the 3D View.
Optionally set the Attachment.
Click OK.
A Box feature appears under the active Body.
PartDesign_SubtractiveBox.m: Part Design → Subtractive Primitive → Subtractive Box

PartDesign_SubtractiveCone.d:
Inserts a subtractive cone in the active Body. Its shape is subtracted from the existing solid.

On the left: active body (A) shown in grey and subtractive cone (B) shown in transparent red; result on the right.
u: Set the Primitive Parameters (for a complete cone, set one of the radii to zero) and the Attachment.
Click OK.
A Cone feature appears under the active Body.
PartDesign_SubtractiveCone.m: Part Design → Subtractive Primitive → Subtractive Cone

PartDesign_SubtractiveCylinder.d:
Inserts a subtractive cylinder in the active Body. Its shape is subtracted from the existing solid.

On the left: active body (A) shown in grey and subtractive cylinder (B) shown in transparent red; result on the right.
u: The task panel opens.
Set the parameters. (v26.3): If the Show interactive draggers when editing features preference is selected (default), some parameters can be adjusted with interactive gizmos in the 3D View.
Optionally set the Attachment.
Click OK.
A Cylinder feature appears under the active Body.
PartDesign_SubtractiveCylinder.m: Part Design → Subtractive Primitive → Subtractive Cylinder

PartDesign_SubtractiveEllipsoid.d:
Inserts a subtractive ellipsoid in the active Body. Its shape is subtracted from the existing solid.

On the left: active body (A) shown in grey and subtractive ellipsoid (B) shown in transparent red; result on the right.
u: Set the Primitive Parameters and Attachment.
Click OK.
An Ellipsoid feature appears under the active Body.
PartDesign_SubtractiveEllipsoid.m: Part Design → Subtractive Primitive → Subtractive Ellipsoid

PartDesign_SubtractiveHelix.d: The SubtractiveHelix tool modifies a solid by sweeping a selected sketch or 2D object along a helix path cutting away the material.
u: Select the sketch to be swept into a helix. A face on the existing solid can alternatively be used.
Set the Helix Parameters (see next section).
Inspect the Helix in the view window, to ensure that the parameters do not result in a self intersecting helix.
Press OK.
PartDesign_SubtractiveHelix.m: Part Design → Subtractive Features → Subtractive Helix

PartDesign_SubtractiveLoft.d: Subtractive Loft creates a subtractive solid in the active Body by making a transition between two or more sketches (also referred to as cross-sections). Its shape is then subtracted from the existing solid.
u: In the Select Attachment dialog, select a sketch to be used as base profile object and click OK.
In the Loft Parameters, press the Add Section button.

Select the next sketch in the 3D View. Repeat to select more sketches in the order you want them to be lofted through. (You can change the section order any time later in the loft dialog by dragging sections in the list to the…
Set options if needed and click OK.
PartDesign_SubtractiveLoft.m: Part Design → Substractive Features → Subtractive Loft

PartDesign_SubtractivePipe.d: Subtractive Pipe creates a subtractive solid in the active Body by sweeping one or more sketches (also referred to as cross-sections) along an open or closed path. Its shape is then subtracted from the existing solid. SubtractivePipe is often used in connection with Part Helix and PartDesign ShapeBinder to create a thread; see the Thread for Screw Tutorial for details.
u: In the Select Attachment dialog, select a sketch to be used as first cross-section and click OK.
In the Pipe Parameters under Profile, press the Object button.
Select the sketch to be used as path in the 3D View:

To use more than one cross-section, under Section Transformation set the Transform mode to Multisection; press Add Section then select a sketch in the 3D View. Repeat for each additional cross-section.
Set options if needed and click OK.
PartDesign_SubtractivePipe.m: Part Design → Substractive Features → Subtractive Pipe

PartDesign_SubtractivePrism.d:
Inserts a subtractive prism in the active Body. Its shape is subtracted from the existing solid.

On the left: active body (A) shown in grey and subtractive prism (B) shown in transparent red; result on the right.
u: Set the Primitive Parameters and Attachment.
Click OK.
A Prism feature appears under the active Body.
PartDesign_SubtractivePrism.m: Part Design → Subtractive Primitive → Subtractive Prism

PartDesign_SubtractiveSphere.d:
Inserts a subtractive sphere in the active Body. Its shape is subtracted from the existing solid.

On the left: active body (A) shown in grey and subtractive sphere (B) shown in transparent red; result on the right.
u: The task panel opens.
Set the parameters. (v26.3): If the Show interactive draggers when editing features preference is selected (default), the radius can be adjusted with an interactive gizmo in the 3D View.
Optionally set the Attachment.
Click OK.
A Sphere feature appears under the active Body.
PartDesign_SubtractiveSphere.m: Part Design → Subtractive Primitive → Subtractive Sphere

PartDesign_SubtractiveTorus.d:
Inserts a subtractive torus in the active Body. Its shape is subtracted from the existing solid.

On the left: active body (A) shown in grey and subtractive torus (B) shown in transparent red; result on the right.
u: Set the Primitive Parameters and Attachment.
Click OK.
A Torus feature appears under the active Body.
PartDesign_SubtractiveTorus.m: Part Design → Subtractive Primitive → Subtractive Torus

PartDesign_SubtractiveWedge.d:
Inserts a subtractive wedge in the active Body. Its shape is subtracted from the existing solid.

On the left: active body (A) shown in grey and subtractive wedge (B) shown in transparent red; result on the right.
u: Set the Primitive Parameters and Attachment.
Click OK.
A Wedge feature appears under the active Body.
PartDesign_SubtractiveWedge.m: Part Design → Subtractive Primitive → Subtractive Wedge

PartDesign_Thickness.d: The PartDesign Thickness tool transforms a solid body into a hollow object with at least one open face, giving to each of its remaining faces a uniform thickness. It adds a Thickness object to the document with its corresponding representation in the Tree View.
u: Optionally activate the Body to apply the Thickness to.
Select one or more faces of the Body.

If there is no active Body, and there are two or more Bodies in the document, the Active Body Required dialog will open and prompt you to activate one. If there is a single Body it will be activated automatically.
The Thickness Parameters task panel opens. See Options for more information.

PartDesign_WizardShaft.d: This tool allows you to create a shaft from a table of values, and to analyse forces and moments.

Part_Boolean.d:
The Part Boolean command can perform four boolean operations. A task panel is used to specify the operation and the objects.

For quicker access to the boolean operations, use Part Cut, Part Fuse, Part Common and Part Section.
u: Optionally select one or two shapes.
The Boolean Operation task panel opens.
Selected shapes are already checked in the shape lists.
Select the appropriate Boolean Operation. Union, Difference, and intersection only accept solid shapes, Section also accepts non-solid shapes.
Optionally (un)check an item in the First shape list.
Optionally (un)check an item in the Second shape list.

Part_BooleanFragments.d:
The Part BooleanFragments command computes all fragments that can result from applying Boolean operations between input shapes. For example, for two intersecting spheres, three non-overlapping but touching solids are generated.

The output shape is always a compound. The content of the compound depends on input shape types and operation mode. That means, you don't immediately get access to individual pieces of the result - the pieces remain grouped together. The individual pieces can be extracted by exploding the compound (Draft Downgrade).
u: Select objects to be intersected. The order of selection is not important, since the action of the command is symmetric. It is enough to select one sub-shape of each object (e.g. faces). You can also select a compound…
A Boolean Fragments parametric object is created. Original objects are hidden, and the result of intersection is shown in the 3D View.

Part_Box.d: The Part Box command creates a parametric box solid, a rectangular cuboid. In the coordinate system defined by its DataPlacement property, the bottom face of the box lies on the XY-plane with its front left corner at the origin, and its front edge parallel to the X-axis.
u: A Box object is created.
Optionally change the dimensions and DataPlacement of the box by doing one of the following:

Part_BoxSelection.d: The Part BoxSelection command selects faces from a user defined rectangular area, a box, in the 3D View.
u: Drag a rectangle to select faces that are (partially) inside the rectangle, or touched by it.

Part_Builder.d: The Part Builder command creates more complex shapes from various geometric primitives.
u: The Create Shape task panel opens.
Select the shape creation mode and optionally press the Box Selection button to use box selection instead of picking geometrical entities one by one:
The object is created.
Optionally create additional objects.

Part_Chamfer.d: The Part Chamfer command chamfers the selected edge(s) of an object. A dialog allows you to choose which edges to work on as well as modify various chamfer parameters.
u: Optionally select one or more edges in the 3D View.
The Chamfer Edges task panel opens.
Press OK to close the task panel and apply the chamfer.

Part_CheckGeometry.d: The Part CheckGeometry command runs a verification and reports if geometry is a valid solid. The command checks if the Boundary representation (BRep or B-rep) of the model is valid.
u: Select a part (beware to select the whole part and not just a face to check for valid solid)
The Settings task panel opens, unless Skip this settings page is enabled. See Options for more information. Click Run Check.

Part_Circle.d:
A Part Circle is a parametric shape that can be created with the Part Primitives command. In the coordinate system defined by its DataPlacement property, the circle lies on the XY-plane with its center at the origin.

A Part Circle is in fact a closed counterclockwise circular arc, it can be turned into an arc by changing its DataAngle1 and/or DataAngle2 properties.
u: In the task panel of the Part Primitives command select the Circle option from the dropdown list.
Select three vertices in the 3D View. There is no need to hold down the Ctrl key.
A circle is created.
The selected vertices are only used at creation time to calculate the DataRadius and DataPlacement of the circle.

Part_ColorPerFace.d: The Part ColorPerFace command sets the display properties of selected faces. To change a whole object use Std SetAppearance instead.
u: Select a single object.
The Appearance per Face task panel opens.
Select one or more faces:
Do one of the following:
Optionally select one or more new faces whose properties you want to change.

Part_Common.d:
The Part Common command extracts the common part (intersection) between selected Part objects. This operation is fully parametric and the components can be modified and the result recomputed.

This command is an automated form of the Boolean Operation.
u: Select two shapes

Part_Compound.d: The Part Compound command creates a compound of objects with a topological shape such as solid objects and other objects with faces and/or edges. It cannot handle meshes as they do not have a topological shape.
u: Mark the topological shapes to be added to the compound in the Tree View.

Part_CompoundFilter.d:
The Part CompoundFilter command can be used to extract the individual pieces of the result of e.g. a Part Slice operation, with which you have split an object.

It can extract children by their indexes, test children for collisions with stencil shape, and filter children based on their properties, such as length, area, volume.

If there is only one child in the result, the output is the child. If there is more than one child to output, the output is a new compound.
u: Select the sliced object
Select the CompoundFilter Object in the Tree View.
In the properties tab set "Filter Type" to "specific items".
Set items to the elements you want to extract:
If you want to extract another piece select the sliced object again. It is now placed under the CompoundFilter in the Tree View.

Repeat the selection procedure from above. The slice and its subelements will be displayed under both CompoundFilters; they are, of course not repeated in the model. A very fast way to extract another piece is to copy the…

Part_Cone.d:
The Part Cone command creates a parametric cone solid. In the coordinate system defined by its DataPlacement property, the bottom face of the cone lies on the XY-plane with its center at the origin.

The default Part Cone is truncated. It can be turned into a full, untruncated, cone by changing its DataRadius1 or DataRadius2 property to zero. It can be turned into a segment of a cone by changing its DataAngle property.
u: The Cone object is created.
Optionally change the dimensions and DataPlacement of the cone by doing one of the following:

Part_CoordinateSystem.d:
The Part CoordinateSystem command creates a local coordinate system, an LCS object, that can be attached to other objects. A coordinate system is one of several datum objects. A datum object is typically used to attach multiple other objects to. If the position or orientation of a datum object changes, all objects attached to it will follow.

A datum object can also provide a geometric reference for a feature or operation. Depending on its type it may for example be used as a direction vector, a rotation axis or a mirror plane.
u: Optionally activate the correct container, for example a PartDesign Body, a Std Part or an Assembly. If multiple containers are active, the datum object is added to the active container that was created first.
Optionally select the geometry the datum object should be attached to.
The Attachment task panel opens.
If no geometry has been selected: optionally press the OK button to finish the command without attaching the datum object.
For further steps see Part EditAttachment. Continue from step 7 on that page if geometry has been preselected.

Part_CrossSections.d: The Part CrossSections command creates one or more cross-sections through the selected shape, parallel to one of the default global planes (XY, XZ or YZ).
u: Select a shape.
The Cross Sections task panel opens.
Press OK to close the task panel.
A Cross-Section object will be created, it inherits the name of the selected shape and adds the suffix _cs.

Part_Cut.d:
The Part Cut command cuts (subtracts) selected Part objects, the last one being subtracted from the first one. This operation is fully parametric and the components can be modified and the result recomputed.

This command is an automated form of the Boolean Operation.
u: Select two shapes.

Part_Cylinder.d:
The Part Cylinder command creates a parametric cylinder solid. It is the result of extruding a circular arc along a straight path. In the coordinate system defined by its DataPlacement property, the bottom face of the cylinder lies on the XY-plane with its center at the origin.

A Part Cylinder can be turned into a segment of a cylinder by changing its DataAngle property.
u: The Cylinder object is created.
Optionally change the dimensions and DataPlacement of the cylinder by doing one of the following:

Part_DatumLine.d:
The Part DatumLine command creates a datum line object that can be attached to other objects. A datum line is one of several datum objects. A datum object is typically used to attach multiple other objects to. If the position or orientation of a datum object changes, all objects attached to it will follow.

A datum object can also provide a geometric reference for a feature or operation. Depending on its type it may for example be used as a direction vector, a rotation axis or a mirror plane.

Part_DatumPlane.d:
The Part DatumPlane command creates a datum plane object that can be attached to other objects. A datum plane is one of several datum objects. A datum object is typically used to attach multiple other objects to. If the position or orientation of a datum object changes, all objects attached to it will follow.

A datum object can also provide a geometric reference for a feature or operation. Depending on its type it may for example be used as a direction vector, a rotation axis or a mirror plane.

Part_DatumPoint.d: The Part DatumPoint command creates a datum point object that can be attached to other objects. A datum point is one of several datum objects. A datum object is typically used to attach multiple other objects to. If the position or orientation of a datum object changes, all objects attached to it will follow.

Part_Defeaturing.d:
The Part Defeaturing command can remove selected form features, such as holes, protrusions, gaps, chamfers, fillets etc. from a model.

The defeaturing command can be very useful in different contexts:

  • To edit an imported solid where no history of operations is available.
  • Fixing defects in the model, e.g. filling gaps, holes etc.
  • Model simplification for numeric analysis, display on mobile devices, etc.

The removed form features are filled by the extension of the adjacent faces, thus no unexpected parts should appear in the result. Please note that the result is a new shape that is not linked to the original; thus, it is non-parametric.
u: Select the face(s) to be removed from the model.
A Defeatured object is created and the original object hidden.

Part_EditAttachment.d: The Part EditAttachment command attaches an object to one or more other objects. The attached object is linked to the referenced object(s), which means that if the placement or geometry of the referenced object(s) is changed, the placement of the attached object will update accordingly.
u: Select the object to be attached.
Do one of the following:
The Attachment task panel opens.
At the top of the task panel Not attached can be read. The first button labeled Selecting… is highlighted to indicate a selection in the 3D View is expected.
Select a vertex, edge or face/plane belonging to another object.

In the input field to the right of the button, the referenced object and subelement are shown. For example, if a face of a Part Box is selected, the field may show Box:Face6. The label of the button displays the subelement…

Part_ElementCopy.d: The Part ElementCopy command creates non-parametric copies of subelements: vertices, edges and faces.
u: Select one or more subelements belonging to one or more objects.

Part_Ellipse.d:
A Part Ellipse is a parametric shape that can be created with the Part Primitives command. In the coordinate system defined by its DataPlacement property, the ellipse lies on the XY-plane with its center at the origin. Its mayor axis is parallel to the X-axis.

A Part Ellipse is in fact a closed counterclockwise elliptical arc, it can be turned into an arc by changing its DataAngle1 and/or DataAngle2 properties.

Part_Ellipsoid.d:
A Part Ellipsoid is a parametric solid that can be created with the Part Primitives command. In the coordinate system defined by its DataPlacement property, the axes of the ellipsoid are aligned with the X, Y and Z axes, and therefore its center is positioned at the origin.

A Part Ellipsoid can be truncated at the top and/or bottom by changing its DataAngle1 and/or DataAngle2 properties. It can be turned into a segment of an ellipsoid by changing its DataAngle3 property.

Part_ExplodeCompound.d:
The Part ExplodeCompound command splits a compound of shapes, to make each contained shape (child) available as a separate object. The children are automatically put into a Group if there is more than one child.

It is semi-parametric: the shapes of the children will update as the source compound changes, but if the number of children in the compound is changed, the explosion will be either missing some shapes, or have redundant objects in an error state.
u: Select a single compound.

Part_Export.d: The Part Export command exports selected objects to a different file format. The supported file formats are: STEP (with or without colors), IGES (with or without colors), and BREP.
u: Set up the Import Export Preferences in the Preferences Editor.
Select one or more objects. See Std Export.
Select the correct file format in the dialog box.
Enter a filename.

Part_Extrude.d:
The Part Extrude command extends a shape by a specified distance, in a specified direction. The output shape type will vary depending on the input shape type and the options selected.

In most common scenarios, the following lists the expected output shape type from a given input shape type,

  • Extruding a Vertex (point) will produce a straight Edge (Line)
  • Extruding an open edge (e.g. line, arc) will produce an open face (e.g. plane)
  • Extruding a closed edge (e.g. circle) will optionally produce a closed face (e.g. an open-ended cylinder) or if the parameter "solid" is "true" will produce a solid (e.g. a closed solid cylinder)
  • Extruding an open Wire (e.g. a Draft Wire) will produce an open shell (several joined faces)
  • Extruding a closed Wire (e.g. a Draft Wire) will optionally produce a shell (several joined faces) or if the parameter "solid" is "true" will produce a solid
  • Extruding a face (e.g. plane) will produce a solid (e.g. Cuboid)
u: Optionally select one or more shapes in the 3D View or in the Tree View.
The Extrude task panel opens.
Press OK to close the task panel.
One Extrude object will be created for each selected shape.

Part_Fillet.d: The Part Fillet command creates fillets (rounds) on the selected edges of a shape. A dialog allows choosing which shape and which edges to work on.
u: Optionally select one or more edges in the 3D View.
The Fillet Edges task panel opens.
Press OK to close the task panel and apply the fillet.

Part_Fuse.d:
The Part Fuse command fuses (unites) selected Part objects into one. This operation is fully parametric and the components can be modified and the result recomputed.

This command is an automated form of the Boolean Operation.
u: Select two or more shapes

Part_Helix.d: A Part Helix is a parametric shape that can be created with the Part Primitives command. In the coordinate system defined by its DataPlacement property, the axis of the helix matches the Z-axis and its bottom point, the start point, lies on the X-axis.

Part_Import.d: The Part Import command imports geometry from a different file format into the active document. The supported file formats are: STEP (with or without colors), IGES (with or without colors), and BREP.
u: Set up the Import Export Preferences in the Preferences Editor.
Optionally select the correct file format in the dialog box.
Select a file.

Part_JoinConnect.d: The Part JoinConnect tool connects the interiors of two walled objects (e.g. pipes). It can also join shells and wires.
u: Select objects to be connected. The order of selection is not important, since the action of the tool is symmetric. It is enough to select one sub-shape of each object (e.g., faces). You can also select a compound containing…
A Connect parametric object is created. Original objects are hidden, and the result of connecting is shown in the 3D View.

Part_JoinCutout.d: The Part JoinCutout tool creates a cutout in a walled object (e.g. a pipe) to fit another walled object.
u: Select the base object first, then the object to define the cutout. The order of selection is important. It is enough to select one sub-shape of each object (e.g. faces).
A Part JoinFeature object is created, with Mode set to 'Cutout'. Original objects are hidden, and the result of cutting is shown in the 3D View.

Part_JoinEmbed.d: The Part JoinEmbed tool embeds a walled object (e.g. a pipe) into another walled object.
u: Select the base object first, then the object to be embedded. The order of selection is important. It is enough to select one sub-shape of each object (e.g. faces).
A Part JoinFeature object is created, with Mode set to 'Embed'. Original objects are hidden, and the result of embedding is shown in the 3D View.

Part_Line.d: A Part Line is a parametric line that can be created with the Part Primitives command. The coordinates of its start and end point are relative to the coordinate system defined by its DataPlacement property.

Part_LinkArrayCircular.d:
The Part LinkArrayCircular command creates a Link array from a selected object by placing copies along concentric circles.

The command can be used on many 3D objects such as those created with the Part Workbench, but also on assembly instances created with the Assembly Workbench.
u: Optionally select one object.
The Circular Link Array task panel opens. See Options for more information.
If you have not yet selected an object, press the Select Object button and select one object.
Enter the required parameters in the task panel.
Part_LinkArrayCircular.m: Part/Assembly → Link Arrays → Circular Link Array
