Part_LinkArrayLinear.d:
The Part LinkArrayLinear command creates a Link array from a selected object by placing copies in a linear pattern along one or two selected directions.

The command can be used on many 3D objects such as those created with the Part Workbench, but also on assembly instances created with the Assembly Workbench.
u: Optionally select one object.
The Linear Link Array task panel opens. See Options for more information.
If you have not yet selected an object, press the Select Object button and select one object.
Enter the required parameters in the task panel.
Part_LinkArrayLinear.m: Part/Assembly → Link Arrays → Linear Link Array

Part_LinkArrayPath.d:
The Part LinkArrayPath command creates a Link array from a selected object by placing copies along a path.

The command can be used on many 3D objects such as those created with the Part Workbench, but also on assembly instances created with the Assembly Workbench.
u: Optionally select one object.
The Path Link Array task panel opens. See Options for more information.
If you have not yet selected an object, press the Select Object button and select one object.
Enter the required parameters in the task panel.
Part_LinkArrayPath.m: Part/Assembly → Link Arrays → Path Link Array

Part_LinkArrayPoint.d:
The Part LinkArrayPoint command creates a Link array from a selected object by placing copies at the points of a selected shape.

The command can be used on many 3D objects such as those created with the Part Workbench, but also on assembly instances created with the Assembly Workbench.
u: Optionally select one object.
The Point Link Array task panel opens. See Options for more information.
If you have not yet selected an object, press the Select Object button and select one object.
Enter the required parameters in the task panel.
Part_LinkArrayPoint.m: Part/Assembly → Link Arrays → Point Link Array

Part_LinkArrayPolar.d:
The Part LinkArrayPolar command creates a Link array from a selected object by placing copies in a polar pattern about the selected axis.

The command can be used on many 3D objects such as those created with the Part Workbench, but also on assembly instances created with the Assembly Workbench.
u: Optionally select one object.
The Polar Link Array task panel opens. See Options for more information.
If you have not yet selected an object, press the Select Object button and select one object.
Enter the required parameters in the task panel.
Part_LinkArrayPolar.m: Part/Assembly → Link Arrays → Polar Link Array

Part_Loft.d: The Part Loft command creates a face, a shell, or a solid shape from two or more profiles (cross-sections).
u: The Loft task panel opens.
Press OK to close the task panel.
A Loft object will be created.

Part_MakeFace.d: The Part MakeFace command creates a planar face from one or more coplanar closed wires (contours). They can be any valid wire, i.e. created with the Part Workbench, the Draft Workbench or the Sketcher Workbench. The contours should not self-intersect, or intersect each other. They can be nested to create voids.
u: Select one or more objects containing one or more closed wires.
A Face object will be created.

Part_MakeSolid.d:
The Part MakeSolid command creates solids from shape objects.

This command is typically used as one of the steps to create a solid from a mesh. See Part ShapeFromMesh for more information.
u: Select one or more shape objects.
For each selected object a solid is created as a separate new object.

Part_Measure_Angular.d:
This command measures the angle between two straight edges, two planar faces or one straight edge and a planar face and displays the measurement in the 3D view.

The appearance of the measurements can be changed in the preferences.
u: Select two straight edges, two planar faces or one straight edge

Alternatively the command can be launched without prior selection. A selection dialog then opens in the Task panel. A Control widget also provides buttons to reset the selection, toggle the measurement display in the 3D view,…
Measurements are automatically discarded when closing the document.

Part_Measure_Clear_All.d: This command clears all measurements from the 3D view.

Part_Measure_Linear.d:
This command measures the distance between two selected topological elements (vertex, edge, face) and displays measurements in the 3D view. The shortest distance between the two elements and the delta measurements (distances parallel to the global X, Y, Z axes) are shown.

The appearance of the measurements can be changed in the preferences.
u: Select any combination of two elements: vertices, edges, faces

Alternatively the command can be launched without prior selection. A selection dialog then opens in the Task panel. A Control widget also provides buttons to reset the selection, toggle the measurement display in the 3D view,…
Measurements are automatically discarded when closing the document.

Part_Measure_Refresh.d: Part Measure Refresh updates the 3D view to display all measurements created with Measure Linear and Measure Angular.

Part_Measure_Toggle_3D.d: This command toggles the visibility of linear and angular measurements in the 3D view.

Part_Measure_Toggle_3d.d: This command toggles the visibility of linear and angular measurements in the 3D view.

Part_Measure_Toggle_All.d: This command toggles the visibility of all measurements in the 3D view.

Part_Measure_Toggle_Delta.d: This command toggles the visibility of delta measurements in the 3D view.

Part_Mirror.d:
The Part Mirror command creates a new object (image) which is a reflection of the original object (source). The image object is created behind a mirror plane. The mirror plane may be standard plane (XY, YZ, or XZ), any plane parallel to a standard plane, or ((v1.0)) any arbitrary plane by using a reference object.

An example:
u: Optionally select one or more source objects.
The Mirror tasks panel opens.
Click OK to close the task panel.
One Part__Mirroring object will be created for each source object.

Part_Offset.d: The Part Offset command creates parallel copies of a selected shape at a certain distance from the base shape, giving a new object.
u: Select an object to offset.
An Offset object is created and the Offset task panel opens.
Press OK to close the task panel.

Part_Offset2D.d:
The Part Offset2D command constructs a wire, parallel to the original wire, at a certain distance from it. Or enlarges/shrinks a planar face, similarly.

The wire/face must be planar. There can be multiple wires in one object, not necessarily coplanar.
u: Select an object to offset.
An Offset2D object is created and the Offset task panel opens.
Press OK to close the task panel.

Part_Plane.d: A Part Plane is a parametric rectangular plane that can be created with the Part Primitives command. In the coordinate system defined by its DataPlacement property, the plane lies on the XY-plane with its front left corner at the origin, and its front edge parallel to the X-axis.

Part_Point.d: A Part Point is a parametric point that can be created with the Part Primitives command. Its coordinates are relative to the coordinate system defined by its DataPlacement property.

Part_PointsFromMesh.d:
The Part PointsFromMesh command creates points objects from geometric objects.

The resulting shapes are compounds of vertices, which can be used as reference to further create lines, sketches and faces with other commands, like those from the Sketcher or the Draft workbenches.
u: Select one or more objects.
The Distance in Parameter Space dialog opens.
Enter a distance value.

Part_Primitives.d: The Part Primitives command opens a dialog to create one or more parametric primitives. 16 primitive types are available.
u: The Geometric Primitives task panel opens.
Select a primitive type from the dropdown list.
Specify the properties.
The primitive object is created.
Note that the task panel stays open.
Optionally create additional primitives.

Part_Prism.d: A Part Prism is a parametric solid that can be created with the Part Primitives command. It is the result of extruding a regular polygon along a straight path. In the coordinate system defined by its DataPlacement property, the bottom face of the prism lies on the XY-plane with its center at the origin and one of its vertices on the X-axis.

Part_ProjectionOnSurface.d: The Part ProjectionOnSurface command projects a shape onto a face from another object. It can for example be used to project logos or text objects.
u: Make sure you have at least two objects in your document; the "source" object that you wish to project, and the "target" object where the projection will be made.
The Projection on Surface task panel opens.
Click on Select Projection Surface, and then click on the "target" surface where the projection will be created.
Then click on the specific button to choose the type of subelement that you want to add to your projection object.
Then click on the specific radio button to choose the type of projection shape to create.
Press the OK to complete the operation and produce the new projection object.

Part_RefineShape.d: The Part RefineShape command creates parametric copies with a refined shape from selected objects. It removes unnecessary edges from planar and cylindrical faces.
u: Select one or more objects.
For each object a cleaned, parametric copy is created
The original objects are hidden.

Part_RegularPolygon.d: A Part RegularPolygon is a parametric shape that can be created with the Part Primitives command. In the coordinate system defined by its DataPlacement property, the polygon lies on the XY-plane with its center at the origin and one of its vertices on the X-axis.

Part_ReverseShape.d: The Part ReverseShape command creates parametric copies with reversed face normals from selected objects.
u: Select one or more objects.
For each selected object a reversed shape is created.

Part_Revolve.d:
The Part Revolve command revolves the selected object around a given axis. The following shape types are allowed, and lead to the listed output shapes:

A Sketch can be used as well. Solids or compound solids are not allowed as input shapes. Normal compounds are currently not allowed either.
u: Optionally select one or more shapes in the 3D View or in the Tree View.
The Revolve task panel opens.
Press OK to close the task panel.
One Revolve object will be created for each selected shape.

Part_RuledSurface.d: The Part RuledSurface command creates a ruled surface spanning between two selected edges/wires.
u: Select two edges or wires (open or closed contours).
A Ruled_Surface object is created between the selected edges/wires.

Part_Scale.d:
The Part Scale command scales shapes by a specified factor in all directions or by distinct factors in each cardinal direction. In the case of distinct factors, the shapes may be distorted.

Scaling occurs relative to the global coordinate system. To scale relative to the placement of the source object create a Link or a Draft Clone instead.
u: Optionally select one or more shapes in the 3D View or in the Tree View.
The Scale tasks panel opens.
Click OK to close the task panel and finish the command.
One Scale object will be created for each selected shape.

Part_Section.d:
The Part Section command creates wire geometry at the intersections of two objects. The result is fully parametric.

  • An intersection of two solids/faces results in one or more section lines.
  • An intersection of two lines, or a line and a solid/face, results in one or more points.

This command is an automated form of the Boolean Operation.
u: Select two objects. The first object will be the DataBase of the Section, but the selection order has no impact on the result.
A Section object will be created.

Part_SectionCut.d: The Part SectionCut command only works for Part and PartDesign objects and assemblies of those. It creates a persistent cut of objects and assemblies. Since the cut result is a normal Part Cut object, it can be modified further or for example 3D-printed. See below for possible applications.
Part_SectionCut.m: 1.0 and below : View → Persistent section cut 1.1 and above : Part → Persistent Section Cut

Part_SelectFilter.d: The Part SelectFilter command can be used to restrict selection in the 3D View to vertices, edges or faces, or to remove that restriction.
u: This option only allows the selection of vertices.
Part_SelectFilter.k: X S / E S / F S / C S

Part_SimpleCopy.d: The Part SimpleCopy command creates non-parametric copies of objects.
u: Select one or more objects.

Part_Slice.d:
The Part Slice command splits shapes by intersection with other shapes. For example, for a box and a plane, a compound of two solids is created.

There are two commands to slice a shape: Slice Apart and Slice to Compound. They both create a 'Slice' parametric feature, that puts the sliced pieces into a compound. However, Slice Apart explodes the resulting compound into separate objects. "Slice to Compound" is fully-parametric, and causes no trouble as the number of pieces changes. "Slice Apart" will not update the number of objects as the number of pieces changes.
u: Select the object to be sliced, first, and then some objects to slice with.The order of selection is important. Compounds with self-intersections are not allowed (self-intersections sometimes can be accounted for by passing…
A parametric Slice object is created. Original objects are hidden, and the result of intersection is shown in 3D View.

Part_SliceApart.d:
The Part SliceApart command splits shapes by intersection with other shapes. For example, for a box and a plane, two solids are created.

Slice apart is the same as Part Slice followed by Part Explode Compound. While "Slice to compound" is fully-parametric, and causes no trouble as the number of pieces changes, "Slice apart" will not update the number of objects as the number of pieces changes. They both create Slice parametric feature, that puts the sliced pieces into a compound, but "Slice apart" explodes the resulting compound into separate objects.
u: Select the object to be sliced apart, first, and then some objects to slice with. The order of selection is important.

Part_Sphere.d:
The Part Sphere command creates a parametric sphere solid. It is the result of revolving a circular arc profile around an axis. In the coordinate system defined by its DataPlacement property, the center of the sphere is positioned at the origin, and its axis of revolution is the Z-axis.

A Part Sphere can be truncated at the top and/or bottom by changing its DataAngle1 and/or DataAngle2 properties. It can be turned into a segment of a sphere by changing its DataAngle3 property.
u: The Sphere object is created.
Optionally change the dimensions and DataPlacement of the sphere by doing one of the following:

Part_Spiral.d: A Part Spiral is a parametric shape that can be created with the Part Primitives command. In the coordinate system defined by its DataPlacement property, the spiral lies on the XY-plane with its center at the origin and its start point on the X-axis. It widens as it turns counterclockwise.

Part_Sweep.d:
The Part Sweep command creates a face, a shell, or a solid shape from one or more profiles (cross-sections) distributed along a spine.

The Part Sweep command is similar to Part Loft with the addition of a spine.
u: The Sweep task panel opens.
Click OK to close the task panel.
A Sweep object is created.

Part_Thickness.d: The Part Thickness command works on a solid shape and transforms it into a hollow object, giving to each of its faces a defined and constant thickness. On some solids it allows you to significantly speed up the work, and avoids making extrusions and pockets.
u: Select one or more faces of an existing solid.
A Thickness object is created and the Thickness task panel opens.
Press OK to close the task panel.

Part_ToleranceSet.d:
The Part ToleranceSet command creates a parametric copy of selected objects with all contained tolerances set to at least a certain minimum value. The created object behaves like a compound if multiple objects are selected/added to the feature, or as a single shape if only one object is selected.

Tolerances affect subsequent OCCT functions such as boolean operations. Tolerances of sub-shapes can be inspected with the help of Subshapebinders and the Check Geometry command.
u: Select one or more objects.
A Tolerance object is created and the original object hidden.

Part_Torus.d:
The Part Torus command creates a parametric torus solid, a doughnut shape. It is the result of sweeping a circular profile around a circular path. In the coordinate system defined by its DataPlacement property, the circular path of the torus lies on the XY-plane with its center at the origin.

A Part Torus can be turned into a segment of a torus by changing its DataAngle3 property. By changing its DataAngle1 and/or DataAngle2 properties the swept profile can become a segment of a circle.
u: The Torus object is created.
Optionally change the dimensions and DataPlacement of the torus by doing one of the following:

Part_TransformedCopy.d:
The Part TransformedCopy command creates non-parametric copies of objects. It is intended for objects nested in containers.

The DataPlacement of the copies is adjusted, accounting for the placement of the container(s), so that their position and rotation relative to the global coordinate system is the same as that of the original objects. If the selected objects are not nested, or nested in a container with a default placement, this command produces the same results as Part SimpleCopy.
u: Select one or more objects.

Part_Tube.d: The Part Tube command creates a parametric tube solid. In the coordinate system defined by its DataPlacement property, the bottom face of the tube lies on the XY-plane with its center at the origin.
u: The Tube object is created
The Tube task panel opens.
Specify the dimensions.
The tube is dynamically updated in the 3D View.
Optionally change the DataPlacement property of the tube in the Property View, or with the Std TransformManip command.

Part_Wedge.d: A Part Wedge is a parametric solid that can be created with the Part Primitives command. It has four to six planar faces. It is defined by virtual front and rear main planes on which a rectangular face (the default), a single straight edge or a single vertex is created. These base shapes define the four quadrilateral or triangular faces that connect them. The resulting solid is only a true wedge if one of the base shapes is a rectangular face and the other a straight edge. In the coordinate system defined by its DataPlacement property, the virtual front and rear main planes of the wedge are plane-parallel to XZ-plane, and the edges of the base shapes are parallel to the X or Z-axis. All its coordinates are relative to that coordinate system.

Part_XOR.d: The Part XOR command removes geometry shared by an even number of objects and leaves a void space between the involved objects. For two objects it represents a symmetric version of Part Cut.
u: Select two or more objects. It is also possible to select a Part Compound containing two or more objects.

Plot_Axes.d: The standard plot module already provides a basic tool to control the plot axes. But that tool is clearly insufficient when multi-axes plots have to be handled, as is the case in the Multi-axes plot tutorial. To overcome that limitation you can install the Plot Workbench using the Add-on manager, so a more complete tool to edit the plot axes will be available.

Plot_Grid.d: This tool allows the user to enable/disable the grid lines on a specific plot.

Plot_Labels.d: This tool allows the user to edit the title and axes labels, as well as their font sizes.

Plot_Legend.d: This tool allows the user to enable/disable the data series legend on a specific plot.

Plot_Positions.d: This tool allows the user to edit the position of some items like titles, axes labels and legend.

Plot_Save.d: The standard plot module already provides a minimum tool to save plots. If you install the Plot Workbench using the Add-on manager, a more complete tool to save the active plot will be available. With this tool you can also select the size and resolution of the output image.

Plot_Series.d: The standard plot module already provides a tool to edit the plot series style. But if you install the Plot Workbench using the Add-on manager, a more complete and straigthforward tool will be available.

Points_Convert.d:
The Points Convert command creates point clouds from shape objects or mesh objects.

Here a shape object refers any object with a DataShape property. Objects created with the Part and PartDesign workbench are shape objects. But so are objects created with the Sketcher and Draft workbench.
u: Select one or more objects.
The Distance dialog box opens.
Enter the maximum distance. The value must be in the 0.01 - 10.00 range.

Points_Export.d: The Points Export command exports a point cloud to a file.
u: Select a single point cloud. It is possible to select more point clouds but the command will create a separate file for each.
Enter a filename. If you do not specify a file extension the.asc extension will be used.

Points_Import.d: The Points Import command imports a point cloud from a file.
u: Select a point cloud file.

Points_Merge.d: The Points Merge command creates a point cloud by combining the points of two or more point clouds.
u: Select two or more point clouds.

Points_PolyCut.d: The Points PolyCut command cuts points from point clouds.
u: During the command the 3D View cannot be changed. It is advisable to properly align the 3D View first.
Select one or more point clouds.
Define a polygon in the 3D View.
Select an option from the 3D View context menu:

Points_Structure.d:
The Points Structure command creates a structured point cloud from the points of an existing scattered point cloud. A structured point cloud has the advantage that tessellation is much easier.

The command only works for point clouds whose points, when viewed from a certain direction, are organized in a regular 2D grid. These point clouds are typically produced by structured-light 3D scanners and do not have undercuts. For complex objects, point clouds from many different view directions have to be combined.
u: The command assumes that the view direction of the point cloud is parallel to the Z axis of the global coordinate system. If this is not the case: adjust the point cloud object's DataPlacement accordingly.
Select the point cloud object.

Raytracing_ExportProject.d: Exports the selected raytracing project to a file.
u: Select raytracing project in the tree view.
Click on or choose Raytracing → Export project... from the top menu.

Raytracing_InsertPart.d: Insert a view of a Part in a raytracing project.

Click on or choose Raytracing → Insert Part from the top menu.
View of selected part will be inserted in the raytracing project.

Raytracing_New.d: Insert new PovRay project in the document.

Or choose Raytracing → New Pov-Ray project and one of the pre-defined templates from the top menu.
A new POVRay project will be created named "PovProject"

Raytracing_Render.d: Renders the selected raytracing project using an external renderer.
u: Select raytracing project in the tree view.
Click on or choose Raytracing → Render from the top menu.

Raytracing_ResetCamera.d: Sets the camera of the selected raytracing project to match the current view.

Make sure that the view is set to perspective view
Click on or choose Raytracing → Reset Camera from the top menu
Selecting a raytracing project in the tree view and looking at the data-tab in the property view will show the current camera-properties

Raytracing_WriteCamera.d: Exports the current camera properties to a pov-file for use in a POV-Ray project.

Raytracing_WritePart.d: Exports the selected part to a pov-file for use in a POV-Ray project.

Choose Raytracing → Utilities →Export part to POV-Ray from the top menu.

Choose Raytracing → Utilities →Export view to POV-Ray... from the top menu.
Raytracing_WriteView.m: Raytracing → Utilities → Export view to POV-Ray...

Robot_SetDefaultValues.d: The Robot SetDefaultValues command sets the default values for speed, acceleration, and continuity for subsequent waypoint creation.

u: Select a robot and a trajectory in the Tree View.
The task panel opens.
In the Trajectory section the following buttons are available (from left to right):

Robot_TrajectoryCompound.d: The Robot TrajectoryCompound command groups and connects multiple trajectories into one.
u: An empty TrajectoryCompound object is created.
A task panel opens.
Switch to the Tree View.
Select trajectories, Edge2Trac trajectories and/or DressUp objects in the Tree View.

Robot_TrajectoryDressUp.d: The Robot TrajectoryDressUp command creates a dress-up object that overrides aspects of a trajectory.
u: Select a trajectory or a Edge2Trac-trajectory in the Tree View.
The Dress Up Parameter task panel opens.
Optionally change one or more of the following values:

Rocket_BodyTube.d:
Body tubes are the basic building block of all rockets. It typically contain the motor and payload, and server as an attachment point for the fins and nose cone.

The body tube tool can be used to create many components other than body tubes, for example: motor mounts, engine blocks, and launch lugs. Centering rings can be thought of as short body tubes with very thick walls, although the workbench has a tool specifically for them.
u: Set options and press OK.

Rocket_Bulkhead.d: A bulkhead is a solid section of material used to close off a section of body tube, or to provide a base for a nose cone.
u: Set options and press OK.

Rocket_CenteringRing.d: A Centering Ring is a solid object used to hold one or more body tubes inside another body tube.
u: Set options and press OK.

Rocket_CompLaunchGuide.d: Creates a launch guide used to ensure a straight flight before the rocket becomes aerodynamically stable.

Rocket_Ejection_Charge_Calculator.d:
Ejection occurs when the chamber containing the recovery system is pressurized with sufficient force to eject the recovery system from the chamber. The force required can vary according to a number of factors:

As such, this calculator will only give you a starting estimate. Too little powder will result in a failed ejection and a failed recovery. Too much powder may result in damage to the rocket or recovery system, which may also result in a failed recovery. It is ALWAYS necessary to do a ground test before flying your rocket.
u: Enter the weight of your rocket and parameters for your parachute.

Rocket_Fin.d: Fins are used to aerodynamically control the direction of flight.
u: Set options and press OK.

Rocket_FinCan.d: Fins are used to aerodynamically control the direction of flight. A fin can is a complete assembly including fins and body tube, often fitted over the outside of the main rocket body tube. Optionally, a fin can may include a launch lug.
u: Set options and press OK.

Rocket_LaunchLug.d: A launch lug is a small tube attached to the side of the rocket that allows the rocket to be guided using a rod until it is fast enough to be aerodynamically stable.
u: Set options and press OK.

Rocket_NoseCone.d: Nose cones come in a variety of shapes and sizes, most of which are difficult to model without programming. For many rocket builders, this makes the process unworkable. This command allows for nose cone creation using simple properties combined with a specialized task dialog.
u: Set options and press OK.

Rocket_Parachute_Size_Calculator.d:
This calculator determines the parachute size required to achieve the desired descent rate based on the parachute parameters.

The desired descent rate depends on your needs. As a rule of thumb, the main parachute should slow the rocket to approximately 6.1m/s(20f/s) while the drone should allow the parachute to descend much faster 18.3m/s(60f/s) - 21.3m/s(70f/s). The editor has presets for these, with the value for the drogue being in the middle of the range. You can set a custom descent rate to suit your needs.
u: Enter the weight of your rocket and parameters for your parachute.

Rocket_RailButton.d: A rail button is a small button attached to the side of the rocket that allows the rocket to be guided using a rail until it is fast enough to be aerodynamically stable.
u: Set options and press OK.

Rocket_RailGuide.d: A rail guide is a component attached to the side of the rocket that allows the rocket to be guided using a rail until it is fast enough to be aerodynamically stable.
u: Set options and press OK.

Rocket_Thrust_To_Weight_Calculator.d: This simple calculator determines the minimum average thrust required to maintain a 5:1 thrust to weight ratio.
u: Enter the weight of your rocket.
Rocket_Thrust_To_Weight_Calculator.m: Rocket → Calculators → Thrust To Weight Calculator

Rocket_Transition.d:
Transitions are like nose cones in many ways. While typically conical, they can have the same shapes as nose cones, but are far more versatile.

The most common application is to change from one body diameter to another, such as between stages, or at the base of a payload fairing. It can also be used for a boat tail, where the diameter of the rocket decreases towards the exhaust nozzle.
u: Set options and press OK.

Rocket_Vent_Hole_Size_Calculator.d:
This calculator determines the minimum size of vent holes for barometric altimeters based on the volume of the space and the number of vent holes.

Calculation comes from the rule of thumb of 1/4" vent hole for every 100 cubic inches of volume. A single vent hole of the appropriate size is susceptible to noise caused by breezes and wind gusts. These effects are minimized by using multiple vent holes distributed around the volume, with 3 holes being considered a practical minimum. The combined area of all vent holes will be equivalent to that of a single larger hole.
u: Enter the parameters of your electronics bay.
Rocket_Vent_Hole_Size_Calculator.m: Rocket → Calculators → Vent Hole Size Calculator

SheetMetal_AddBase.d:
The SheetMetal AddBase command creates a SheetMetal base object from a sketch.

From an open contour it creates a prismatic profile:

From a closed outline it creates a base plate (blank):
u: Select an open contour sketch.
A BaseBend object is created, corners along the contour are automatically converted into cylindrical bends, and the Sketched base shape properties Task Panel opens:
Optionally adjust the profile parameters in the Property View.

SheetMetal_AddBend.d:
The SheetMetal AddBend command replaces sharp edges between between two sections (base plate/walls/flanges) of a sheet metal object with rounded bends. Without these bends the object will not be unfoldable.

This command is the third of three steps to convert a shell object made with the Part Workbench or PartDesign Workbench into an unfoldable sheet metal object:

  • SheetMetal AddRelief
  • SheetMetal AddJunction
  • SheetMetal AddBend
u: Select one or more edges.
The Bend sharp corner properties Task Panel opens (v0.5.00).
Optionally press the Select button to add more faces.
Optionally adjust the parameters in the Task Panel.
A SolidBend object will be created consisting of one new bend at each selected edge.
Optionally adjust the parameters in the Property View.

SheetMetal_AddCornerRelief.d:
The SheetMetal AddCornerRelief command adds a corner relief. A relief is usually created at corners where two bends meet, but the command can also create a relief at an open corner.

The command can only create one relief at a time.
u: Select two edges of a corner.
A CornerRelief object is created and the Corner relief properties Task Panel opens ((v0.5.00)). A new corner relief is added at the selected corner.
Optionally press the Select button to reselect the edges.
Optionally re-select one of the Relief Type radio buttons:
Optionally toggle the Relief Size radio buttons:
Optionally adjust the K-Factor.

SheetMetal_AddCutout.d:
The SheetMetal AddCutout command creates an extruded cutout from a sketch extrusion.

The difference between a 'normal' cutout and an extruded cutout is that in the latter case the edges are made perpendicular to the selected face of the sheet metal object. The effect of the command is only visible if the sketch is not plane-parallel to the face.
u: Select a planar face and a sketch with a closed contour (in any order).
The Extruded Cutout properties Task Panel opens.
Optionally press the Face button to reselect the planar face.
Optionally press the Sketch button to reselect a sketch.
Optionally adjust the parameters in the Task Panel.
An ExtrudedCutout object will be created consisting of one or more holes in a line through the object.

SheetMetal_AddFoldWall.d:
The SheetMetal AddFoldWall command folds a sheet metal plate (blank) at a chosen line.

It can be used with a pre-cut blank to

  • create a perforated bend zone
  • leave planar sections within the bend area and beyond e.g. tabs. (needs gaps in the bend line)
u: Select the face to be bent.
Press Ctrl and select the sketch containing the bend line (segments) (preferably in the Tree View) to add it to the selection.
A Fold object is created and the Fold on sketch line properties Task Panel opens:
Optionally adjust the parameters in the Property View.

SheetMetal_AddHem.d:
The SheetMetal AddHem command creates hems on selected edges. By changing the Dataangle property a flange it can be turned into a hem.

A hem usually consists of a cylindrical bend of roughly 180° and a planar strip (wall).
u: Select one or more edges of a solid shape.
A Hem object is created that consists of one new hem at each selected edge, and the Hem properties Task Panel opens:
Optionally adjust the parameters in the Property View.

SheetMetal_AddJunction.d:
The SheetMetal AddJunction command creates open junctions between two sections (walls/flanges) of a sheet metal object. Without these junctions sheet metal sections connected to the same base will not be unfoldable.

This command is the second of three steps to convert a shell object made with the Part Workbench or PartDesign Workbench into an unfoldable sheet metal object:

  • SheetMetal AddRelief
  • SheetMetal AddJunction
  • SheetMetal AddBend
u: Select one or more edges.
The Junction properties Task Panel opens (v0.5.00).
Optionally press the Select button to add more faces.
Optionally adjust the parameters in the Task Panel.
A Junction object will be created consisting of one opening at each selected edge.
Optionally adjust the parameters in the Property View.

SheetMetal_AddRelief.d:
The SheetMetal AddRelief command creates corner reliefs, cutouts, at the points where three sections (base plate/walls/flanges) of a sheet metal object meet. Without these reliefs the object will not be unfoldable.

This command is the first of three steps to convert a shell object made with the Part Workbench or PartDesign Workbench into an unfoldable sheet metal object:

  • SheetMetal AddRelief
  • SheetMetal AddJunction
  • SheetMetal AddBend
u: Select one or more corner vertex(es).
The Corner relief on solid parameters Task Panel opens (v0.5.00).
Optionally press the Select button to add more vertices.
Optionally adjust the parameters in the Task Panel.
A CornerRelief object will be created consisting of one new corner relief at each selected vertex.
Optionally adjust the parameters in the Property View.

SheetMetal_AddWall.d:
The SheetMetal AddWall command creates flanges on selected edges. By changing the Dataangle property a flange it can be turned into a hem.

A flange usually consists of a 90° cylindrical bend and a planar strip (wall).

It is called a hem instead if the bend is roughly 180°.
u: Select one or more edges of a solid shape.
A Bend object is created that consists of one new flange at each selected edge, and the Flange properties Task Panel opens:
Optionally adjust the parameters in the Property View.

SheetMetal_BaseShape.d:
The SheetMetal BaseShape command creates a SheetMetal BaseShape object from parameters.

A rectangular sixth shape, called Flat, was introduced in v 0.4.10.
u: The Sheet metal base shape properties Task Panel opens.
Select the desired shape from the Base shape type options.
Select the position of the origin in the Location of part origin widget.
Optionally adjust the parameters in the Task Panel.
A BaseShape object will be created.
Optionally adjust the parameters in the Property View.

SheetMetal_ExtendBySketch.d:
The SheetMetal ExtendBySketch command extends a sheet metal plate at a selected edge face.

In connection with an outline sketch it can create interlocking geometry to close a profile:
u: Select one or more edge faces to be extended.
Press Ctrl and select the sketch in the Tree View or the 3D View to add it to the selection.
An Extend object will be created and the Extend properties Task Panel opens.

SheetMetal_Extrude.d:
The SheetMetal Extrude command extends a sheet metal plate at a selected edge face.

It creates a simple extension along the face normal of the selected edge face:

If an outline sketch is added it creates interlocking geometry to close a profile:
u: Select one or more edge faces to be extended.
An Extend object will be created with a new face extension extruded from each selected face and the Extend properties Task Panel ((v0.5.00)) opens:
Optionally adjust the parameters in the Property View.

SheetMetal_Forming.d:
The SheetMetal Forming command creates an embossed shape in a SheetMetal wall using a separate solid object.

The back side face of the solid defining the shape, and the face to be embossed are used to position and orient the solid, i.e. their local coordinate systems will have the same origin and the same orientation by default. The angle around the Z-axis and offsets in the X, Y, and Z direction can be altered by changing their values in the Property View.
u: Select the face of the SheetMetal object to be embossed.
Hold down the Ctrl key (or the Command key on macOS).
Add the bottom face (back side) of the solid defining the shape to the selection.
Release the Ctrl key (or the Command key).
The Forming tool parameters Task Panel opens (v0.5.00).
Optionally select new faces/edges.

Ship_AreasCurve.d:
Plot the transversal areas curve

The transversal areas curve offers really valuable information in the first stages of a ship's design, as it gives an idea of the shape and volume distribution of the ship.

Special attention should be paid to the eventual shoulders of the curve, which would indicate a large ship resistance (less efficiency in other words).

Ship_CreateShip.d:
Create a New Ship or new Ship Instance.

Ship works over Ship entities, that must be created on top of provided geometry. Geometry must be a solid, or set of solids.The following criteria must be taken into account:

  • All hull geometry must be provided (including symmetric bodies).
  • Starboard geometry must be included at negatives y domain.
  • Origin (0,0,0) point is the Midship section (Midpoint between after and forward perpendicular) and base line intersection.
Ship_CreateShip.m: Ship design → Create a new ship

Ship_Hydrostatics.d:
Plot the ship hydrostatics.

Hydrostatics computation is a critical stage of a ship's design, it provides an understanding to the underlying principal stability hull parameters.

It is indeed mandatory data in order to get the ship certified by classification societies. Combined with the information of load conditions provides the most basic information about ship stability.

The Ship workbench plot the hydrostatics in 3 main groups. In all of them the Δ(T) curve (displacement-draft ratio) is depicted. Although many other hydrostatics can be eventually considered, they can be actually derived from the already provided ones, which are documented below.

Ship_LoadCondition.m: Weights → Create a new loading condition

Ship_LoadExample.d:
This tool loads example geometries.

Ship works over Ship entities, that must be created on top of provided geometry. Geometry must be a solid, or set of solids. The following criteria must be taken into account:

  • All hull geometry must be provided (including symmetric bodies).
  • Starboard geometry must be included at negatives y domain.
  • Origin (0,0,0) point is the Midship section (Midpoint between after and forward perpendicular) and base line intersection.
u: A task panel will display, prompting to choose one of the example ship geometries.
Select the example you want to load and press Accept.
Result: The tool loads a new document with the selected geometry.
Ship_LoadExample.m: Ship design → Load an example ship geometry

Ship_ResistanceBlountFox.d:
Calculates ship resistance by the Blount and Fox method. This method was formulated by Donald L. Blount and David L. Fox in 1976 [1], with application to fast vessels in a pre-planing regime. It is based on a Savitsky [2] correction at low speeds.

Plots the resistance curve, the equilibrium trim, the power prediction and the resistance coefficients. It also exports the results to a spreadsheet.

The resistance is represented in kN, as a function of speed in knots. It includes the total resistance, the total resistance and the pressure resistance. The dialogue includes a checkbox to include both, Blount and Fox and Savitsky resistance curves in the graph, this allows the user to compare both methods resistance easier.
Ship_ResistanceBlountFox.m: Resistance → Resistance Blount and Fox prediction

Ship_ResistanceSavitsky.d:
Calculates ship resistance by the Savitsky method. This method was formulated by Daniel Savitsky in 1964 [1], with application to fast vessels in a planing regime.

Plots the resistance curve, the equilibrium trim, the power prediction and the resistance coefficients. It also exports the results to a spreadsheet.

The resistance is represented in kN, as a function of speed in knots. It includes the total resistance, the total resistance and the pressure resistance.

Ship_Tank.d:
The Ship Tank tool creates a new tank instance in a ship instance.

Tank instances are so far similar to Weight instances (see Ship Weight), i.e. they act as weights that shall be considered for the center of gravity and displacement computation. However, they have small differences in the inputs required to setup a tank instance, as well as in the way its contribution to the ship weight is computed. Along this line tanks can only be created on top of solid/volumetric geometries, and the density is not queried until they are added to a load condition (see Ship LoadCondition). Afterwards, their contribution to the ship weight and center of gravity will depend on the filling level (to be defined in the load condition) and the ship roll and trim angle, as long as the fluid inside reshapes, effectively affecting the gravity center position (the so-called free-surface effect).

Ship_Weight.d:
Add a weight to the ship instance.

Until this point, all the tools in Ship workbench are based on a Ship instance (see Ship CreateShip), which only holds information regarding the ship shape. Following the progressive data introduction system, at this point the user might define load conditions, which involves creating weights with this tool, creating tanks (see Ship Tank) and assembling them in load conditions (see Ship LoadCondition). With that information the center of gravity of the ship can be defined, enabling further computations.
Ship_Weight.m: Weights → Create a new ship weight

Sketcher_CarbonCopy.d:
The Sketcher CarbonCopy tool copies all geometry and constraints from another sketch into the active sketch.

Dimensional constraints which exist before the copy operation remain linked to the original sketch's dimensional constraints through expressions.
u: Make sure you are in the edit mode of an existing sketch. This sketch is the target of the operation.
The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.
Pick an edge from another sketch. This sketch is the source of the operation. See Notes.
Geometry elements as well as constraints are copied into the active sketch.
This tool always runs in continue mode: optionally copy additional sketches.
To finish, right-click or press Esc, or start another geometry or constraint creation tool.

Sketcher_Clone.d:
The Sketcher Clone command clones the selected sketch elements from one point to another, using the last selected point as reference. If any constraints are part of the source elements, then the new constraints are linked to the source constraints; if the constraints in the source are changed, the constraints in the clone are also changed. To avoid this linking see Sketcher Copy.

Note that a clone of a clone becomes a Sketcher Copy. If you wish to create linked constraints, clone the original source elements again.
u: Select the sketch elements to clone.
Move the mouse in the 3D view to the desired location for the clone.By keeping Shift pressed, the angle to the location point can be fixed in steps of 5°. (v0.20)
Left-click in the 3D view to create the clone.

Sketcher_CloseShape.d: This tool can be used to make a selected contour in sketcher closed by making an endpoint of a sketcher element coincident with the endpoint of the sketcher element selected next.

The Sketcher ConstrainBlock tool blocks edges in place with a single constraint. It is mainly intended for B-splines, which can be difficult to fully constrain otherwise.

The block constraint only affects the freely movable parts of an edge. Blocked edges can have other constraints, and applying additional constraints to a blocked edge can modify it.

The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.

A constraint is added.
Optionally keep creating constraints.
To finish, right-click or press Esc, or start another geometry or constraint creation tool.

The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.

Sketcher_ConstrainSnellsLaw.d: The Sketcher ConstrainSnellsLaw tool constrains two lines to follow the law of refraction of light as it penetrates through an interface where two materials with different refraction indices meet. See Snell's law.
u: Prepare two lines to represent a beam of light, and an edge to act as an interface. The lines should be on different sides of the interface. The interface can be a line, an arc, a circle or a conic.

Enter the Ratio n2/n1. Where n2 is for the medium where the second selected line resides, and n1 is for the first line's medium.
A refraction constraint is added. If required the endpoints are made coincident and constrained onto the interface. These additional constraints are called helper constraints.

Pick the start point of the arc (labelled 3 or 4 in the image above), this also defines its minor radius. Or with Dim-OVP: enter this radius and/or the start parameter of the arc. The parameter is relative to the axis of the…

Sketcher_CreateBSpline.d: The Sketcher CreateBSpline tool creates a B-spline curve from control points. (v1.0): Or optionally from knot points.
u: The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.

Optionally press the R key or check the Periodic checkbox to create a closed B-spline (also possible after points have been picked). (v1.0)
Pick several points.
Optionally press the F key before finishing to delete the last point. (v1.0)

Sketcher_CreateBSplineByInterpolation.d: The Sketcher CreateBSplineByInterpolation tool creates a B-spline curve from knot points. (v1.0): This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateBSpline but with a different initial mode.
u: For further steps see Sketcher CreateBSpline.

Sketcher_CreateChamfer.d: The Sketcher CreateChamfer tool creates a chamfer between two non-parallel edges. This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateFillet but with a different initial mode.
u: For further steps see Sketcher CreateFillet.

Sketcher_CreateCircle.d: The Sketcher CreateCircle tool creates a circle from its center and a point along the circle. (v1.0): Or optionally from three points along the circle.
u: The cursor changes to a cross with the current tool mode icon.
The Circle Parameters section ((v1.0)) is added at the top of the Sketcher Dialog.
Optionally press the M key or select from the dropdown list in the parameters section to change the tool mode:
The circle is created and applicable Pos-OVP and Dim-OVP based constraints are added.
If the tool runs in continue mode:

Sketcher_CreateEllipseBy3Points.d: The Sketcher CreateEllipseBy3Points tool creates an ellipse from the endpoints of one of its axes and a point along the ellipse. (v1.0): This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateEllipseByCenter but with a different initial mode.
u: For further steps see Sketcher CreateEllipseByCenter.

Sketcher_CreateEllipseByCenter.d: The Sketcher CreateEllipseByCenter tool creates an ellipse from its center, an endpoint of one of its axes, and a point along the ellipse. (v1.0): Or optionally from both endpoints of one of its axes and a point along the ellipse.
u: The cursor changes to a cross with the current tool mode icon.
The Ellipse Parameters section ((v1.0)) is added at the top of the Sketcher Dialog.
Optionally press the M key or select from the dropdown list in the parameters section to change the tool mode:
The ellipse is created, including a set of internal geometry (major axis, minor axis and two foci), and applicable Pos-OVP and Dim-OVP based constraints are added.
If the tool runs in continue mode:

Sketcher_CreateFillet.d:
The Sketcher CreateFillet tool creates a fillet between two non-parallel edges. (v1.0): The tool can also create a chamfer.

(v1.0): If two edges connected by a coincident constraint are filleted or chamfered, the corner point can optionally be preserved. The tool then adds a point object that has a point-on-object constraint with both edges. Constraints connected to the corner point are transferred to the new point object. 1.1 and below: The edges must be straight.
u: If there is a previous selection it is cleared. The tool does not accept a pre-selection.
The cursor changes to a cross with the current tool mode icon.
The Fillet/Chamfer Parameters section ((v1.0)) is added at the top of the Sketcher Dialog.
Optionally press the U key or uncheck the Preserve corner checkbox to disable that option. (v1.0)
Optionally press the M key or select from the dropdown list in the parameters section to change the tool mode:
Do one of the following:

Sketcher_CreateHeptagon.d: The Sketcher CreateHeptagon tool creates a heptagon. (v1.0): This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateRegularPolygon but with the number of sides preset to 7.
u: For further steps see Sketcher CreateRegularPolygon.

Sketcher_CreateHexagon.d: The Sketcher CreateHexagon tool creates a hexagon. (v1.0): This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateRegularPolygon but with the number of sides preset to 6.
u: For further steps see Sketcher CreateRegularPolygon.

Sketcher_CreateLine.d: The Sketcher CreateLine tool creates a line. (v1.0): If On-View-Parameters are enabled the tool has three modes.
u: The cursor changes to a cross with the current tool mode icon.
If On-View-Parameters are enabled the Line Parameters section ((v1.0)) is added at the top of the Sketcher Dialog.
Optionally press the M key or select from the dropdown list in the parameters section to change the tool mode:
The line is created and applicable Pos-OVP and Dim-OVP based constraints are added.
If the tool runs in continue mode:

Sketcher_CreateOblong.d: The Sketcher CreateOblong tool creates a rounded rectangle. (v1.0): This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateRectangle but with a different initial mode.
u: For further steps see Sketcher CreateRectangle.

Sketcher_CreateOctagon.d: The Sketcher CreateOctagon tool creates an octagon. (v1.0): This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateRegularPolygon but with the number of sides preset to 8.
u: For further steps see Sketcher CreateRegularPolygon.

Sketcher_CreatePentagon.d: The Sketcher CreatePentagon tool creates a pentagon. (v1.0): This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateRegularPolygon but with the number of sides preset to 5.
u: For further steps see Sketcher CreateRegularPolygon.

Sketcher_CreatePeriodicBSpline.d: The Sketcher CreatePeriodicBSpline tool creates a periodic (closed) B-spline curve from control points. (v1.0): This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateBSpline but with a different initial mode.
u: For further steps see Sketcher CreateBSpline.

Sketcher_CreatePeriodicBSplineByInterpol.d: The Sketcher CreatePeriodicBSplineByInterpolation tool creates a periodic (closed) B-spline curve from knot points. (v1.0): This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateBSpline but with a different initial mode.
u: For further steps see Sketcher CreateBSpline.
Sketcher_CreatePeriodicBSplineByInterpol.m: Sketch → Geometries → Periodic B-Spline From Knots

Sketcher_CreatePoint.d: The Sketcher CreatePoint tool creates a point.
u: The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.
Pick a point. Or with Pos-OVP: enter its X- and/or Y-coordinate.
The point is created and applicable Pos-OVP based constraints are added.
If the tool runs in continue mode:

Sketcher_CreatePointFillet.d: The Sketcher CreatePointFillet tool creates a fillet between two non-parallel edges. If two straight edges connected by a Coincident constraint are filleted, the related common point is preserved by adding a Point object that has a Point onto object constraint with both edges. Constraints connected to the common point are transferred to the new point object. Apart from that this tool is identical to the Sketcher CreateFillet tool. See there for more information.
u: For further steps see Sketcher CreateFillet.
Sketcher_CreatePointFillet.m: Sketch → Sketcher geometries → Create corner-preserving fillet

Sketcher_CreatePolyline.d: The Sketcher CreatePolyline tool creates a series of line and arc segments connected by their endpoints. The tool has a fillet option.
u: The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.
The Polyline Parameters section is added at the top of the Sketcher Dialog.
Optionally press the F key or click the Fillet checkbox to toggle the fillet option. If this option is selected a fillet is created between a new segment and its previous segment if possible.
The modes of the tool require a previous segment. Do one of the following:
Optionally press the M key or select from the dropdown list in the parameters section to change the tool mode:
Optionally repeat the previous step to create more segments.

Sketcher_CreatePolylineLegacy.d: The Sketcher CreatePolylineLegacy tool creates a series of line and arc segments connected by their endpoints. The tool has several modes.
u: The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.
The modes of the tool require a previous segment. Do one of the following:
Optionally press the M key one or more times to cycle through the modes for the next segment. The available modes are:
While in any of the arc modes, optionally hold down the Ctrl key to snap the arc to increments of 45° relative to the previous segment.
Pick the endpoint of the segment.
Optionally repeat this to create more segments.

Sketcher_CreateRectangle.d: The Sketcher CreateRectangle tool creates a rectangle. (v1.0): The tool has four modes, two of which can also produce parallelograms. Rounded corners and creating an offset copy are optional features.
u: The cursor changes to a cross with the current tool mode icon.
The Rectangle Parameters section ((v1.0)) is added at the top of the Sketcher Dialog.
Optionally press the U key or check the Rounded corners checkbox to apply fillets to the rectangle. (v1.0)
Optionally press the J key or check the Frame checkbox to create a second offset shape. (v1.0)
Optionally press the M key or select from the dropdown list in the parameters section to change the tool mode:
If Rounded corners is selected: Pick a point to define the fillet radius. Or with Dim-OVP: enter it.

Sketcher_CreateRectangle_Center.d: The Sketcher CreateRectangle Center tool creates a centered rectangle. (v1.0): This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateRectangle but with a different initial mode.
u: For further steps see Sketcher CreateRectangle.

Sketcher_CreateRegularPolygon.d: The Sketcher CreateRegularPolygon tool creates a regular polygon.
u: Enter the Number of sides in the dialog that opens.
The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.
The Polygon Parameters section ((v1.0)) is added at the top of the Sketcher Dialog.
Optionally change the number of Sides (this can also be done after picking the center):
Pick the center of the polygon. Or with Pos-OVP: enter its X- and/or Y-coordinate.

Pick the first point of the polygon, this also defines the radius of the circumscribed circle. Or with Dim-OVP: enter the radius of the circle and/or the angle of the first point. The angle is relative to the X-axis of the…

Sketcher_CreateSlot.d: The Sketcher CreateSlot tool creates a slot, a closed polyline consisting of two semicircles connected by two parallel straight lines.
u: The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.
Pick the center of the first semicircle. Or with Pos-OVP: enter its X- and/or Y-coordinate.
Pick the center of the second semicircle. Or with Dim-OVP: enter the distance between the centers and/or angle of the slot. The angle is relative to the X-axis of the sketch.
Pick a point to define the radius of the slot. Or with Dim-OVP: enter this radius.
The slot is created and applicable Pos-OVP and Dim-OVP based constraints are added.
If the tool runs in continue mode:

Sketcher_CreateSquare.d: The Sketcher CreateSquare tool creates a square. (v1.0): This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateRegularPolygon but with the number of sides preset to 4.
u: For further steps see Sketcher CreateRegularPolygon.

Sketcher_CreateText.d: The Sketcher CreateText tool creates text geometry controlled by a text constraint.
u: The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.
The Text Parameters section is added at the top of the Sketcher Dialog.
Optionally press the M key or select from the dropdown list in the parameters section to change the tool mode:
The text, a Text object, is created and applicable Pos-OVP based constraints are added.
If the tool runs in continue mode:

Sketcher_CreateTriangle.d: The Sketcher CreateTriangle tool creates an equilateral triangle. (v1.0): This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateRegularPolygon but with the number of sides preset to 3.
u: For further steps see Sketcher CreateRegularPolygon.

Sketcher_DeleteAllConstraints.d: The Sketcher DeleteAllConstraints tool deletes all constraints from the sketch.
u: The Delete All Constraints dialog opens.
Sketcher_DeleteAllConstraints.m: Sketch → Sketcher Tools → Delete All Constraints

Sketcher_DeleteAllGeometry.d: The Sketcher DeleteAllGeometry tool deletes all geometry and all constraints from the sketch.
u: The Delete All Geometry dialog opens.
Sketcher_DeleteAllGeometry.m: Sketch → Sketcher Tools → Delete All Geometry

Sketcher_Dimension.d: The Sketcher Dimension tool is the context-sensitive constraint tool of the Sketcher Workbench. Based on the current selection, it offers appropriate dimensional constraints, but also geometric constraints.
u: Optionally select one or more elements (edges or points). B-spline edges are currently not supported.
The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.
If you have not yet selected an element: select one.
Depending on the selected element(s) a constraint is proposed.
Optionally select an additional element.
Optionally deselect an element by clicking it again.

Sketcher_EditSketch.d: The Sketcher EditSketch tool opens the Sketcher Dialog to edit an existing sketch.
u: The sketch is put in edit mode and the Sketcher Dialog opens.
To finish edit mode see Sketcher LeaveSketch.

Sketcher_Extend.d: The Sketcher Extend tool extends or shortens a line or an arc to an arbitrary location, or to a target edge or point.
u: If there is a previous selection it is cleared. The tool does not accept a pre-selection.
The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.
Select a line or an arc.
Move the cursor in the direction to extend or shorten.
Do one of the following:
If the tool runs in continue mode:

Sketcher_External.d: 1.0 and below: The Sketcher External tool projects edges and/or vertices belonging to objects outside the sketch onto the sketch plane. The projected geometry is called "external geometry". It stays parametrically linked to its source objects. External geometry edges are marked with a dedicated color (default magenta) and ((v1.0)) linetype. Similar to construction geometry, external geometry is not visible outside the sketch, it is intended to help define constraints and other geometry inside the sketch itself.
u: The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.
Select an external edge or a vertex. See Notes.
External geometry is created.
This tool always runs in continue mode: optionally keep selecting external edges and/or a vertices.
To finish, right-click or press Esc, or start another geometry or constraint creation tool.
Sketcher_External.m: Sketch → Sketcher tools → Create external geometry

Sketcher_Grid.d:
(v1.1): The Sketcher Grid settings can be changed in the menu of the Sketch Edit section of the Sketcher Dialog.

1.0 and below: The settings can be changed via the toolbar button.

Sketcher_Intersection.d: The Sketcher Intersection tool ((v1.1)) intersects faces and/or edges belonging to objects outside the sketch with the sketch plane. The intersected geometry is called "external geometry". It stays parametrically linked to its source objects. External geometry is marked with a dedicated color (default magenta). It can be defining geometry that is visible outside the sketch or construction geometry that is not visible outside the sketch.
u: The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.
Select one or more external faces and/or edges. See Notes.
External geometry is created.
This tool always runs in continue mode: optionally keep selecting external faces and/or edges.
To finish, right-click or press Esc, or start another geometry or constraint creation tool.

Sketcher_JoinCurves.d: The Sketcher JoinCurves tool creates a B-spline by joining two existing B-splines or other edges.
u: Do one of the following:

Sketcher_LeaveSketch.d: The Sketcher LeaveSketch tool finishes sketch edit mode and closes the Sketcher Dialog.
u: The Sketcher Dialog is closed.

Sketcher_MapSketch.d:
The Sketcher MapSketch tool attaches a sketch to selected geometry.

Typical use cases are:

  • The sketch was created on a standard plane (XY, XZ or YZ) and you want to attach it to the face of a solid in order to build a new feature upon it.
  • The sketch was attached to a specific face of a solid but you need to attached it to a different face.
  • A broken model needs to be repaired.
u: Select an object with a shape, or one or more vertices, edges, and/or faces, and/or a plane.
The Select Sketch dialog opens.
Select a sketch from the dropdown list.
The Sketch Attachment dialog opens.
Select an attachment method from the dropdown list. Or select Do not attach to detach the sketch.

Sketcher_MergeSketches.d: The Sketcher MergeSketches tool merges two or more sketches.
u: Select two or more sketches.
A new sketch is created.

Sketcher_MirrorSketch.d: The Sketcher MirrorSketch tool mirrors sketches across their X-axis, Y-axis, or origin.
u: Select one or more sketches.
The Select Mirror Axis or Point dialog opens.
Select one of the available options:
For each selected sketch a new sketch is created.

Sketcher_Move.d: The Sketcher Move command moves the selected sketch elements from one point to another, using the last selected point as reference.
u: Select the sketch elements for the move operation.
Move the mouse in the 3D view to the desired location.By keeping Ctrl pressed (Cmd on macOS), the angle to the location can be fixed in steps of 5°. (v0.20)
Left-click in the 3D view to finish the move. The existing constraints move as well.
If you want to detach an element and move it freely, delete its locking constraints and drag it with the mouse.

Sketcher_NewSketch.d:
The Sketcher NewSketch tool creates a new sketch and opens the Sketcher Dialog to edit it.

Note that the PartDesign Workbench has its own New Sketch tool. When working on a PartDesign Body that tool should be used instead.
u: If the sketch should be attached to existing geometry: select an object with a shape, or one or more vertices, edges, and/or faces, and/or a plane.
If geometry has been selected:
If there is no selection, or Do not attach has been selected in the previous step:
A sketch is created.
The sketch is put in edit mode and the Sketcher Dialog opens.
To finish edit mode see Sketcher LeaveSketch.

Sketcher_Offset.d: The Sketcher Offset tool creates equidistant edges around selected edges.
u: Select one or more lines, circles and/or circular arcs.
The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.
The Offset Parameters section is added at the top of the Sketcher Dialog.
Optionally press the U key or check the Delete original geometries checkbox to only keep the new outline.
Optionally press the J key or check the Add offset constraint checkbox to add a dimensional constraint between the offset outline and the original geometry.
Optionally press the M key or select from the dropdown list in the parameters section to change the tool mode:

Sketcher_Projection.d: The Sketcher Projection tool ((v1.1)) creates a perpendicular projection of edges and/or vertices belonging to objects outside the sketch onto the sketch plane. The projected geometry is called "external geometry". It stays parametrically linked to its source objects. External geometry is marked with a dedicated color (default magenta). It can be defining geometry that is visible outside the sketch or construction geometry that is not visible outside the sketch.
u: The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.
Select one or more external faces, edges and/or vertices. See Notes.
External geometry is created.
This tool always runs in continue mode: optionally keep selecting external faces, edges and/or vertices.
To finish, right-click or press Esc, or start another geometry or constraint creation tool.

Sketcher_RectangularArray.d: The Sketcher Rectangular array command creates an array of selected sketcher elements.
u: Select sketcher elements in task panel or in 3D view.
Specify the options for the array in the dialog that opens.
Move the mouse in the 3D view towards the desired reference point.By keeping Ctrl pressed, the angle to the reference point can be fixed in steps of 5°. (v0.20)
Left-click in the 3D view to create the array.
To set the distances between the array elements, edit the dimensional constraints of the array.

Sketcher_RemoveAxesAlignment.d: The Sketcher RemoveAxesAlignment tool removes the axes alignment of selected edges by replacing horizontal and vertical constraints with parallel and perpendicular constraints. The edges can then be rotated without losing their orthogonal relationship.
u: Select two or more edges with horizontal or vertical constraints, for example a rectangle.
Sketcher_RemoveAxesAlignment.m: Sketch → Sketcher Tools → Remove Axes Alignment

Sketcher_RenderingOrder.d:
(v1.1): The Sketcher Rendering Order can be changed in the menu of the Sketch Edit section of the Sketcher Dialog.

1.0 and below: The order can be changed via the toolbar button.

Sketcher_ReorientSketch.d: The Sketcher ReorientSketch tool places a sketch on one of the main planes with an optional offset. It can also be used to detach a sketch.
u: Select a sketch.
If the sketch is attached:
The Choose Orientation dialog opens.
Optionally press the Cancel button to only detach the sketch and finish the tool.
Specify the plane for the orientation. The plane is relative to the local coordinate system the sketch is in:
Optionally change the Offset. The offset is measured along the Z, Y or X-axis of the local coordinate system.

Sketcher_RestoreInternalAlignmentGeometr.d: The Sketcher RestoreInternalAlignmentGeometry tool deletes the internal geometry of elements, or recreates missing internal geometry. The tool does not delete internal geometry that has associated constraints.
u: Select one or more sketch elements that support internal geometry (ellipse, elliptical arc, hyperbolic arc, parabolic arc or B-spline).
Internal geometry is deleted for selected elements with a complete set of internal geometry, else missing internal geometry is recreated.
Sketcher_RestoreInternalAlignmentGeometr.m: Sketch → Visual Helpers → Toggle Internal Geometry

Sketcher_Rotate.d: The Sketcher Rotate tool rotates or optionally creates rotated copies of selected elements. The total number of elements (including the original) can be set directly, and full 360-degree patterns can be created by entering the angle for a full circle. A Symmetric option was added to distribute the elements evenly on both sides of the original. (v26.3)
u: Select one or more edges and/or point objects. Constraints, except horizontal and vertical constraints, restricted to the selected elements are also processed. If the original elements are rotated, any other constraints…
The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.
The Rotate Parameters section is added at the top of the Sketcher Dialog.
Optionally set the total number of Elements (including the original; the default of 1 keeps only the original): (v26.3)

Optionally check the Symmetric checkbox to distribute the elements evenly on both sides of the original instead of only in the rotation direction. For an even total, the original element is replaced by two symmetric elements.…
Optionally check the Apply equal constraints checkbox to exclude dimensional constraints from the operation, and instead apply equal constraints between the original objects and their copies.
Sketcher_Rotate.m: Sketch → Sketcher Tools → Rotate / Polar Transform

Sketcher_Scale.d: The Sketcher Scale tool scales or optionally creates scaled copies of selected elements.
u: Select one or more edges and/or point objects. Constraints restricted to the selected elements are also processed. If the original elements are scaled, any other constraints associated with them will be deleted.
The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.
The Scale Parameters section is added at the top of the Sketcher Dialog.
Optionally press the U key or check the Keep original geometries checkbox to create scaled copies of the selected elements.
Pick the base point for the scale operation. Or with Pos-OVP: enter its X- and/or Y-coordinate.
Pick the end point of the first auxiliary line. Its angle and length are arbitrary.

Sketcher_SelectConflictingConstraints.d:
The Sketcher SelectConflictingConstraints tool selects the conflicting constraints in the sketch.

If such constraints exist in a sketch the Sketch Edit section of the Sketcher Dialog displays this message:

  • Over-constrained:(#, #, #)

Where (#, #, #) are the indices of the constraints. Clicking the underlined text will select the conflicting constraints.
u: The conflicting constraints are selected.
Optionally click in an empty area in the 3D View to clear the selection.
Sketcher_SelectConflictingConstraints.m: Sketch → Visual Helpers → Select Conflicting Constraints

Sketcher_SelectConstraints.d: The Sketcher SelectConstraints tool selects the constraints associated with sketch elements.
u: Select one or more sketch elements.
The associated constraints are selected.
Optionally click in an empty area in the 3D View to clear the selection.
Sketcher_SelectConstraints.m: Sketch → Visual Helpers → Select Associated Constraints

Sketcher_SelectElementsAssociatedWithCon.d: The Sketcher SelectElementsAssociatedWithConstraints tool selects the sketch elements associated with constraints.
u: Select one or more constraints.
The associated sketch elements are selected.
Optionally click in an empty area in the 3D View to clear the selection.
Sketcher_SelectElementsAssociatedWithCon.m: Sketch → Visual Helpers → Select Associated Geometry

Sketcher_SelectElementsWithDoFs.d:
The Sketcher SelectElementsWithDoFs tool selects the under-constrained elements in the sketch.

If such elements exist in a sketch the Sketch Edit section of the Sketcher Dialog displays this message:

  • Under-constrained: n Degrees of Freedom

Where n is the remaining number of degrees of freedom. Clicking the underlined text will select the under-constrained elements.

Please note that a sketch can also have under-constrained elements if one of the other messages is displayed.
u: The under-constrained sketch elements are selected.
Optionally click in an empty area in the 3D View to clear the selection.
Sketcher_SelectElementsWithDoFs.m: Sketch → Visual Helpers → Select Under-Constrained Elements

Sketcher_SelectHorizontalAxis.d: The Sketcher SelectHorizontalAxis tool selects the horizontal axis of the sketch.
u: The horizontal axis of the sketch is selected.
Sketcher_SelectHorizontalAxis.m: Sketch → Sketcher Tools → Select Horizontal Axis

Sketcher_SelectOrigin.d: The Sketcher SelectOrigin tool selects the origin of the sketch.
u: The origin of the sketch is selected.

Sketcher_SelectRedundantConstraints.d:
The Sketcher SelectRedundantConstraints tool selects the redundant constraints in the sketch.

If such constraints exist in a sketch the Sketch Edit section of the Sketcher Dialog displays this message:

  • Redundant constraints:(#, #, #)

Where (#, #, #) are the indices of the constraints. Clicking the underlined text will select the redundant constraints.

Please note that a sketch can also have redundant constraints if one of the other messages is displayed.
u: The redundant constraints are selected.
Optionally click in an empty area in the 3D View to clear the selection.
Sketcher_SelectRedundantConstraints.m: Sketch → Visual Helpers → Select Redundant Constraints

Sketcher_SelectVerticalAxis.d: The Sketcher SelectVerticalAxis tool selects the vertical axis of the sketch.
u: The vertical axis of the sketch is selected.
Sketcher_SelectVerticalAxis.m: Sketch → Sketcher Tools → Select Vertical Axis

Sketcher_Snap.d:
(v1.1): The Sketcher Snap settings can be changed in the menu of the Sketch Edit section of the Sketcher Dialog.

1.0 and below: The settings can be changed via the toolbar button.

Sketcher_Split.d: The Sketcher Split tool splits an edge. If the edge is a closed curve (i.e. a circle, an ellipse or a periodic B-spline) it is converted to an open curve (an arc, an elliptical arc or a non-periodic B-spline respectively).
u: If there is a previous selection it is cleared. The tool does not accept a pre-selection.
The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.
Click an edge at the point where it should be split.

If the original edge is a line or an open curve, two new edges are created connected by a coincident constraint. For closed curves a new open curve is created, the new point then does not receive a coincident constraint.…
This tool always runs in continue mode: optionally keep splitting edges.
To finish, click in an empty area in the 3D View, right-click or press Esc, or start another geometry or constraint creation tool.

Sketcher_StopOperation.d: The Sketcher StopOperation tool stops any currently running Sketcher tool.
u: Make sure a geometry or constraint creation tool is active.
The running tool is deactivated and the cursor changes to a simple arrow.

Sketcher_SwitchVirtualSpace.d:
The Sketcher SwitchVirtualSpace tool either (un)hides constraints or switches the visible virtual space.

A sketch has two virtual spaces that can contain constraints. All constraints are created in the main virtual space, but they can be hidden which moves them to the other virtual space.
u: Select one or more constraints. Constraints that are not visible in the current virtual space can be selected in the Constraints section of the Sketcher Dialog.
Sketcher_SwitchVirtualSpace.m: Sketch → Visual Helpers → Switch Virtual Space

Sketcher_Symmetry.d: The Sketcher Symmetry creates mirrored copies of selected elements.
u: Select one or more edges and/or point objects.
The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.
The Symmetry Parameters section ((v1.0)) is added at the top of the Sketcher Dialog.
Optionally press the U key or check the Delete original geometries checkbox to only keep the mirrored elements ((v1.0)).

Optionally press the J key or check the Create symmetry constraints checkbox to add a symmetric constraint between each original and mirrored point ((v1.0)). (v26.3): This option is enabled by default.
Select a line or a sketch axis to define the symmetry line, or a point to define the symmetry point.

Sketcher_ToggleActiveConstraint.d:
The Sketcher ToggleActiveConstraint tool activates or deactivates selected constraints. Deactivating constraints allows you to test other geometry arrangements without deleting constraints.

This is tool is similar to Sketcher ToggleDrivingConstraint, but contrary to that tool also works for geometric constraints, and values of deactivated dimensional constraints are preserved.
u: Select one or more constraints.
Active selected constraints are deactivated and turn grey (default color), while deactivated selected constraints are activated and return to red (default color).

Sketcher_ToggleConstruction.d:
The Sketcher ToggleConstruction tool either toggles the geometry creation tools to/from construction mode, or toggles selected geometry to/from construction geometry.

Construction geometry is marked with a dedicated color (default blue) and ((v1.0)) linetype. Construction geometry is not visible outside the sketch, it is intended to help define constraints and other geometry inside the sketch itself. Construction lines can however be used as a rotation axis by PartDesign Revolution.
u: Make sure there is no selection.
The mode of the geometry creation tools is toggled:
(v26.3): During a FreeCAD session this mode is remembered per sketch.

Sketcher_ToggleDrivingConstraint.d:
The Sketcher ToggleDrivingConstraint tool either toggles the dimensional constraint creation tools between driving and reference mode, or toggles selected dimensional constraints between those modes.

Contrary to driving constraints, reference constraints do not constrain the sketch, their value depends on other constraints, they are driven. They can be useful to verify measurements. They can be used in expressions, but not in the sketch itself.
u: Make sure no dimensional constraints have been selected.
The mode of the dimensional constraint creation tools is toggled:

Sketcher_Translate.d: The Sketcher Translate tool moves or optionally creates copies of selected elements. Copies are evenly distributed along one or two directions. A Symmetric option can distribute copies evenly on both sides of the original. (v26.3)
u: Select one or more edges and/or point objects. Constraints restricted to the selected elements are also processed. Any other constraints associated with the elements will be deleted.
The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.
The Translate Parameters section is added at the top of the Sketcher Dialog.
Pick the start point of the translation vector. Or with Pos-OVP: enter its X- and/or Y-coordinate.
Pick the end point of the translation vector. Or with Dim-OVP: enter the length and/or angle of the vector. The angle is relative to the X-axis of the sketch.
The elements are moved. No Pos-OVP or Dim-OVP based constraints are added.
Sketcher_Translate.m: Sketch → Sketcher Tools → Move / Array Transform

Sketcher_Trimming.d: The Sketcher Trimming tool trims an edge at the nearest intersections with other edges. If the selected edge does not intersect other edges it is deleted.
