u: If there is a previous selection it is cleared. The tool does not accept a pre-selection.
The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.
There are two modes:

If a portion is cut out, existing applicable constraints are transferred to the resulting new edge. Point-on-object constraints are added between the endpoint(s) of the trimmed edge and the cutting edge(s).
This tool always runs in continue mode: optionally keep trimming edges.
To finish, click in an empty area in the 3D View, right-click or press Esc, or start another geometry or constraint creation tool.

Sketcher_ValidateSketch.d: The Sketcher ValidateSketch tool can analyze and repair a sketch that is no longer editable or has invalid constraints, or add missing coincident constraints to a sketch created from imported geometry such as DXF files. It can also be useful to locate a missing coincidence in a native sketch that generates an error when trying to apply a PartDesign feature.
u: This tool cannot be used while a sketch is in edit mode. To finish edit mode see Sketcher LeaveSketch.
Select a sketch.
The Sketch Validation task panel opens. See Options for more information.

Sketcher_ViewSection.d: The Sketcher ViewSection tool toggles a temporary section plane that hides any objects and parts of objects in front of the sketch plane while the sketch is in edit mode. This is a per-sketch setting stored in the ViewSection View property of sketches.
u: This tool is only available if a sketch is in edit mode.

Sketcher_ViewSketch.d: The Sketcher ViewSketch tool aligns the 3D View to the sketch. The view is rotated so that the view direction is perpendicular to the sketch plane, and the X-axis of the sketch appears horizontal. It is useful if you have changed the view orientation to examine another aspect of the model and want to return to the default sketch view.
u: This tool is only available if a sketch is in edit mode.

Spreadsheet_AlignBottom.d: The Spreadsheet AlignBottom tool aligns the contents of selected cells to the bottom.
u: Make sure there is an active spreadsheet.
Select one or more cells.

Spreadsheet_AlignCenter.d: The Spreadsheet AlignCenter tool aligns the contents of selected cells to the horizontal center.
u: Make sure there is an active spreadsheet.
Select one or more cells.

Spreadsheet_AlignLeft.d: The Spreadsheet AlignLeft tool aligns the contents of selected cells to the left.
u: Make sure there is an active spreadsheet.
Select one or more cells.

Spreadsheet_AlignRight.d: The Spreadsheet AlignRight tool aligns the contents of selected cells to the right.
u: Make sure there is an active spreadsheet.
Select one or more cells.

Spreadsheet_AlignTop.d: The Spreadsheet AlignTop tool aligns the contents of selected cells to the top.
u: Make sure there is an active spreadsheet.
Select one or more cells.

Spreadsheet_AlignVCenter.d: The Spreadsheet AlignVCenter tool aligns the contents of selected cells to the vertical center.
u: Make sure there is an active spreadsheet.
Select one or more cells.

Spreadsheet_CreateSheet.d: The Spreadsheet CreateSheet tool adds a new spreadsheet to the active document.
u: Double-click the spreadsheet in the Tree View to open it on a new tab in the Main View Area.
Edit the contents of the cells.
Close the spreadsheet tab when you are finished, the values are saved automatically as you type them.

Spreadsheet_Export.d: The Spreadsheet Export tool exports a spreadsheet as a CSV file, which can be used in other applications. Note that the tab character, and not the comma, is the default field delimiter. But this can be changed in the Spreadsheet Preferences.
u: Make sure there is an active spreadsheet.

Spreadsheet_Import.d: The Spreadsheet Import tool imports a CSV file into a new spreadsheet. Note that the tab character, and not the comma, is the default field delimiter. But this can be changed in the Spreadsheet Preferences.
u: Select a CSV file.

Spreadsheet_MergeCells.d: The Spreadsheet MergeCells tool merges a rectangular cell range.
u: Make sure there is an active spreadsheet.
Select two or more cells that form a rectangular cell range. The range may include already merged cells.

Spreadsheet_SetAlias.d: The Spreadsheet SetAlias tool opens a dialog to define an alias for a cell. A cell can be referenced by its address (capital column letter + row number, e.g. B4) or by its alias.
u: Make sure there is an active spreadsheet.
Select a cell.
Enter an alias:

Spreadsheet_SplitCell.d: The Spreadsheet SplitCell tool splits a previously merged cell.
u: Make sure there is an active spreadsheet.
Select a merged cell.

Spreadsheet_StyleBold.d: The Spreadsheet StyleBold tool toggles the contents of selected cells to/from bold.
u: Make sure there is an active spreadsheet.
Select one or more cells.

Spreadsheet_StyleItalic.d: The Spreadsheet StyleItalic tool toggles the contents of selected cells to/from italic.
u: Make sure there is an active spreadsheet.
Select one or more cells.

Spreadsheet_StyleUnderline.d: The Spreadsheet StyleUnderline tool toggles the contents of selected cells to/from underlined.
u: Make sure there is an active spreadsheet.
Select one or more cells.

Std_About.d: The Std About command opens a dialog box that shows information about the FreeCAD program.
u: Select one of the tabs: About, Credits, License, Libraries or Privacy Policy.
Whenever you need to provide FreeCAD version information do the following:
Press Esc or the OK button to close the dialog.

Std_ActivateNextWindow.d: The Std ActivateNextWindow command activates the next window in the Main View Area. The next window is determined by the tabs order in Main View Area.
u: The Main View Area must contain at least two windows.

Std_ActivatePrevWindow.d: The Std ActivatePrevWindow command activates the previous window in the Main View Area. The previous window is determined by the tabs order in Main View Area.
u: The Main View Area must contain at least two windows.

Std_AddonMgr.d: The Std AddonMgr command opens the Addon Manager. With the Addon Manager you can install and manage external workbenches, macros, and preference packs provided by the FreeCAD community. By default the available addons are taken from two repositories, FreeCAD-addons and from the Macros recipes page of this wiki. If git is installed on your system, additional macros will be loaded from FreeCAD-macros. Custom repositories can be added in the Addon Manager preferences.
u: If you are using the Addon Manager for the first time, a dialog box will open warning you that no guarantees can be made regarding the safety or functionality of the addons. Press the Continue button to confirm.
The Addon Manager dialog box opens. For more information see Options.
If you have installed or updated a workbench a new dialog box will open informing you that you have to restart FreeCAD for the changes to take effect.

Std_AlignToSelection.d:
The Std AlignToSelection command points the camera in the active 3D View in the direction of the normal of a face, the normal of a plane defined by a planar curved edge, or the direction of a straight edge. (v26.3): If multiple elements are selected that define multiple normals, the average of the normals is used.

The final direction of the camera is the direction of the normal, or its opposite, whichever is closest to the previous camera direction.
u: Select one (1.1 and below) or more (26.3 and above) faces or edges the 3D View.
Std_AlignToSelection.m: View → Standard Views → Align to Selection

Std_Alignment.d: The Std Alignment command aligns an object in relation to a fixed reference object using one or more point pairs.
u: Select the reference object. This will be the fixed object and not be changed.
Hold down the Ctrl key while you select the object whose placement you want to change.
A new window will appear in the Main View Area. This window consists of two views: on the left the movable object is displayed and on the right the fixed object.
Define the first point pair by clicking a point in each view. This point pair is used to move the movable object.
Define one or two additional point pairs if you also want to rotate the movable object.
Right-click one of the views and select the Align option from the context menu to complete the command.

Std_AnnotationLabel.d: The Std AnnotationLabel command creates an annotation label in the 3D View.
u: Select one or more objects. The first selected object determines the Base Position of the label, which in turn determines its initial Text Position. See Notes.
Select the Edit → Create → Annotation Label option from the menu. (v26.3)
A Label object is created.
Change the Label Text property to set the label text.
Optionally, drag the label in the 3D View to a different position.
Optionally, change the View properties to modify the appearance of the label.

Std_AxisCross.d:
The Std AxisCross command toggles the axis cross in the active 3D View.

The axis cross consists of three arrows representing the positive X-, Y- and Z-axis of the global coordinate system. Their common start point is the origin of the global coordinate system.

Std_BoxSelection.d: The Std BoxSelection command selects objects from a user defined rectangular area, a box, in the 3D View. Multiple box selections can be combined by holding down Ctrl while dragging subsequent boxes.
u: Do one of the following:

Std_CascadeWindows.d: The Std CascadeWindows command rearranges the windows in the Main View Area so that they are all visible but do overlap. The result is determined by the order in which the windows were last activated.
u: The Main View Area must contain at least two windows.

Std_ClarifySelection.d: The Std ClarifySelection command displays a menu listing nearby geometrical entities of different types next to the cursor when hovering the model.
u: Place the cursor over geometry in the 3D View.
A menu listing object types appears next to the cursor. Depending on the objects near the cursor, it may include:
Choose an object type.
Move the cursor over the submenu that appears. Hovered submenu items are highlighted in the 3D View.
Click an item to select it.

Std_CloseActiveWindow.d: The Std CloseActiveWindow command closes the active window. To close a document all its windows must be closed.
u: To close a document: repeat this for all windows belonging to it.
When closing the last window of a document that has been modified, a dialog box will prompt you to save it.

Std_CloseAllWindows.d: The Std CloseAllWindows command closes all windows, thereby closing all documents.
u: If there are modified documents a dialog box will prompt you to save them.

Std_Copy.d: The Std Copy command copies objects to the Clipboard.
u: Select one or more objects.
If the objects have dependencies that have not been selected, a dialog box will prompt you to specify which should be included.

Std_Cut.d:
The Std Cut command is limited: it can only be used for spreadsheet cells. The command copies the contents and properties of cells to the Clipboard and then clears them.

To cut other objects you can use the Std Copy command followed by a delete operation.
u: Select one or more cells in the spreadsheet.
Select one or more objects.

Std_DemoMode.d: The Std DemoMode command will continuously rotate the camera in a 3D View.
u: The View Turntable dialog box opens.
Move the Angle slider to tilt the camera's virtual turn table.
Move the Speed slider to adjust the rotation speed of the camera.
Check the Fullscreen checkbox to switch the 3D View to fullscreen mode.
The Enable timer option is not supported at this time.
In fullscreen mode the dialog will disappear after ca. 5 seconds. It will reappear if the mouse is moved over the 3D View.

Std_DependencyGraph.d:
The Std DependencyGraph command displays the dependencies between objects in the active document in a graph. As opposed to the Tree View, objects are listed in reverse chronological order, with the first created object at the bottom.

It can be useful in analyzing a FreeCAD document and locating forks in a tree. The dependency graph layout will depend on which workbench was used to create the objects in the document. For example a model made exclusively in the PartDesign workbench can display a linear dependency graph with a single vertical branch. A model made with Part operations will have many branches, but for a single part they will join up at the top after Boolean operations. If they don't, it means that they are separate objects.
u: A new tab titled Dependency Graph opens in the Main View Area.
Use the mouse scroll wheel to zoom in or out.
Use the sliders at the bottom and at the right of the screen to pan the view. Alternatively hold down the left mouse button and move the mouse.

Std_DevHandbook.d:
The Std DevHandbook command opens the FreeCAD Developers Handbook in the system's default Internet browser. The command requires a working Internet connection.

Currently the command points to https://freecad.github.io/DevelopersHandbook.

Std_DlgCustomize.d: The Std DlgCustomize command opens the Customize dialog box giving access to several customization options.
u: The commands available in the Customize dialog box depend on the workbenches that have been loaded in the current FreeCAD session. So you should first load all workbenches whose commands you want to have access to.
The Customize dialog box opens. For more information see Interface Customization.
The Help button does not work at this time.

Std_DlgMacroExecute.d: The Std DlgMacroExecute command opens the Execute macro dialog box. From this dialog box macros can be executed, edited and managed.
u: The Execute macro dialog box opens. See Options.

Std_DlgMacroExecuteDirect.d: The Std DlgMacroExecuteDirect command executes the macro in the current Macro Editor window.
u: If required open the correct macro in the Macro Editor.
Make sure the Macro Editor window has the input focus.
The macro is executed.

Std_DlgMacroRecord.d: The Std DlgMacroRecord command starts a macro recording session during which user actions are stored in a FreeCAD macro, a file with the.FCMacro extension. A macro can later be replayed, executed, to repeat the recorded actions.
u: The Record Macro dialog box opens.
Enter a name for the macro in the Macro Name input box.
Optionally change the Macro Path by pressing the Choose folder button.
The Stop button does not work at this time.
The button image of the command changes to and the menu text changes to Stop Macro Recording.
Perform the actions you want to record.

Std_DlgParameter.d:
The Std DlgParameter command opens the Parameter Editor. In the Parameter Editor the parameters that control the behavior of FreeCAD and its workbenches can be inspected and optionally removed, added or changed. The parameters are stored in a file called user.cfg, the location of this file depends on your OS.

Working with the Parameter Editor requires some experience. For the most common parameters the Preferences Editor should be used instead.
u: The Parameter Editor dialog box opens. For more information see Options.
Optionally press the Save to disk button to immediately update the user.cfg file. This is not required as FreeCAD will automatically update that file when the application closes.

Std_DlgPreferences.d: The Std DlgPreferences command opens the Preferences Editor.

Std_DockOverlayAll.d:
The Std DockOverlayAll command toggles the overlay mode on or off for all docked panels simultaneously.

Overlay mode provides a way to maximize the space available for 3D Views by transforming docked panels (like the Combo View and Report View) into transparent floating widgets. When activated, these panels float on top of the main window, allowing the 3D View to expand into the space they previously occupied. The panels become fully opaque and usable when the mouse cursor hovers over them, and transparent again when the cursor moves away. This allows for interacting with the 3D model "through" the transparent panel.
Std_DockOverlayAll.m: View → Overlay Docked Panel → Toggle Overlay for All Panels

Std_DockOverlayMouseTransparent.d:
The Std DockOverlayMouseTransparent command toggles a global "click-through" mode for all panels currently in the overlay system.

When this mode is activated, all overlay panels become completely non-interactive to mouse input. All mouse actions —clicks, drags, scrolls, etc.— will pass directly through the panels to the 3D View or whichever widget is underneath them. The panels effectively become a visual-only layer.
u: The overlay mode must be active.
To disable the mode, use the same command again or press Esc.
Std_DockOverlayMouseTransparent.m: View → Overlay Docked Panel → Bypass Mouse Events in Overlay Panels

Std_DockOverlayToggle.d:
The Std DockOverlayToggle command moves a single docked panel into or out of the overlay system. This provides a more fine-grained control over the workspace, as apposed to the global Std DockOverlayAll command, which affects all panels at once.

To use this command, the mouse cursor must be positioned over the desired panel. When invoked, the panel will switch its state:

  • If it is a normal, docked panel, it will be moved into the overlay system, becoming a transparent floating widget.
  • If it is already an overlay panel, it will be moved out of the system and returned to its last known normal docked position.
u: The mouse cursor must be positioned over the docked panel you wish to affect. The panel can be in either its normal docked state or in overlay mode.
Std_DockOverlayToggle.m: View → Overlay Docked Panel → Toggle Overlay

Std_DockOverlayToggleBottom.d:
The Std DockOverlayToggleBottom command provides a shortcut to quickly show or hide the entire group of panels that are currently in the overlay system on the bottom side of the screen.

This command does not move panels into or out of the overlay system; it only toggles the visibility of the bottom overlay container itself. This is a convenience feature for users who want to temporarily hide all panels on one side of the view to maximize their workspace without having to exit the overlay mode completely.
u: The overlay mode must be active, and there must be at least one panel in the bottom overlay area.
Std_DockOverlayToggleBottom.m: View → Overlay Docked Panel → Toggle Bottom

Std_DockOverlayToggleLeft.d:
The Std DockOverlayToggleLeft command provides a shortcut to quickly show or hide the entire group of panels that are currently in the overlay system on the left side of the screen.

This command does not move panels into or out of the overlay system; it only toggles the visibility of the left overlay container itself. This is a convenience feature for users who want to temporarily hide all panels on one side of the view to maximize their workspace without having to exit the overlay mode completely.
u: The overlay mode must be active, and there must be at least one panel in the left overlay area.
Std_DockOverlayToggleLeft.m: View → Overlay Docked Panel → Toggle Left

Std_DockOverlayToggleRight.d:
The Std DockOverlayToggleRight command provides a shortcut to quickly show or hide the entire group of panels that are currently in the overlay system on the right side of the screen.

This command does not move panels into or out of the overlay system; it only toggles the visibility of the right overlay container itself. This is a convenience feature for users who want to temporarily hide all panels on one side of the view to maximize their workspace without having to exit the overlay mode completely.
u: The overlay mode must be active, and there must be at least one panel in the right overlay area.
Std_DockOverlayToggleRight.m: View → Overlay Docked Panel → Toggle Right

Std_DockOverlayToggleTop.d:
The Std DockOverlayToggleTop command provides a shortcut to quickly show or hide the entire group of panels that are currently in the overlay system on the top side of the screen.

This command does not move panels into or out of the overlay system; it only toggles the visibility of the top overlay container itself. This is a convenience feature for users who want to temporarily hide all panels on one side of the view to maximize their workspace without having to exit the overlay mode completely.
u: The overlay mode must be active, and there must be at least one panel in the top overlay area.
Std_DockOverlayToggleTop.m: View → Overlay Docked Panel → Toggle Top

Std_DockOverlayToggleTransparent.d:
The Std DockOverlayToggleTransparent command toggles the special "transparent active" mode for the single docked panel currently under the mouse cursor.

While Std DockOverlayTransparentAll acts as a global switch for all panels, this command enables the user to change the behavior of one panel at a time, in a more fine-grained manner.

In the standard overlay mode, panels become opaque when the mouse hovers over them. When "transparent active" mode is enabled for a panel, it will remain transparent even when the mouse is over it. The controls inside the panel remain fully interactive. This is useful for working in a panel while maintaining a view of the 3D model underneath it.
u: The main overlay mode must be active.
Move the mouse cursor so that it is positioned over the overlay panel you wish to change.
Std_DockOverlayToggleTransparent.m: View → Overlay Docked Panel → Toggle Transparent Mode

Std_DockOverlayTransparentAll.d:
The Std DockOverlayTransparentAll command toggles a special "transparent active" mode for all panels currently in the overlay system.

Normally, when overlay mode is active, panels become fully opaque when the mouse cursor hovers over them. The "transparent active" mode changes this behavior, causing the panels to remain transparent even when the mouse is over them. The controls inside the panel (buttons, tree items, etc.) are still fully interactive. This allows a user to work within a panel while still seeing the 3D model underneath, which can be useful on smaller screens.
u: The overlay mode must be active.
Std_DockOverlayTransparentAll.m: View → Overlay Docked Panel → Toggle Transparent Panels

Std_DrawStyle.d: The Std DrawStyle command can override the effect of the ViewDisplay Mode property of objects in a 3D View.

Std_DuplicateSelection.d: The Std DuplicateSelection command duplicates objects within the active document.
u: Select one or more objects.
If the objects have dependencies that have not been selected, a dialog box will prompt you to specify which should be included.

Std_Edit.d: The Std Edit command activates or deactivates an object's edit mode.
u: If no object is in edit mode: select a single object.
Either the default edit mode of the selected object is activated or the existing edit mode deactivated.

Std_Export.d: The Std Export command exports selected objects to a different file format. Many file formats are supported and for some formats multiple export options exist. See Import Export for more information.
u: Select one or more objects. To avoid exporting invisible or duplicate objects:
Select the correct file format in the dialog box.
Enter a filename.

Std_ExportDependencyGraph.d: The Std ExportDependencyGraph command exports the dependency graph of the active document to the *.gv file format used by the Graphviz software.
u: Enter a filename in the dialog box.

Std_Expressions.d: The Std Expressions command copies expression data to and from the Clipboard. The data references the names of objects and documents and can only be used in that context.
u: Select one or more objects.
Select the Expression Actions → Copy Selected option from the Tree View context menu.
Expression data from the objects is copied to the Clipboard.

Std_FreeCADDonation.d:
The Std FreeCADDonation command opens the FreeCAD Donate wiki page in the system's default Internet browser. The command requires a working Internet connection.

Currently the command points to https://wiki.freecad.org/Donate.

Std_FreeCADFAQ.d:
The Std FreeCADFAQ command opens the FreeCAD FAQ page in the system's default Internet browser. The command requires a working Internet connection.

Currently the command points to https://wiki.freecad.org/Frequently_asked_questions.

Std_FreeCADForum.d:
The Std FreeCADForum command opens the FreeCAD Forum in the system's default Internet browser. The command requires a working Internet connection.

Currently the command points to https://forum.freecad.org.

Std_FreeCADPowerUserHub.d:
The Std FreeCADPowerUserHub command opens the FreeCAD Power users documentation page in the system's default Internet browser. The command requires a working Internet connection.

Currently the command points to https://wiki.freecad.org/Power_users_hub.

Std_FreeCADUserHub.d:
The Std FreeCADUserHub command opens the FreeCAD Users documentation page in the system's default Internet browser. The command requires a working Internet connection.

Currently the command points to https://wiki.freecad.org/User_hub.

Std_FreeCADWebsite.d:
The Std FreeCADWebsite command opens the main website of the FreeCAD project in the system's default Internet browser. The command requires a working Internet connection.

Currently the command points to https://www.freecad.org.

Std_FreezeViews.d:
The Save Views… menu option saves all existing frozen views in a file with the *.cam extension.

  • To use this option one or more frozen views must exist. A frozen view is created with the Freeze View menu option.
  • Select the View → Freeze Display → Save Views… option from the menu.
  • Enter a filename in the dialog box.
  • Press the Save button.
  • Press Esc or the Cancel button to abort the command.
u: To use this option one or more frozen views must exist. A frozen view is created with the Freeze View menu option.
Enter a filename in the dialog box.

Std_Group.d:
Std Group (internally called App DocumentObjectGroup) is a general purpose container that allows you to group different types of objects in the Tree View, regardless of their data type. It is used as a simple folder to categorize and organize the objects in your model, in order to keep a logical structure. Std Groups may be nested inside other Std Groups.

The Std Group tool is not defined by a particular workbench, but by the base system, thus it is found in the Structure toolbar that is available in all workbenches.
u: An empty Group is created.
To add objects to the Group, select them in Tree View, and drag and drop them onto the Group.
To remove objects from the Group, drag them out of the Group, and onto the document label at the top of the Tree View.
Objects can also be added and removed by editing the DataGroup property of the Group.

Std_HideObjects.d: The Std HideObjects command hides all objects belonging to the active document in 3D Views.

Std_HideSelection.d: The Std HideSelection command hides selected objects in 3D Views.
u: Select one or more objects.

Std_LinkImport.d:
Std LinkImport imports the DataLinked Object from a Link into the current document, and then changes the attachment to this object.

This operation is helpful when working with assemblies in order to organize re-usable models that may be located in other documents.

Use Std LinkImportAll to import all linked objects.
u: Make sure you have a "source" document with an original object, say, a Std Part, and a second "target" document with a Link to that object.
Open the target document and select the Link to the object; its DataLinked Object property should show something like source#Part.
Std_LinkImport.m: Edit → Create → Link Actions → Import Links

Std_LinkImportAll.d:
Std LinkImportAll imports all DataLinked Objects from Links into the current document, and then changes the attachment to point to these imported objects.

This command runs Std LinkImport for all Links in a document.
u: Make sure you have a "source" document with original objects, and a second "target" document with Links to those objects.
Open the target document.
Std_LinkImportAll.m: Edit → Create → Link Actions → Import All Links

Std_LinkMake.d:
Std LinkMake creates an App Link, a type of object that references or links to another object in the same document, or in another document. It is especially designed to efficiently duplicate a single object multiple times, which helps with the creation of complex assemblies from smaller subassemblies, and from multiple reusable components like screws, nuts, and similar fasteners.

The App Link object was introduced in v0.19; in the past, simple duplication of objects could be achieved with Draft Clone, but this is a less efficient solution due to its implementation, which essentially creates a copy of the internal Shape of the source object. Instead, a Link directly references the original Shape, so it is more memory-efficient.
u: Select an object in the Tree View or 3D View for which you wish to create a Link.
The produced object has the same icon as the original object, but has an arrow overlay indicating it is a Link.
Std_LinkMake.m: Edit → Create → Link Actions → Make Link

Std_LinkMakeGroup.d:
Std LinkMakeGroup creates a specialized container called a LinkGroup. Unlike a Std Group, a LinkGroup has its own coordinate system (Placement) and can manage the lifecycle of its contents through different modes. It is primarily used for organizing assemblies and managing complex object references.

This command was originally envisaged for the Assembly 3 third-party workbench, and it was added to FreeCAD's core in v0.19 as part of the App Link introduction. As such, it predates the introduction of FreeCAD's built-in Assembly Workbench in v1.0. Thus some of Std LinkMakeGroup's features may no longer apply to building assemblies when using the Assembly workbench.
u: Select one or more objects in the Tree View or 3D View.
Right-click on the selection to display the context menu.
Navigate to Link Actions → Link Group in the context menu.
Select one of the options from the menu:

Std_LinkMakeRelative.d: Std LinkMakeRelative creates an App Link, just like Std LinkMake, but it operates on selected subelements first, and sets the DataLink Transform property to true.
u: Select a subelement in the 3D View, this means a vertex, edge, or face, or any combination of these. These subelements must belong to a single object.
The produced object has the same icon as the original object, but has two arrow overlays indicating it is a relative Link.
Std_LinkMakeRelative.m: Edit → Create → Link Actions → Make Sub-Link

Std_LinkReplace.d:
Std LinkReplace replaces an object that is inside another for an App Link version of the former.

This operation acts on the "children" of a "parent" object as seen in the Tree View. For example, given two objects (A and B) that participate in a Part Boolean operation, say, C = A + B, the A object can be replaced by a Link, so that C = A_link + B.

This operation can be done to replace nested objects that are in a complex assembly for a Link, which may be more efficient if that nested object is used many times in different sub-assemblies. The inverse operation is Std LinkUnlink. To create a generic Link see Std LinkMake.
u: Make sure you have one object that is inside another one. For example, consider that a Part Fuse was used with two previously created objects, a Part Sphere and a Part Cylinder.
Select the Sphere in the Tree View.
Std_LinkReplace.m: Edit → Create → Link Actions → Replace With Link

Std_LinkSelectAllLinks.d: The Std LinkSelectAllLinks command selects all App Link objects, links, that directly or indirectly link to the same source object.
u: To find links in multiple documents make sure the Tree View is switched to MultiDocument mode.
Select a source object that has links.
All links that link to the source object are selected.
Optionally use Std SelBack to reselect the source object.
Std_LinkSelectAllLinks.m: View → Link Navigation → Select All Links

Std_LinkSelectLinked.d: The Std LinkSelectLinked command selects the DataLinked Object, the source object, of an App Link object, a link.
u: Select a link.
The linked object is selected. If this object belongs to an external document that document is activated.
Optionally use Std SelBack to reselect the link.
Std_LinkSelectLinked.m: View → Link Navigation → Go to Linked Object

Std_LinkSelectLinkedFinal.d: The Std LinkSelectLinkedFinal command selects the DataLinked Object, the source object, of an App Link object, a link. But if that source object is also a link its linked object is selected instead. This is repeated until the linked object is not a link. This final source object is the deepest linked object.
u: Select a link.
The deepest linked object is selected. If this object belongs to an external document that document is activated.
Optionally use Std SelBack to reselect the link.
Std_LinkSelectLinkedFinal.m: View → Link Navigation → Go to Deepest Linked Object

Std_LinkUnlink.d:
Std LinkUnlink is essentially the opposite operation to Std LinkReplace.

This operation is used to remove a Link from a container like Std Part, and instead place the original object inside.
u: Make sure you have a Link that is inside a container, for example, a Link to a Part Sphere inside a Std Part.
Select the internal Link in the Tree View.

Std_MacroStartDebug.d: This command does not work at this time.

Std_MacroStepInto.d: This command does not work at this time.

Std_MacroStepOver.d: This command does not work at this time.

Std_MacroStopDebug.d: This command does not work at this time.

Std_MacroStopRecord.d: The Std MacroStopRecord command ends a macro recording session.
u: The command is only available during a macro recording session. See Std DlgMacroRecord.

Std_MainFullscreen.d: The Std MainFullscreen command toggles FreeCAD's main window fullscreen mode.

Std_MassProperties.d:
The Std MassProperties command starts the mass properties measurement feature. It provides the following information:

  • Physical Properties
  • Center of gravity
  • Center of volume
  • Inertia
u: Optionally preselect the solids to be measured.
A task panel opens. See Options for more information.
If no solids were preselected, select them in the 3D View or Tree View.
Press Esc or the Close button to finish the command.

Std_Measure.d: The Std Measure command gives access to the Unified Measurement Facility. It replaces several previous measurement commands, providing a versatile measurement functionality.
u: Optionally preselect the entities to be measured.
The Measurement task panel opens. See Options for more information.
If no geometrical entities were preselected, do one of the following:

The measurement result will be shown in the Result field and on a label displayed in the 3D View. That label will also include an icon indicating the type of measurement. The labels can be customized in the Preferences. They…
Press Esc or the Close button to finish the command.

Std_MeasureDistance.d: The Std MeasureDistance command creates a distance object that measures and displays the distance between two points.
u: Select the first dimension point anywhere on an object in the 3D View.
Select the second dimension point anywhere on an object in the 3D View.
The selection order of the points can have an impact on the position of the dimension line.
Optionally flip the position of the dimension line by changing the ViewMirror property of the distance object.

Std_MergeProjects.d: The Std MergeProjects command adds the contents of a FreeCAD file into the active document.
u: Select a FreeCAD file in the dialog box.

Std_New.d: The Std New command creates a new empty document and makes it the active document.

Std_OnlineHelp.d:
The Std OnlineHelp command opens the help documentation. To open the documentation for a specific command, use the Std WhatsThis command.

Since FreeCAD version 0.20 this command and the Help system are managed by a separate Help Module. For versions 0.20 and 0.21 this module is an addon that must be installed separately. In later versions the Help Module is integrated in FreeCAD.
u: The help documentation opens.

Std_Open.d: The Std Open command opens a file. If the file is not a native FreeCAD file (*.FCStd) its geometry will be imported into a new document. See Std Import for more information.
u: Optionally select the correct file format in the dialog box.
Select a file.

Std_OrthographicCamera.d: The Std OrthographicCamera command switches the camera in the active 3D View to orthographic view mode. In this mode, objects that are further from the camera do not appear smaller than those that are closer.

Std_Part.d:
Std Part (internally called App Part) is a general purpose container that keeps together a group of objects so that they can be moved together as a unit in the 3D View.

The Std Part object was developed to be the basic building block to create mechanical assemblies. In particular, it is meant to arrange objects that have a Part TopoShape, like Part Primitives, PartDesign Bodies, and other Part Features. The Std Part provides an Origin object with local X-, Y-, and Z-axis, and standard planes, that can be used as reference to position the contained objects. In addition, Std Parts may be nested inside other Std Parts to create a big assembly from smaller sub-assemblies.
u: An empty Part is created and automatically becomes active.
To add objects to the Part, select them in Tree View, and drag and drop them onto the Part.
To remove objects from the Part, drag them out of the Part, and onto the document label at the top of the Tree View.
Objects can also be added and removed by editing the DataGroup property of the Part.

Std_Paste.d: The Std Paste command pastes objects from the Clipboard into the active document.

Std_PerspectiveCamera.d: The Std PerspectiveCamera command switches the camera in the active 3D View to perspective view mode. In this mode, objects that are further from the camera appear smaller than those that are closer.

Std_Placement.d: The Std Placement command displays the Placement task panel for a selected object.
u: Select a single object that has a DataPlacement property.
Change one or more of the translation and rotation parameters.
Do one of the following:
Press Esc or the Cancel button to abort the operation. This will undo any changes that have not been applied.

Std_Print.d: The Std Print command is primarily intended to print TechDraw Workbench pages, but can also be used to print what is currently visible in the 3D View.
u: If required activate the correct TechDraw page or change the 3D View to your liking.
The standard print dialog box pops up.

Std_PrintPdf.d: The Std PrintPdf command is primarily intended to create PDF files from TechDraw Workbench pages, but can also be used to create a PDF from what is currently visible in the 3D View.
u: If required activate the correct TechDraw page or change the 3D View to your liking.
Enter a filename in the dialog box.

Std_PrintPreview.d: The Std PrintPreview command will show a preview of the result of the Std Print command. You can also print directly from the preview dialog box.
u: If required activate the correct TechDraw page or change the 3D View to your liking.
The Print Preview dialog box that pops up has several button options. If you have zoomed in you can pan by holding down the left mouse button and moving the mouse.
Use the dialog box's Print button.

Std_ProjectInfo.d: The Std ProjectInfo command shows a dialog box with details of the active document. Some of this information can be edited.
u: A dialog box with the following information pops up:
Enter the required information and press the OK button.

Std_ProjectUtil.d: With the Std ProjectUtil command you can extract files from a FreeCAD document (*.FCStd), which is in fact a ZIP file, and, after manual edits, create a new document from them.
u: The Document Utility dialog box opens.
Select the *.FCStd file you want to edit.
Select a folder where the document should be extracted. It is advisable to select an empty folder.

Std_Properties.d: The Std Properties command displays the Property View panel. This panel is only available if the Tree View and Property View mode preference is set to Independent. If the preference is set to Combined, or if the panel is already visible, this command has no effect.
u: Select one or more objects.
The Property View panel is displayed.

Std_PythonHelp.d:
The Std PythonHelp command starts a web server that communicates with the system's default Internet browser over a local socket. The web server displays information about the available Python modules, classes and functions of FreeCAD. The required pages are generated automatically.

The web server is based on Python's pydoc module, and thus extracts the docstrings of Python files (*.py), and textual documentation defined in the Python wrappers (*.xml) which expose the underlying C++ code.
u: Click on any of the links to go to the documentation of a specific class or function.

Std_Quit.d: The Std Quit command closes the FreeCAD application and optionally saves modified documents.
u: If there are modified documents a dialog box will prompt you to save them.

Std_RandomColor.d: The Std RandomColor command applies a random Diffuse Color to the ViewShape Appearance property of selected objects.
u: Select one or more objects.

Std_RecallWorkingView.d: The Std RecallWorkingView recalls the active 3D View's stored working view. For more information see Std StoreWorkingView.
u: Make sure a 3D View is active for which the Std StoreWorkingView command has been used at least once.
Std_RecallWorkingView.m: View → Standard Views → Recall Working View

Std_RecentFiles.d: The Std RecentFiles menu option displays a list of recent files which can be opened.
u: Select the File → Open Recent option from the menu to display the recent files list.
Select a file from the list to open it.

Std_Recompute.d: The Std Recompute command recomputes selected objects ((v26.3)), or the active document if no objects are selected and a recompute is required.
u: Optionally select one or more objects.

Std_Redo.d: The Std Redo command reverses the action of the Std Undo command.
Std_Redo.k: Ctrl + Shift + Z or Ctrl + Y

Std_Refresh.d: The Std Refresh command recomputes the active document. The command is disabled if no recompute is required.

Std_ReportBug.d:
The Std ReportBug command opens the FreeCAD GitHub issues page in the system's default Internet browser. This page should be used to report bugs and submit feature requests. The command requires a working Internet connection.

Currently the command points to https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/issues.

Std_RestartInSafeMode.d: The Std RestartInSafeMode command restarts FreeCAD in a factory reset state for debugging. It temporarily disables user configurations, addons, themes and other customizations.
u: A warning dialog box opens.
FreeCAD is restarted in safe mode.
Restart FreeCAD again to exit safe mode

Std_Revert.d: The Std Revert command closes the active document and reopens the last saved version of the document.

Std_Save.d: The Std Save command saves the active document.
u: For a new document: enter a filename in the dialog box and press the Save button.

Std_SaveAll.d: The Std SaveAll command saves all open documents.
u: For new documents: enter a filename in the dialog box and press the Save button.

Std_SaveAs.d: The Std SaveAs command saves the active document under a new file name.
u: Enter a filename in the dialog box.

Std_SaveCopy.d: The Std SaveCopy command saves a copy of the active document under a new file name.
u: Enter a filename in the dialog box.

Std_SceneInspector.d: The Std SceneInspector command opens a dialog box displaying an overview of all nodes in the scenegraph of the active 3D View. It is more a utility for programmers than for average users. It can be used to find out why the rendering is slow or why something isn't rendered properly.
u: The Scene Inspector dialog box opens.
The dialog box is modeless, meaning it can stay open while you continue working in FreeCAD.
Optionally press the Refresh to update the overview.

Std_SelBack.d: The Std SelBack command restores the previous recorded Tree View selection. Note that selections are only recorded if Tree RecordSelection mode is switched on.
u: There has to be a previous Tree View selection.
The previous selection is restored.
Std_SelBack.m: View → Tree View Actions → Selection Back

Std_SelBoundingBox.d: The Std SelBoundingBox command toggles the global bounding box highlighting mode. If this mode is switched on, selected objects are marked in a 3D View with a highlighted bounding box even if their ViewSelection Style is set to Shape.

Std_SelForward.d: The Std SelForward command restores the next recorded Tree View selection. Note that selections are only recorded if Tree RecordSelection mode is switched on.
u: There has to be a next Tree View selection.
The next selection is restored.
Std_SelForward.m: View → Tree View Actions → Selection Forward

Std_SelectAll.d: The Std SelectAll command selects all objects in the active document.

Std_SelectVisibleObjects.d: The Std SelectVisibleObjects command selects all visible objects. Note that for each PartDesign body typically two objects will be selected: the body itself and its DataTip object.

Std_SendToPythonConsole.d:
The Std SendToPythonConsole command creates variables in the Python Console referencing selected objects and selected subobjects, along with some other useful variables. They can be used in the development of Python code.

The following variables are created:
u: Select one or more objects and/or one or more subobjects belonging to one or more objects.
If required the Python Console opens.
The Python Console receives the keyboard focus.

Std_SetAppearance.d: The Std SetAppearance command sets the display properties of selected objects.
u: Select one or more objects.
The Display Properties task panel opens. See Options.
Change one or more properties.
The objects are updated immediately.
Optionally select one or more new objects whose properties you want to change.

Std_SetMaterial.d: The Std SetMaterial command sets the material of selected objects.
u: Select one or more objects.
The Material task panel opens.
If required click on the down arrow to the right of the current material to show the full task panel.
Select a material from the list.
The objects are updated immediately.
Optionally select one or more new objects whose material you want to change.

Std_ShowObjects.d: The Std ShowObjects command shows all objects belonging to the active document in 3D Views. Be careful when you use this command as it will also show sub-elements of PartDesign bodies and objects used for Part Booleans. In most cases these should stay invisible.

Std_ShowSelection.d: The Std ShowSelection command shows selected objects in 3D Views.
u: Select one or more objects.

Std_StoreWorkingView.d:
The Std StoreWorkingView command stores the camera settings of the active 3D View in its temporary working view. This view can be recalled with the Std RecallWorkingView command.

Each 3D View has its own working view. Storing a new working view will overwrite the existing working view of the active 3D View. When a 3D View is closed its working view is lost.
u: Make sure a 3D View is active.
Std_StoreWorkingView.m: View → Standard Views → Store Working View

Std_TextDocument.d: The Std TextDocument command creates an object capable of holding arbitrary text. This element can be used to write general information or documentation about the model.
u: Double-click the newly created object in the Tree View to open a tab in which to write text.
Add text.
Close the tab and save the file when asked.

Std_TextureMapping.d: The Std TextureMapping command temporarily maps a texture onto all objects in a 3D View.
u: The Texture task panel opens.
Optionally check the Environment checkbox.
Select an image file in the dialog box.

Std_TileWindows.d: The Std TileWindows command rearranges the windows in the Main View Area so that they are all visible and do not overlap. The result is determined by the order in which the windows were last activated.
u: The Main View Area must contain at least two windows.

Std_ToggleBottomPanels.d: The Std ToggleBottomPanels command toggles the visibility of the bottom panels (usually the Report View and the Python Console).

Std_ToggleBreakpoint.d: This command does not work at this time.

Std_ToggleClipPlane.d: The Std ToggleClipPlane command temporarily hides objects and parts of objects on one side of up to three virtual planes in the active 3D View.
u: The Clipping dialog box opens.
Do one of the following:
Optionally change the view to inspect the model.

Std_ToggleFreeze.d: The Std ToggleFreeze command toggles the freeze state of objects. A frozen object is not recomputed when the objects it depends on change. The freeze state of objects is not stored in the document.
u: Select one or more objects.
Select the Toggle Freeze option from the Tree View context menu.
Frozen objects are marked with the command icon in the Tree View.
If objects have been thawed: optionally recompute the document.

Std_ToggleNavigation.d:
The Std ToggleNavigation command is intended for certain inspection operations and certain interactive mesh editing operations. These operations are quite 'expensive' and therefore rely on an edit mode during which most navigation options are disabled. With this command it is possible to temporarily switch from edit mode to navigation mode, and, after changing the 3D View, switch back to edit mode.

Do not confuse this command with the Std Edit command.
u: Switch to the Mesh Workbench.
The Regular Solid dialog box opens.
Choose Ellipsoid from the dropdown list.
Select the mesh object.
Pick points in the 3D View to define a polygon that overlaps one half of the mesh.
Right-click and choose Inner from the context menu.

Std_ToggleObjects.d: The Std ToggleObjects command toggles the visibility of all objects belonging to the active document in 3D Views. Be careful when you use this command as it will also toggle the visibility of sub-elements of PartDesign bodies and objects used for Part Booleans. In most cases these should stay invisible.

Std_ToggleSelectability.d: The Std ToggleSelectability command toggles the selectability of objects in 3D Views.
u: Select one or more objects.

Std_ToggleTransparency.d: The Std ToggleTransparency command toggles the transparency of selected objects between 0% (opaque) and 70%.
u: Select one or more objects.
Objects that were transparent (1% or more) become opaque. Opaque objects become 70% transparent.

Std_ToggleVisibility.d: The Std ToggleVisibility command toggles the visibility of selected objects in 3D Views.
u: Select one or more objects.

Std_TransformManip.d: The Std TransformManip command allows you to apply rotation increments and translation increments to a selected object. This can be done either by dragging the interactive dragger in the 3D View or, (v1.1), by entering precise values in the task panel, either in any (local) dragger coordinate system, the global coordinate system, or (v26.3), any custom coordinate system defined by an object with a placement in the document.
u: Select an object with a DataPlacement property. See Notes.
The Transform task panel opens.
Optionally adjust the snapping parameters: These are values for snapping to increments when dragging in the 3D View, either for rotation or translation.
Do one or more of the following:

Optionally, adjust the location of the dragger, coordinate system, input precise delta (local), absolute (global), or relative to a custom coordinate system increments, or move the object to a target object. (v1.1). See the…
Do one of the following:

Std_TreeCollapseDocument.d: The Std TreeCollapseDocument command switches the Tree View DocumentMode to CollapseDocument. In this mode activating a document’s 3D View will automatically expand that document in the Tree View and collapse all other documents. The other modes are SingleDocument and MultiDocument.

Std_TreeDrag.d: The Std TreeDrag command initiates a drag operation for selected objects in the Tree View. This command is useful when the objects you want to drag and drop and the target container are not visible at the same time in the Tree View.
u: Select one or more objects.
If required scroll the Tree View to reveal the target container.
Left-click the target container.
Std_TreeDrag.m: View → Tree View Actions → Initiate Dragging

Std_TreeMultiDocument.d: The Std TreeMultiDocument command switches the Tree View DocumentMode to MultiDocument. In this mode all documents are visible in the Tree View and multiple documents can be expanded. The other modes are SingleDocument and CollapseDocument.
Std_TreeMultiDocument.m: View → Tree View Actions → Multi Document

Std_TreePreSelection.d: The Std TreePreSelection command toggles the Tree View PreSelection mode. If this mode is on, an object that the mouse is over in the Tree View will be pre-selectected (temporarily highlighted) in all 3D Views belonging to that object's document.

Std_TreeRecordSelection.d: The Std TreeRecordSelection command toggles the Tree View RecordSelection mode. If this mode is on, each Tree View selection is stored for future use. With the and buttons you can go backwards and forwards through these selections and restore them.
Std_TreeRecordSelection.m: View → Tree View Actions → Record Selection

Std_TreeSelectAllInstances.d: The Std TreeSelectAllInstances command expands the Tree View to reveal all instances of the same object and selects them.
u: Select an object.
Select the Select All Instances option from the Tree View context menu.

Std_TreeSelection.d:
The Std TreeSelection command scrolls the Tree View to the first created object in a 3D View selection.

If the Tree View SyncSelection mode is off, the Tree View is scrolled to the first created object in the selection whose parent is already expanded in the Tree View. If none of the objects' parents are expanded the command will have no effect in that mode.
u: Select one or more objects in a 3D View.
Std_TreeSelection.m: View → Tree View Actions → Go to Selection

Std_TreeSingleDocument.d:
The Std TreeSingleDocument command switches the Tree View DocumentMode to SingleDocument. In this mode only a single document is visible in the Tree View. The other modes are MultiDocument and CollapseDocument.

In SingleDocument mode you can switch to a different document by activating a 3D View belonging to that document. You can do this in the Main View Area or via the Windows menu.
Std_TreeSingleDocument.m: View → Tree View Actions → Single Document

Std_TreeSyncPlacement.d: The Std TreeSyncPlacement command toggles the Tree View SyncPlacement mode. If this mode is on, the DataPlacement of objects is automatically adjusted when they are dragged and dropped from one container into another container with a different coordinate system, preserving their placement relative to the global coordinate system.
Std_TreeSyncPlacement.m: View → Tree View Actions → Sync Placement

Std_TreeSyncSelection.d: The Std TreeSyncSelection command toggles the Tree View SyncSelection mode. If this mode is on, selecting an object in a 3D View will automatically expand the Tree View to show that object.
Std_TreeSyncSelection.m: View → Tree View Actions → Sync Selection

Std_TreeSyncView.d: The Std TreeSyncView command toggles the Tree View SyncView mode. If this mode is on, selecting an object from a different document in the Tree View automatically activates that document’s last used docked 3D View.
Std_TreeSyncView.m: View → Tree View Actions → Sync View

Std_Undo.d: The Std Undo command undoes the last action.

Std_UnitsCalculator.d: The Std UnitsCalculator command opens the Units Converter. The Units Converter can be used to convert values from one unit system to another.
u: The Units Converter dialog box opens. For more information see Options.
The dialog box is modeless, meaning it can stay open while you continue working in FreeCAD.

Std_UserEditMode.d: The Std UserEditMode command defines the edit mode to be used when an object is double-clicked in the Tree View.
u: In the menu go to Edit → Edit Mode and select an edit mode.

Std_VarSet.d: The Std VarSet command creates a VarSet. A VarSet is a set of properties that can be used as variables in expressions.
u: Do one of the following:
The Add Property dialog box opens.
Enter a Name for the property.
Enter a Group name for the property or select a group from the list. Group names have the same restrictions as property names.
Select the property Type from the list. See below for the most common types.
Enter a Value for the property. This input accepts units for properties that have units. You can also specify an expression.

Std_ViewBottom.d: The Std ViewBottom command points the camera in the active 3D View in the direction of the positive Z-axis.

Std_ViewBoxZoom.d: The Std ViewBoxZoom command zooms in on a user defined rectangular area, a box, in the active 3D View.
u: Drag a rectangle in the 3D View.

Std_ViewCreate.d: The Std ViewCreate command creates a new 3D View for the active document. Additional 3D Views can be useful if you want to inspect the model from multiple directions or at different zoom levels.

Std_ViewDimetric.d: The Std ViewDimetric command realigns the camera in the active 3D View to obtain a dimetric view. For a truly dimetric view the 3D View must be in orthographic mode, but the command also works if the view is in perspective mode.

Std_ViewDockUndockFullscreen.d:
The Docked menu option docks the active 3D View inside the main FreeCAD interface.

  • Activate an undocked 3D View.
  • There are several ways to invoke the option:
u: Activate an undocked 3D View.

Std_ViewFitAll.d: The Std ViewFitAll command zooms and pans the camera so that all visible objects fit inside the active 3D View.

Std_ViewFitSelection.d: The Std ViewFitSelection command zooms and pans the camera so that all selected objects fit inside the active 3D View. This command is useful if for some reason objects are beyond the boundaries of the current 3D View or can't easily be found using 3D navigation.
u: Select one or more objects.

Std_ViewFront.d: The Std ViewFront command points the camera in the active 3D View in the direction of the positive Y-axis.

Std_ViewFullscreen.d: The Std ViewFullscreen command switches 3D Views to and from fullscreen mode. 3D Views are automatically undocked for fullscreen mode.
u: Activate the correct 3D View.

Std_ViewHome.d: The Std ViewHome command changes the camera in the active 3D View to the default camera orientation. And zooms and pans the camera so that all visible objects fit inside the view.

Std_ViewIsometric.d: The Std ViewIsometric command realigns the camera in the active 3D View to obtain an isometric view. For a truly isometric view the 3D View must be in orthographic mode, but the command also works if the view is in perspective mode.

Std_ViewIvIssueCamPos.d: The Std ViewIvIssueCamPos command prints the camera settings of the active 3D View in the Report View and the Python Console.

Std_ViewIvStereoInterleavedColumns.d: The Std ViewIvStereoInterleavedColumns command changes the active 3D View to interleaved columns stereo view mode. To use this stereo mode a special graphics card, a special display and glasses with polarized lenses are requires.

Std_ViewIvStereoInterleavedRows.d: The Std ViewIvStereoInterleavedRows command changes the active 3D View to interleaved rows stereo view mode. To use this stereo mode a special graphics card, a special display and glasses with polarized lenses are requires.

Std_ViewIvStereoOff.d: The Std ViewIvStereoOff command switches off stereo view mode in the active 3D View.

Std_ViewIvStereoQuadBuff.d: The Std ViewIvStereoQuadBuff command changes the active 3D View to quad buffer stereo view mode. To use this stereo mode a special graphics card, a special display and shutter glasses are requires.

Std_ViewIvStereoRedGreen.d: The Std ViewIvStereoRedGreen command changes the active 3D View to red/cyan, anaglyph, stereo view mode. To use this stereo mode glasses with colored lenses are required.

Std_ViewLeft.d: The Std ViewLeft command points the camera in the active 3D View in the direction of the positive X-axis.

Std_ViewLoadImage.d: The Std ViewLoadImage command opens an image in a new tab in the Main View Area.
u: Optionally select the correct file type in the dialog box.
Select a file.
The image opens in a new tab.
Optionally right-click in the tab and select Fit to Window, Zoom In or Zoom Out.
To pan an image that is larger than the tab either use the scrollbars, or hold down the middle mouse button and move the cursor.
Close the tab when done.

Std_ViewRear.d: The Std ViewRear command points the camera in the active 3D View in the direction of the negative Y-axis.

Std_ViewRight.d: The Std ViewRight command points the camera in the active 3D View in the direction of the negative X-axis.

Std_ViewRotateLeft.d: The Std ViewRotateLeft command rotates the camera in the active 3D View around the view direction in 90-degree increments towards the left (counterclockwise).

Std_ViewRotateRight.d: The Std ViewRotateRight command rotates the camera in the active 3D View around the view direction in 90-degree increments towards the right (clockwise).

Std_ViewScreenShot.d: The Std ViewScreenShot command opens a dialog box to create an image file, a screenshot, from the active 3D View.
u: The Save Image dialog box opens.
Optionally press the Extended button to reveal an additional panel in the dialog box. For more information see Options.
Optionally browse to the correct folder.
Enter a filename and select the file type.

Std_ViewStatusBar.d: The Std ViewStatusBar command toggles the display of the Status Bar.

Std_ViewTop.d: The Std ViewTop command points the camera in the active 3D View in the direction of the negative Z-axis.

Std_ViewTrimetric.d: The Std ViewTrimetric command realigns the camera in the active 3D View to obtain a trimetric view. For a truly trimetric view the 3D View must be in orthographic mode, but the command also works if the view is in perspective mode.

Std_ViewZoomIn.d: The Std ViewZoomIn command zooms in in the active 3D View.

Std_ViewZoomOut.d: The Std ViewZoomOut command zooms out in the active 3D View.

Std_WhatsThis.d: The Std WhatsThis command opens the help documentation for a specific command.
u: Click a toolbar button or a menu option.
The help documentation for the selected command opens.

Std_Windows.d: The Std Windows command opens a dialog box with a list of Main View Area windows. From this list a selected window can be activated.
u: The Choose Window dialog box opens.
Do one of the following:
The dialog box closes.
The selected window is activated.

Std_Workbench.d: The Std Workbench command activates a selected workbench.

Surface_BlendCurve.d:
The Surface BlendCurve tool creates a Bezier curve between two edges, with desired continuity.

The base geometry can belong to curves created with the Draft Workbench or the Sketcher Workbench, but can also belong to solid objects such as those created with the Part Workbench.
u: Select two edges in the 3D View
Adjust the curve shape in the object's Data properties or (v1.1): double-click on the object and use the task panel.

Surface_CurveOnMesh.d:
The Surface CurveOnMesh tool creates approximated spline segments on top of a selected mesh.

If the object is not a Mesh, but a parametric shape or surface, it must first be converted into a mesh using Mesh FromPartShape.

These edges created on top of the mesh may be further used to re-create the surface in a parametric way by using tools such as Surface GeomFillSurface and Surface Sections.
u: Select a mesh object.
Press Start.
Using the mouse pointer, pick points on the surface of the mesh in the 3D View; pick as many points as necessary to draw a smooth preview line.

When enough points have been added, right click on the 3D View to open the context menu, and select Create. Depending on how smooth the original mesh is, one spline or multiple splines will be created in the Tree View.
Repeat the sequence Start → Pick → Create, to add more approximated splines.
The new spline will be created, and will appear in the Tree View, immediately after choosing Create; the task panel will remain active.

Surface_ExtendFace.d: The Surface ExtendFace tool extrapolates an existing face or surface at its boundaries with its local U and V parameters.
u: Make sure you have an object that has faces. The object could be created with the Surface Workbench but it could also be any other object, for example, created with Part or PartDesign.
Select the face to extend by clicking on it on the 3D View.

Surface_Filling.d:
The Surface Filling tool creates a surface from a series of connected boundary edges. The curvature of the surface can be additionally controlled by non-boundary edges and vertices, and a support surface.

The base geometry can belong to curves created with the Draft Workbench or the Sketcher Workbench, but can also belong to solid objects such as those created with the Part Workbench or the PartDesign Workbench.
u: The Boundaries task panel opens. See Options.
Select two or more edges in the 3D View:
A preview of the final shape will be shown once enough valid geometry has been selected.
Optionally select a Support Surface. See Example.
Optionally select one or more Edge Constraints.
Optionally select one or more Vertex Constraints.

Surface_GeomFillSurface.d: The Surface GeomFillSurface tool creates a parametric surface from two, three, or four boundary edges, trying to create a smooth transition between them.
u: Select edges in the 3D View. The edges must be connected and form a closed boundary.
Press OK.

Surface_Sections.d: The Surface Sections tool creates a surface from a series of sectional edges.
u: Make sure you have at least two edges or curves in space. For example, these can be created with tools of the Draft Workbench or the Sketcher Workbench.
Press Add Edge.
Use the pointer to pick the desired edges in the 3D View; a preview of the final shape will be shown after selecting two valid edges.
Press OK to complete the operation.

TechDraw_2LineCenterLine.d: The TechDraw 2LineCenterLine tool adds a centerline between two edges.
TechDraw_2LineCenterLine.m: TechDraw → Add Lines → Centerline Between 2 Lines

TechDraw_2PointCenterLine.d: The TechDraw 2PointCenterLine tool adds a centerline between two points.
TechDraw_2PointCenterLine.m: TechDraw → Add Lines → Centerline Between 2 Points

TechDraw_2PointCosmeticLine.d: The TechDraw 2PointCosmeticLine tool adds a cosmetic line between two points. The points can be 2D or 3D. The resulting line can be used for dimensioning.
TechDraw_2PointCosmeticLine.m: TechDraw → Add Lines → Cosmetic Line Through 2 points

TechDraw_3PtAngleDimension.d: The TechDraw 3PtAngleDimension tool adds an angular dimension to a View. The dimension shows the interior angle between three points.
u: Select three points. The second point will be the apex of the angle. The geometry may be selected in the 3D View or in the drawing.
If you have selected geometry in the 3D View: add the correct TechDraw View to the selection by selecting it in the Tree View.
A dimension is added to the View.
The dimension may be dragged to the desired position.
If needed, add tolerances as described on this page.
TechDraw_3PtAngleDimension.m: TechDraw → Dimensions → Angle Dimension From 3 Points

TechDraw_ActiveView.d: The TechDraw ActiveView tool inserts a bitmap image of the active 3D View into a drawing page.
u: Navigate to the correct 3D View.
If there are multiple drawing pages in the document: optionally select the desired page in the Tree View.
If there are multiple drawing pages in the document and you have not yet selected a page, the Page Chooser dialog box opens:
The Insert Active View task panel opens. See Options for more information.
TechDraw_ActiveView.m: TechDraw → Views From Other Workbenches → Active View

TechDraw_AngleDimension.d: The TechDraw AngleDimension tool adds an angular dimension to a View. The dimension shows the interior angle between two straight edges.
u: Select two straight edges. The geometry may be selected in the 3D View or in the drawing.
If you have selected geometry in the 3D View: add the correct TechDraw View to the selection by selecting it in the Tree View.
A dimension is added to the View.
The dimension may be dragged to the desired position.
If needed, add tolerances as described on this page.

TechDraw_Annotation.d: The TechDraw Annotation tool adds a text block to a drawing page.
u: If there are multiple drawing pages in the document: optionally activate the desired page by selecting it in the Tree View.
If there are multiple drawing pages in the document and you have not yet activated a page, the Page Chooser dialog box opens:
A text block containing Default Text appears on the page.
Use the Property View to change the text.
Optionally drag the Annotation to the different position.

TechDraw_ArchView.d:
The TechDraw ArchView tool inserts a BIM View object (formerly known as an Arch View object 0.21 and below), a view of an Arch SectionPlane, on a TechDraw page.

(v1.0): The TechDraw View tool can also create a BIM View.
u: Select an Arch section plane in the 3D View or Tree View.
If there are multiple drawing pages in the document: optionally add the desired page to the selection by selecting it in the Tree View.
If there are multiple drawing pages in the document, and if no page is displayed in the Main View Area and you have not yet selected a page, the Page Chooser dialog box opens:
TechDraw_ArchView.m: TechDraw → Views From Other Workbenches → BIM View

TechDraw_AreaDimension.d: The TechDraw AreaDimension tool adds an area dimension to a face in a Part View.
u: Select a face. The geometry may be selected in the 3D View or in the drawing.
If you have selected geometry in the 3D View: add the correct TechDraw View to the selection by selecting it in the Tree View.
A dimension is added to the view.
The dimension may be dragged to the desired position.
If needed, add tolerances as described on this page.

TechDraw_AxoLengthDimension.d: The TechDraw AxoLengthDimension tool adds a length dimension to an axonometric view. The dimension may be the length of an edge or the distance between two points.
u: Do one of the following:
An axonometric dimension is added to the View.
The dimension may be dragged to the desired position.
If needed, add tolerances as described on this page.

TechDraw_Balloon.d: The TechDraw Balloon tool can add balloons with leader line in a drawing.
u: Select one of the following:
If a View or a region was selected:

TechDraw_BrokenView.d: The TechDraw BrokenView tool inserts a "broken view" that is either based on an existing Part View, or one or more objects, such as Bodies or Parts. The broken view also requires one or more sketches that define the location and size of the areas to be removed, and also the length of the breaking lines. The BrokenView behaves similarly to other Views. The projection direction is taken from the existing Part View, the 3D camera direction or the normal of a selected face.
u: Optionally rotate the 3D View. The 3D View determines the initial values of the DataDirection and DataXDirection properties of the broken view.
Select the object you want to create a broken view of, or select an existing TechDraw view that contains this object.
Add one or more break sketches to the selection by selecting them in the Tree View. Each sketch should only contain two parallel lines. You can also use other objects with two parallel edges.

TechDraw_ClipGroup.d: The TechDraw ClipGroup tool creates a clipping window which can contain Views.
u: If there are multiple drawing pages in the document: optionally activate the desired page by selecting it in the Tree View.
If there are multiple drawing pages in the document and you have not yet activated a page, the Page Chooser dialog box opens:
Views can be dragged and dropped to and from the Clip Group in the Tree View. (v1.0)

TechDraw_ClipGroupAdd.d: The TechDraw ClipGroupAdd tool adds a View to an existing Clip.
u: Select a Clip and a View in the 3D view or Tree view.
TechDraw_ClipGroupAdd.m: TechDraw → Clipped Views → Add View to Clip Group

TechDraw_ClipGroupRemove.d: The TechDraw ClipGroupRemove tool removes a View from an existing Clip and returns it to the Page area.
u: Select a View that is part of a Clip in the 3D view or Tree view.
TechDraw_ClipGroupRemove.m: TechDraw → Clipped Views → Remove View from Clip Group

TechDraw_CommandAddOffsetVertex.d: The TechDraw CommandAddOffsetVertex tool adds a cosmetic vertex at a specified offset from a selected vertex.
u: Select a vertex.
A task panel opens.
Enter the desired (positive or negative) X-offset and Y-offset in mm.
A cosmetic vertex is added.

TechDraw_ComplexSection.d: The TechDraw ComplexSection tool inserts a cross-section view based on an existing Part View and a profile.
u: Select a Part View and a profile object in the 3D View or Tree View. Profiles are typically sketches, but any object whose shape can be made into a wire will work.
A task panel opens which will help calculate the various properties. Reasonable values for the view Direction are calculated, but these can be changed.
TechDraw_ComplexSection.m: TechDraw → TechDraw Views → Complex Section View

TechDraw_CosmeticCircle.d: The TechDraw CosmeticCircle tool adds a cosmetic circle at a selected center point. The point can be 2D or 3D.

TechDraw_CosmeticEraser.d: The TechDraw CosmeticEraser tool removes cosmetic objects. Cosmetic objects include cosmetic vertices, cosmetic lines and centerlines.
u: Select one or more cosmetic objects on a page.

TechDraw_CosmeticVertex.d: The TechDraw CosmeticVertex tool adds a vertex, which is not part of the source geometry, to a view. This vertex behaves like any other vertex and can be used for dimensioning.
u: Select a view.
A task panel opens.
Optionally press the Point Picker button and pick a point on the page. Press the Escape Picking button to cancel this operation.
Optionally change or specify the X- and Y-coordinates of the point. The coordinates are relative to the center of the view.

TechDraw_DecorateLine.d: The TechDraw DecorateLine tool changes the appearance of edges, including cosmetic lines and centerlines. It can also make edges invisible.
u: Select a View or one or more edges in a View.
A task panel opens.
If you have selected edges: optionally change their Style, Color, Weight and/or Visible properties in the Line Decoration section.
To make invisible edges in the View permanently visible again: optionally press one or more of the buttons in the Restore Invisible Lines section:
TechDraw_DecorateLine.m: TechDraw → Add Lines → Edit Line Appearance

TechDraw_DetailView.d: The TechDraw DetailView tool creates a view of a small area of an existing view.
u: Select a base view for the detail view.
A highlight outline is added to the base view, a detail view is added to the page, and a task panel opens.
For clarity it is best to move the detail view so that it no longer overlaps the base view: hold down the left mouse button on its frame or label and drag it to a new position.
To change the position of the highlight outline do one of the following:
Optionally change the Radius of the detail view.
Optionally change the Scale type and Scale factor of the detail view. See TechDraw View for more information.

TechDraw_DiameterDimension.d:
The TechDraw DiameterDimension tool adds a diameter dimension to a View. The dimension may be applied to any edge which is a circle or circular arc.

For more information see TechDraw RadiusDimension.

TechDraw_Dimension.d: The TechDraw Dimension tool is the TechDraw equivalent of the Sketcher Dimension tool. It offers contextual dimensioning and thus can replace most of the other dimension tools.
u: Optionally preselect some geometric elements (vertices, edges or faces).
The cursor changes to a cross with the tool icon.
If you have not yet selected an element: select one.
Depending on the selected element(s) a dimension is proposed.
Optionally select an additional element.
The proposed dimension is updated.

TechDraw_DimensionRepair.d:
The TechDraw DimensionRepair tool can adjust the 2D or 3D geometry references of a dimension. These references may become incorrect due to the "topological naming problem" or Hidden Line Removal.

See TechDraw LengthDimension for more on dimensions and the topological naming problem.
u: Select the dimension to be corrected and, optionally, the new geometry references, points or edges, in the TechDraw View or in the 3D View.
The Dimension Repair task panel opens showing the selected dimension and the current geometry references.
Select new geometry references if you have not done so already.
If 3D references have been selected: optionally change the DataMeasure Type property of the dimension to True.

TechDraw_DraftView.d: The TechDraw DraftView tool inserts a view of a selected Part-based or Group object into a drawing page. Unlike the standard View tool, views created with this tool are handled by the Draft Workbench, and specially designed for showing 2D objects. See Notes.
u: Optionally rotate the 3D View. The camera direction in the 3D View determines the initial value of the DataDirection property of the View.
Select one or more objects in the 3D View or Tree View. A separate view will created for each object.
If there are multiple drawing pages in the document: optionally add the desired page to the selection by selecting it in the Tree View.
If there are multiple drawing pages in the document and you have not yet selected a page, the Page Chooser dialog box opens:
TechDraw_DraftView.m: TechDraw → Views From Other Workbenches → Draft View

TechDraw_ExportPageDXF.d: The TechDraw ExportPageDXF tool saves a drawing page as a DXF file.
u: If there are multiple drawing pages in the document: optionally activate the desired page by selecting it in the Tree View.
If there are multiple drawing pages in the document and you have not yet activated a page, the Page Chooser dialog box opens:
The Save DXF file dialog box opens.
Select a location and file name.
TechDraw_ExportPageDXF.m: TechDraw → Page → Export Page as DXF

TechDraw_ExportPageSVG.d: The TechDraw ExportPageSVG tool saves the current drawing page as an SVG file.
u: If there are multiple drawing pages in the document: optionally activate the desired page by selecting it in the Tree View.
If there are multiple drawing pages in the document and you have not yet activated a page, the Page Chooser dialog box opens:
The Export page as SVG dialog box opens.
Select a location and file name.
TechDraw_ExportPageSVG.m: TechDraw → Page → Export Page as SVG

TechDraw_ExtensionArcLengthAnnotation.d: The TechDraw ExtensionArcLengthAnnotation tool calculates the arc length of selected edges and inserts an arc length annotation.
u: Select one or more edges.
The total arc length of the edges is calculated and an annotation is inserted.

TechDraw_ExtensionAreaAnnotation.d: The TechDraw ExtensionAreaAnnotation tool calculates the area of selected faces and inserts an area annotation.
u: Select one or more faces.
The total area of the faces is calculated and an area annotation is inserted.

TechDraw_ExtensionCascadeHorizDimension.d: The TechDraw ExtensionCascadeHorizDimension tool evenly spaces horizontal dimensions.
u: Optionally specify the cascade spacing with the TechDraw ExtensionSelectLineAttributes tool.
Select two or more horizontal dimensions.
