The first dimension defines the position. This dimension will not be moved, the other dimensions will be positioned relative to this dimension.
The dimensions are evenly spaced and their dimension texts are centered.

TechDraw_ExtensionCascadeObliqueDimensio.d: The TechDraw ExtensionCascadeObliqueDimension tool evenly spaces oblique dimensions.
u: Optionally specify the cascade spacing with the TechDraw ExtensionSelectLineAttributes tool.
Select two or more parallel oblique dimensions.
The first dimension defines the position. This dimension will not be moved, the other dimensions will be positioned relative to this dimension.
The dimensions are evenly spaced.

TechDraw_ExtensionCascadeVertDimension.d: The TechDraw ExtensionCascadeVertDimension tool evenly spaces vertical dimensions.
u: Optionally specify the cascade spacing with the TechDraw ExtensionSelectLineAttributes tool.
Select two or more vertical dimensions.
The first dimension defines the position. This dimension will not be moved, the other dimensions will be positioned relative to this dimension.
The dimensions are evenly spaced and their dimension texts are centered.

TechDraw_ExtensionChangeLineAttributes.d: The TechDraw ExtensionChangeLineAttributes tool changes the attributes (style, width and color) of cosmetic lines and centerlines.
u: Optionally specify the line attributes with the TechDraw ExtensionSelectLineAttributes tool.
Select one or more cosmetic lines and/or centerlines.
The attributes of the selected lines are updated.

TechDraw_ExtensionCircleCenterLines.d: The TechDraw ExtensionCircleCenterLines tool adds centerlines to circles and arcs.
u: Optionally specify the line attributes with the TechDraw ExtensionSelectLineAttributes tool.
Select one or more circles or arcs.
Centerlines are added to each circle and arc.

TechDraw_ExtensionCreateHorizChainDimens.d: The TechDraw ExtensionCreateHorizChainDimension tool creates a horizontal chain dimension: a sequence of aligned dimensions.
u: Select three or more vertices.
The two leftmost vertices determine the position of the chain dimension.
A chain dimension with centered dimension texts is created.
TechDraw_ExtensionCreateHorizChainDimens.m: TechDraw → Format/Organize Dimensions → Horizontal Chain Dimension

TechDraw_ExtensionCreateHorizChamferDime.d: The TechDraw ExtensionCreateHorizChamferDimension tool creates a horizontal size and angle dimension for a chamfer.
u: Select two vertices.
A chamfer dimension is created.
TechDraw_ExtensionCreateHorizChamferDime.m: TechDraw → Format/Organize Dimensions → Horizontal Chamfer Dimension

TechDraw_ExtensionCreateHorizCoordDimens.d: The TechDraw ExtensionCreateHorizCoordDimension tool creates horizontal coordinate dimensions: multiple evenly spaced dimensions starting from the same baseline.
u: Optionally specify the cascade spacing with the TechDraw ExtensionSelectLineAttributes tool.
Select three or more vertices.

The selection order of the first two vertices determines the position of the baseline. If the vertex that is selected first is to the left of the second, the baseline is created at the leftmost vertex, else it is created at…
Coordinate dimensions with centered dimension texts are created.
TechDraw_ExtensionCreateHorizCoordDimens.m: TechDraw → Format/Organize Dimensions → Horizontal Coordinate Dimension

TechDraw_ExtensionCreateLengthArc.d: The TechDraw ExtensionCreateLengthArc tool creates an arc length dimension.
u: Select a single circular arc.
An arc length dimension is created.
TechDraw_ExtensionCreateLengthArc.m: TechDraw → Format/Organize Dimensions → Arc Length Dimension

TechDraw_ExtensionCreateObliqueChainDime.d: The TechDraw ExtensionCreateObliqueChainDimension tool creates an oblique chain dimension: a sequence of aligned dimensions.
u: Select three or more vertices.
The two vertices selected first define the direction and determine the position of the chain dimension.
A chain dimension with centered dimension texts is created.
TechDraw_ExtensionCreateObliqueChainDime.m: TechDraw → Format/Organize Dimensions → Oblique Chain Dimension

TechDraw_ExtensionCreateObliqueCoordDime.d: The TechDraw ExtensionCreateObliqueCoordDimension tool creates oblique coordinate dimensions: multiple evenly spaced dimensions starting from the same baseline.
u: Optionally specify the cascade spacing with the TechDraw ExtensionSelectLineAttributes tool.
Select three or more vertices.

The selection order of the first two vertices determines the position of the baseline. If the vertex that is selected first is to the left of the second, the baseline is created at the leftmost vertex, else it is created at…
The first two vertices also define the direction.
Coordinate dimensions with centered dimension texts are created.
TechDraw_ExtensionCreateObliqueCoordDime.m: TechDraw → Format/Organize Dimensions → Oblique Coordinate Dimension

TechDraw_ExtensionCreateVertChainDimensi.d: The TechDraw ExtensionCreateVertChainDimension tool creates a vertical chain dimension: a sequence of aligned dimensions.
u: Select three or more vertices.
The two highest vertices determine the position of the chain dimension.
A chain dimension with centered dimension texts is created.
TechDraw_ExtensionCreateVertChainDimensi.m: TechDraw → Format/Organize Dimensions → Vertical Chain Dimension

TechDraw_ExtensionCreateVertChamferDimen.d: The TechDraw ExtensionCreateVertChamferDimension tool creates a vertical size and angle dimension for a chamfer.
u: Select two vertices.
A chamfer dimension is created.
TechDraw_ExtensionCreateVertChamferDimen.m: TechDraw → Format/Organize Dimensions → Vertical Chamfer Dimension

TechDraw_ExtensionCreateVertCoordDimensi.d: The TechDraw ExtensionCreateVertCoordDimension tool creates vertical coordinate dimensions: multiple evenly spaced dimensions starting from the same baseline.
u: Optionally specify the cascade spacing with the TechDraw ExtensionSelectLineAttributes tool.
Select three or more vertices.

The selection order of the first two vertices determines the position of the baseline. If the vertex that is selected first is below the second, the baseline is created at the lowest vertex, else it is created at the highest…
Coordinate dimensions with centered dimension texts are created.
TechDraw_ExtensionCreateVertCoordDimensi.m: TechDraw → Format/Organize Dimensions → Vertical Coordinate Dimension

TechDraw_ExtensionCustomizeFormat.d: The TechDraw ExtensionCustomizeFormat tool customizes the formatting of a balloon text or dimension text. GD&T symbols and other special characters can be added.
u: Select a Balloon object or a Dimension object.
The Customize Format task panel opens.
Edit the Format field using the available task panel buttons and/or the keyboard.
The Preview field shows the result of the current formatting.

TechDraw_ExtensionDecreaseDecimal.d: The TechDraw ExtensionDecreaseDecimal tool decreases the number of decimal places of the dimension text.
u: Select one or more dimensions.
The number of decimal places of the selected dimensions is decreased by one.
TechDraw_ExtensionDecreaseDecimal.m: TechDraw → Format/Organize Dimensions → Decrease Decimal Places

TechDraw_ExtensionDrawCosmArc.d: The TechDraw ExtensionDrawCosmArc tool adds a cosmetic counter clockwise arc based on three vertices.
u: Optionally specify the line attributes with the TechDraw ExtensionSelectLineAttributes tool.
Select the first vertex to determine the center point of the arc.
Select the second vertex to determine the radius and the start angle of the arc.
Select the third vertex to determine the end angle of the arc.
A cosmetic arc is added.

TechDraw_ExtensionDrawCosmCircle.d: The TechDraw ExtensionDrawCosmCircle tool adds a cosmetic circle based on two vertices.
u: Optionally specify the line attributes with the TechDraw ExtensionSelectLineAttributes tool.
Select the first vertex to determine the center point of the circle.
Select the second vertex to determine the radius of the circle.
A cosmetic circle is added.

TechDraw_ExtensionDrawCosmCircle3Points.d: The TechDraw ExtensionDrawCosmCircle3Points tool adds a cosmetic circle based on three vertices.
u: Optionally specify the line attributes with the TechDraw ExtensionSelectLineAttributes tool.
Select three vertices on the circumference to determine the circle.
A cosmetic circle is added.

TechDraw_ExtensionExtendLine.d: The TechDraw ExtensionExtendLine tool extends a cosmetic line or centerline at both ends.
u: Optionally specify the delta distance with the TechDraw ExtensionSelectLineAttributes tool.
Select a single cosmetic line or centerline.
The line is extended at both ends.

TechDraw_ExtensionHoleCircle.d: The TechDraw ExtensionHoleCircle tool adds centerlines to a circular pattern of circles.
u: Optionally specify the line attributes with the TechDraw ExtensionSelectLineAttributes tool.
Select three or more circles forming a circular pattern.
The centerlines are added.

TechDraw_ExtensionIncreaseDecimal.d: The TechDraw ExtensionIncreaseDecimal tool increases the number of decimal places of the dimension text.
u: Select one or more dimensions.
The number of decimal places of the selected dimensions is increased by one.
TechDraw_ExtensionIncreaseDecimal.m: TechDraw → Format/Organize Dimensions → Increase Decimal Places

TechDraw_ExtensionInsertDiameter.d: The TechDraw ExtensionInsertDiameter tool inserts a '⌀' symbol at the beginning of the dimension text.
u: Select one or more dimensions.
The '⌀' symbol is inserted in the dimension text of the selected dimensions.

TechDraw_ExtensionInsertRepetition.d: The TechDraw ExtensionInsertRepetition tool inserts a repeated feature count at the beginning of the dimension text.
u: Select one or more dimensions.
The Change Editable Field dialog opens.
The Autofill checkbox has no purpose for this tool.
Enter the Value that should appear before the '×' symbol.
Press Enter or press the OK button.
The entered value and the '×' symbol are inserted in the dimension text of the selected dimensions.

TechDraw_ExtensionInsertSquare.d: The TechDraw ExtensionInsertSquare tool inserts a '□' symbol at the beginning of the dimension text.
u: Select one or more dimensions.
The '□' symbol is inserted in the dimension text of the selected dimensions.

TechDraw_ExtensionLineParallel.d: The TechDraw ExtensionLineParallel tool adds a cosmetic line parallel to another line through a vertex.
u: Optionally specify the line attributes with the TechDraw ExtensionSelectLineAttributes tool.
Select a straight edge to determine the direction and the length of the line.
Select a vertex to determine the position of the line.
A cosmetic line is added.

TechDraw_ExtensionLinePerpendicular.d: The TechDraw ExtensionLinePerpendicular tool adds a cosmetic line perpendicular to another line through a vertex.
u: Optionally specify the line attributes with the TechDraw ExtensionSelectLineAttributes tool.
Select a straight edge to determine the direction and the length of the line.
Select a vertex to determine the position of the line.
A cosmetic line is added.

TechDraw_ExtensionLockUnlockView.d: The TechDraw ExtensionLockUnlockView tool locks or unlocks the position of a view by toggling its DataLock Position property. A locked view has a fixed position relative to the page or the group it belongs to.
u: Select a single drawing view.
The DataLock Position property of the view is toggled. Locked views have a red padlock icon in the lower left corner.

TechDraw_ExtensionPosHorizChainDimension.d: The TechDraw ExtensionPosHorizChainDimension tool aligns horizontal dimensions to create a chain dimension.
u: Select two or more horizontal dimensions.
The first dimension defines the position. This dimension will not be moved.
The dimensions are aligned and their dimension texts are centered.
TechDraw_ExtensionPosHorizChainDimension.m: TechDraw → Attributes/Modifications → Align Horizontal Chain Dimensions

TechDraw_ExtensionPosObliqueChainDimensi.d: The TechDraw ExtensionPosObliqueChainDimension tool aligns oblique dimensions to create a chain dimension.
u: Select two or more parallel oblique dimensions.
The first dimension defines the position. This dimension will not be moved.
The dimensions are aligned.
TechDraw_ExtensionPosObliqueChainDimensi.m: TechDraw → Attributes/Modifications → Align Oblique Chain Dimensions

TechDraw_ExtensionPosVertChainDimension.d: The TechDraw ExtensionPosVertChainDimension tool aligns vertical dimensions to create a chain dimension.
u: Select two or more vertical dimensions.
The first dimension defines the position. This dimension will not be moved.
The dimensions are aligned and their dimension texts are centered.
TechDraw_ExtensionPosVertChainDimension.m: TechDraw → Attributes/Modifications → Align Vertical Chain Dimensions

TechDraw_ExtensionPositionSectionView.d: The TechDraw ExtensionPositionSectionView tool orthogonally aligns a section view with its source view. You can select a section view or ((v1.0)) select an edge and a vertex.

TechDraw_ExtensionRemovePrefixChar.d: The TechDraw ExtensionRemovePrefixChar tool removes all prefix symbols from the dimension text.
u: Select one or more dimensions.
All prefix symbols are removed from the dimension text of the selected dimensions.

TechDraw_ExtensionSelectLineAttributes.d: The TechDraw ExtensionSelectLineAttributes tool opens a task panel where you can select the attributes (style, width and color) for new cosmetic lines and centerlines created with the Extensions tools, and specify the cascade spacing and delta distance. The line attributes are also used by the TechDraw ExtensionChangeLineAttributes tool.
u: The Select Line Attributes task panel opens.
Optionally change the Line style, the Line width and the Line color.
Optionally change the Cascade spacing. The Cascade Dimension tools and the Coordinate Dimension tools use this value.
Optionally change the Delta distance. The TechDraw ExtensionExtendLine tool and TechDraw ExtensionShortenLine tool use this value.
TechDraw_ExtensionSelectLineAttributes.m: TechDraw → Attributes/Modifications → Select Line Attributes, Cascade Spacing and Delta Distance

TechDraw_ExtensionShortenLine.d: The TechDraw ExtensionShortenLine tool shortens a cosmetic line or centerline at both ends.
u: Optionally specify the delta distance with the TechDraw ExtensionSelectLineAttributes tool.
Select a single cosmetic line or centerline.
The line is shortened at both ends.

TechDraw_ExtensionThreadBoltBottom.d: The TechDraw ExtensionThreadBoltBottom tool adds a cosmetic thread to the top or bottom view of bolts/screws/rods.
u: Optionally specify the line attributes with the TechDraw ExtensionSelectLineAttributes tool.
Select one or more circles.
Cosmetic threads are added.
TechDraw_ExtensionThreadBoltBottom.m: TechDraw → Centerlines/Threading → Cosmetic Thread Bolt Bottom View

TechDraw_ExtensionThreadBoltSide.d: The TechDraw ExtensionThreadBoltSide tool adds a cosmetic thread to the side view of a bolt/screw/rod.
u: Optionally specify the line attributes with the TechDraw ExtensionSelectLineAttributes tool.
Select two parallel lines.
A cosmetic thread is added.
TechDraw_ExtensionThreadBoltSide.m: TechDraw → Centerlines/Threading → Cosmetic Thread Bolt Side View

TechDraw_ExtensionThreadHoleBottom.d: The TechDraw ExtensionThreadHoleBottom tool adds a cosmetic thread to the top or bottom view of holes.
u: Optionally specify the line attributes with the TechDraw ExtensionSelectLineAttributes tool.
Select one or more circles.
Cosmetic threads are added.
TechDraw_ExtensionThreadHoleBottom.m: TechDraw → Centerlines/Threading → Cosmetic Thread Hole Bottom View

TechDraw_ExtensionThreadHoleSide.d: The TechDraw ExtensionThreadHoleSide tool adds a cosmetic thread to the side view of a hole.
u: Optionally specify the line attributes with the TechDraw ExtensionSelectLineAttributes tool.
Select two parallel lines.
A cosmetic thread is added.
TechDraw_ExtensionThreadHoleSide.m: TechDraw → Centerlines/Threading → Cosmetic Thread Hole Side View

TechDraw_ExtensionVertexAtIntersection.d: The TechDraw ExtensionVertexAtIntersection tool adds cosmetic vertex(es) at the intersection(s) of selected edges.
u: Select two edges. Straight edges will be considered as infinite lines, and arcs will be considered as full circles.
A cosmetic vertex is added at each intersection.

TechDraw_FaceCenterLine.d: The TechDraw FaceCenterLine tool adds a centerline to selected faces.
TechDraw_FaceCenterLine.m: TechDraw → Add Lines → Centerline on Face

TechDraw_FillTemplateFields.d: The FillTemplateFields tool fills the editable text fields in the template of the current page with entries from document information.
u: Before starting the tool, create a page with the selected template and add a view.
The Fill Template Fields in Page window will appear.

Deselect the Update checkboxes next to fields that you don't want to update. You can also use the Update All checkbox to enable and disable all fields. Optionally, edit the strings shown on the right if you want to modify the…
Press Ok to update the fields or Cancel to discard the changes.

TechDraw_GeometricHatch.d: The TechDraw GeometricHatch tool fills a closed region in a view with a pattern based on an Autodesk PAT hatching specification. Alternatively the TechDraw Hatch tool uses SVG based hatch patterns. See Hatching for details.
u: Select a closed region in a view.
The Geometric Hatch task panel opens.
Optionally change the Pattern file, the Pattern name, the Pattern scale, the Line width, the Line color, the Rotation, the Offset X and the Offset Y.

TechDraw_Hatch.d: The TechDraw Hatch tool fills a closed region in a view with a tiled SVG or bitmap ((v0.21)) based hatch pattern. Alternatively the TechDraw GeometricHatch tool uses PAT based hatch patterns. See Hatching for details.
u: Select a closed region in a view.
The Create Face Hatch task panel opens.
Optionally change the Pattern file, the SVG pattern scale, the SVG line color, the Rotation, the Offset X and the Offset Y. The SVG settings are ignored for bitmap patterns.

TechDraw_HoleShaftFit.d: The TechDraw HoleShaftFit tool adds hole or shaft tolerances using ISO 286 to a linear dimension or a diameter dimension.
u: Select a single linear dimension (length, horizontal or vertical) or a single diameter dimension.
A task panel opens.
Specify shaft fit or hole fit as applicable.
Select the desired ISO 286 fit option from the combo box. The corresponding field and the fit type (loose fit, snug fit or press fit) are updated.
The selected option and the calculated tolerance values are added to the dimension.

TechDraw_HorizontalDimension.d:
The TechDraw HorizontalDimension tool adds a horizontal dimension to a View. The dimension may be the horizontal distance between two points or the horizontal length of a straight edge. As with the TechDraw LengthDimension tool it is also possible to select two edges or a point and an edge, but these options make less sense for this tool.

For more information see TechDraw LengthDimension.

TechDraw_HorizontalExtentDimension.d: The TechDraw HorizontalExtentDimension tool adds a linear dimension to a View. The dimension extends from the left most point on the selected objects to the right most point.
u: Select a View or a collection of Edges in a View.
A dimension is added to the View.
The dimension may be dragged to the desired position.
If needed, add tolerances as described on this page.

TechDraw_Image.d:
The TechDraw Image tool inserts a bitmap image (PNG, TIFF, JPEG, etc.) from a file into the page as a view.

(v1.0): The TechDraw View tool can also create an Image View.
u: If there are multiple drawing pages in the document: optionally activate the desired page by selecting it in the Tree View.
If there are multiple drawing pages in the document and you have not yet activated a page, the Page Chooser dialog box opens:
A file browser opens.
Select an image file.
An Image View is inserted.
Optionally change its DataScale property to adjust its size.

TechDraw_LandmarkDimension.d:
The TechDraw LandmarkDimension tool adds a linear dimension to a View. The dimension is based on two point objects (Draft Point, Part Point or PartDesign Point objects) from the 3D model.

The purpose of this tool is to provide a workaround to the corruption of dimensions caused by the "topological naming" issues. The source points should use Expressions or other containing mechanisms to establish their position. Since the points are Document Objects, and not shape components, their name does not change with recomputes, and hence they are easily found.
u: Select two point objects in the 3D view or Tree view.
Add the correct TechDraw View to the selection by selecting it in the Tree view.
A dimension is added to the View.
The dimension may be dragged to the desired position.
If needed, add tolerances as described on this page.
TechDraw_LandmarkDimension.m: TechDraw → Dimensions → Insert Landmark Dimension - EXPERIMENTAL

TechDraw_LeaderLine.d: The TechDraw LeaderLine tool adds a line to a View. Other annotation objects (such as Rich Text Annotations) can be connected to the leaderline to form complex annotations.

TechDraw_LengthDimension.d: The TechDraw LengthDimension tool adds a linear dimension to a View. The dimension may be the distance between two points, the length of a straight edge, the perpendicular distance between two edges, or the perpendicular distance between a point and an edge.
u: Select the points and/or edges which define your measurement. The geometry may be selected in the 3D View (first two options) or in the drawing (all options):
If you have selected geometry in the 3D View: add the correct TechDraw View to the selection by selecting it in the Tree View.
A dimension is added to the View.
The dimension may be dragged to the desired position.
If needed, add tolerances as described on this page.

TechDraw_LinkDimension.d:
The TechDraw LinkDimension tool creates a link between 3D geometry and one or more existing projected Dimensions on a Page. This link allows the Dimension to use actual 3D values instead of 2D projected values.

The Link Dimension tool's most common use is in dimensioning isometric views in a ProjectionGroup. The projected length of an Edge in an isometric view will, of course, not necessarily equal the actual length of the Edge. In an orthogonal view the projected and actual lengths will be equal.
u: Create an appropriate dimension on the drawing page using any of TechDraw LengthDimension, TechDraw HorizontalDimension, etc. This dimension will be in the right place on the Page, but will show the projected dimension value.
Select the geometry in the 3D view, for example, an edge, that corresponds to the projected geometry of your dimension.
A task panel opens.
Select one or more Dimensions to be linked to the selected 3D geometry.
Press OK.
TechDraw_LinkDimension.m: TechDraw → Dimensions → Link Dimension to 3D Geometry

TechDraw_Midpoints.d: The TechDraw Midpoints tool adds cosmetic vertices at the midpoint of one or more selected edges.
u: Select one or more edges in a view.

TechDraw_MoveView.d: The TechDraw MoveView tool moves a View and all its dependents (Balloons, Dimensions, etc) to a different Page.
u: Optionally select a View, a from Page and a to Page. The pages must be selected in that order.
A dialog will open to allow you to select a View, from Page and to Page.

TechDraw_PageDefault.d: The TechDraw PageDefault tool creates a new Page object using the the template file specified in the TechDraw Preferences.
u: An active document must exist.

TechDraw_PageTemplate.d:
The TechDraw PageTemplate tool creates a new Page object using the template file selected from a dialog.

The starting directory for the dialog can be specified in the TechDraw Preferences.
u: An active document must exist.
TechDraw_PageTemplate.m: TechDraw → Page → New Page From Template

TechDraw_PrintAll.d: The TechDraw PrintAll tool sends all pages in a document to the printer.

TechDraw_ProjectShape.d: The TechDraw ProjectShape tool creates projections of shapes. The projections are created in the 3D View, and not on a TechDraw Page.
u: Optionally rotate the 3D View. The objects will be projected onto a plane parallel to the screen i.e. along the 3D View's camera direction, which is used as the default DataDirection property.
Select one or more objects. For each object a separate projection will be created.
The Project Shapes task panel opens. See Properties.
Set the desired options.

The selected options should not result in an empty projection as this will cause an error. For example, for an object with only sharp edges such as a Part Box, the Visible sharp edges and/or Hidden sharp edges option must be…
The projection is placed on the XY-plane.

TechDraw_ProjectionGroup.d:
The TechDraw ProjectionGroup tool creates a multiview projection of one or more 3D objects, using the traditional first- or third-angle projection. The isometric views of the 4 front corners can also be included.

(v1.0): The TechDraw View tool can also create a Projection Group. It is advisable to use that tool instead.

TechDraw_Quadrants.d: The TechDraw Quadrant tool adds three cosmetic vertices along the length of one or more selected edges. The vertices are placed at 25%, 50% and 75% of the length of the edges. For a circular edge this results in cosmetic vertices at 90°, 180° and 270°, in addition to its geometric vertex at 0°.
u: Select one or more edges in a view. Any edge can be selected, not just circles.

TechDraw_RadiusDimension.d: The TechDraw RadiusDimension tool adds a radius dimension to a View. The dimension may be applied to any edge which is a circle or circular arc.
u: Select a circle or circular arc. The geometry may be selected in the 3D View or in the drawing. Note some arcs which appear to be circular are actually ellipses or B-splines. You cannot make a radius dimension in these cases.
If you have selected geometry in the 3D View: add the correct TechDraw View to the selection by selecting it in the Tree View.
A dimension is added to the View.
The dimension may be dragged to the desired position.
If needed, add tolerances as described on this page.

TechDraw_RedrawPage.d: The TechDraw RedrawPage tool forces a page update despite any contrary settings of the Keep Updated page property, or the Update with 3D and Allow page override preferences.
u: If there are multiple drawing pages in the document: optionally activate the desired page or select it in the Tree View.
If there are multiple drawing pages in the document and you have not yet selected a page, the Page Chooser dialog box opens:

TechDraw_RichTextAnnotation.d: The TechDraw RichTextAnnotation tool adds a formatted annotation block to a Leaderline or a View.
u: If there are multiple drawing pages in the document: optionally activate the desired page by selecting it in the Tree View.
To attach the RichTextAnnotation to a Leaderline, select the line in the Tree View or on the page.
If there are multiple drawing pages in the document and you have not yet activated a page, the Page Chooser dialog box opens:
A task panel opens.
The task panel allows quick entry of text.
The Start Rich Text Editor button opens a full featured editor:

TechDraw_SectionView.d: The TechDraw SectionView tool inserts a cross-section view based on an existing Part View.
u: Select a Part View in the 3D View or Tree View.
A task panel opens which will help calculate the various properties. Reasonable values for the view Direction are calculated, but these can be changed.

TechDraw_ShareView.d: The TechDraw ShareView tool makes a View and all its dependents (Balloons, Dimensions, etc) visible on a second Page.
u: Optionally select a View, a from Page and a to Page. The pages must be selected in that order.
A dialog will open to allow you to select a View, from Page and to Page.

TechDraw_ShowAll.d: The TechDraw ShowAll tool is intended to temporarily show, and then hide, invisible lines in a View. Lines can be made invisible with the TechDraw DecorateLine tool. Note that "invisible" is a cosmetic state, not to be confused with hidden lines which are geometric constructs.
u: Select a View with invisible lines on a Page or in the Tree View.
All invisible lines in the View are either shown or hidden.
TechDraw_ShowAll.m: TechDraw → Add Lines → Toggle Edge Visibility

TechDraw_SpreadsheetView.d:
The TechDraw SpreadsheetView tool allows you to place a view of a selected spreadsheet on a TechDraw page.

(v1.0): The TechDraw View tool can also create a Spreadsheet View.
u: Select a spreadsheet in the Tree View.
If there are multiple drawing pages in the document: optionally add the desired page to the selection by selecting it in the Tree View.
If there are multiple drawing pages in the document, and if no page is displayed in the Main View Area and you have not yet selected a page, the Page Chooser dialog box opens:
A Spreadsheet View is inserted.
Adjust the cell range of the view by changing its DataCell Start and DataCell End properties.
TechDraw_SpreadsheetView.m: TechDraw → Views From Other Workbenches → Spreadsheet View

TechDraw_StackBottom.d:
The TechDraw StackBottom tool moves Views to the bottom of the stacking order. The stacking order controls the apparent depth of Views on a page.

See TechDraw StackTop.

TechDraw_StackDown.d:
The TechDraw StackDown tool moves Views down one level in the stacking order. The stacking order controls the apparent depth of Views on a page.

See TechDraw StackTop.

TechDraw_StackTop.d: The TechDraw StackTop tool moves Views to the top of the stacking order. The stacking order controls the apparent depth of Views on a page.
u: Select one or more Views on a Page or in the Tree View. For this tool, and TechDraw StackBottom, the selection order is relevant.
The ViewStack Order property of the Views is changed.

TechDraw_StackUp.d:
The TechDraw StackUp tool moves Views up one level in the stacking order. The stacking order controls the apparent depth of Views on a page.

See TechDraw StackTop.

TechDraw_SurfaceFinishSymbols.d: The TechDraw SurfaceFinishSymbols tool adds a surface finish symbol to a page.
u: Select an existing view.
A task panel opens.
Specify the required symbol by clicking one of the 6 symbol buttons.
Optionally change the Symbol angle.
Select the ISO or the ASME style.
Select and/or enter the required attributes.

TechDraw_Symbol.d:
The TechDraw Symbol tool inserts a Symbol object. A Symbol is a stripped down view that contains only a single SVG file complying with the svg-tiny specification (see TechDraw Templates).

A Symbol can be anything that helps annotate a drawing and that doesn't need to be further modified, it may however contain editable texts.

(v1.0): The TechDraw View tool can also create a Symbol.
u: If there are multiple drawing pages in the document: optionally activate the desired page by selecting it in the Tree View.
If there are multiple drawing pages in the document and you have not yet activated a page, the Page Chooser dialog box opens:
A file browser opens.
Select an SVG file.
A symbol is inserted.
Optionally change its DataScale property to adjust its size.

TechDraw_ToggleFrame.d: The TechDraw ToggleFrame tool turns the display of View frames, labels and vertices on or off.
u: If there are multiple drawing pages in the document: optionally activate the desired page by selecting it in the Tree view.
If there are multiple drawing pages in the document and you have not yet activated a page, the Page Chooser dialog box opens:
Currently visible View frames will disappear. Currently invisible View frames will appear.
It is possible for different Views to be in different states of frame display. If this happens, invoke this tool once or twice to resynchronize the Views.
TechDraw_ToggleFrame.m: TechDraw → TechDraw Views → Turn View Frames On/Off

TechDraw_VerticalDimension.d:
The TechDraw VerticalDimension tool adds a vertical dimension to a View. The dimension may be the vertical distance between two points or the vertical length of a straight edge. As with the TechDraw LengthDimension tool it is also possible to select two edges or a point and an edge, but these options make less sense for this tool.

For more information see TechDraw LengthDimension.

TechDraw_VerticalExtentDimension.d:
The TechDraw VerticalExtentDimension tool adds a linear dimension to a View. The dimension extends from the bottom most point on the selected objects to the top most point.

For more information see TechDraw HorizontalExtentDimension.

TechDraw_View.d:
The TechDraw View tool adds a representation of one or more objects to a Drawing page. (v1.0): It can create a Projection Group Item (a single view), a Projection Group, a Spreadsheet View, an Arch View, a Symbol or an Image View.

In 0.21 and below the tool can only create a Part View, which is very similar to a Projection Group Item.

TechDraw_WeldSymbol.d: The TechDraw WeldingSymbol tool adds welding specifications to an existing leader line.
u: Select an existing leaderline.
A task panel opens.
Specify the welding symbols and accompanying text to be added to the leader line.

Templater_AuxView.d: The Templater AuxView tool adds an auxiliary view to the active TechDraw drawing page based on a straight line in an existing base view. This line, together with the Z-axis of the base view, defines the orientation of the auxiliary view. The end vertices of the line can either be selected separately or derived from a selected edge.
u: Select two vertices or one edge in an existing view.
A new auxiliary view, an AuxView object, is created. Its line of sight is perpendicular to the line between the selected vertices.
The Auxiliary view settings task panel opens.
Click Ok to close the task panel and finish the tool.
Drag the view and the annotation elements to their final positions.

Templater_NewTemplateMulti.d: The Templater NewTemplateMulti tool creates a small example template and inserts it as a new drawing page into the active document.
u: The Template settings task panel opens.
Click Ok to close the task panel and finish the tool.
A new template will be saved in the .../Mod/Templater/Resources folder.
If the Insert template option is checked the created template will be displayed in a new TechDraw view.

Templater_NewTemplateWiki.d: The Templater NewTemplateWiki tool creates a small example template and inserts it as a new drawing page into the active document. See the TechDraw TemplateGenerator tutorial to learn how an almost identical template is scripted.
u: The Template settings task panel opens.
Click Ok to close the task panel and finish the tool.
A new template will be saved in the .../Mod/Templater/Resources folder.
The created template will be displayed in a new TechDraw view.

Templater_ToleranceFrame.d: The Templater ToleranceFrame tool creates a tolerance frame or a datum frame as an SVG file and adds it to the selected view.
u: Select a view or any geometry inside the view.
The Feature frame settings task panel opens.
Select a Tolerance Type for a tolerance frame, or type a single (upper case) letter for a datum frame.
If a tolerance type was selected adjust the following values: (they will be ignored for a datum frame)
Click Ok to close the task panel and finish the tool.
A NewSymbol.svg file will be saved in the .../Mod/Templater/Resources folder and added to the selected view as a new FeatureFrame object.

View_Measure_Clear_All.d: The View Measure Clear All command clears the active 3D view's Part measurements.

View_Measure_Toggle_All.d: The View Measure Toggle All command toggles the display of the active 3D view's Part measurements.

WebTools_BimServer.d: This command allows you to interact with a BIMServer instance, open files stored on the BIM server, and save new revisions of those files. BIMServer is a free, open-source server system made to work with IFC files. In its current state, it allows to manage projects with multiple IFC files, and manage revisions. Its highly extensible database system and plugin architecture also allows to design advanced querying/validating tools and intelligent merging workflows.
u: Make sure the above requirements are met, and you have access to a running BIMServer instance.
Select menu Web Tools → BIM Server
Once the connection to the BIMServer has been made, choose a project to work with from the Project drop-down box

WebTools_Git.d:
This command allows to manage the current document with Git. Git is a powerful file version control system, which can manage different versions of files and keep track of the changes.

Git is a complex tool, consider learning the basics of it before using this tool, to avoid wrong operations that can cause data loss. An abundant literature about Git is available and easy to find on the internet.

Prerequisite: To be able to use this command, the gitpython package must be installed on your system. On most linux distributions, gitpython is available from the standard software repositories as gitpython or python-git.
u: Make sure the Report view is open since Git messages will be printed there.
Save the current active document making sure the saved file is inside an existing git repository. It can be in a subdirectory.
Select menu Web Tools → Git
This opens up a Task panel in the Combo view.

WebTools_Sketchfab.d: This tool allows you to export and upload objects to your SketchFab account. (v0.17)
u: Make yourself an account on SketchFab if you don't have one yet. Free accounts are just fine, paid accounts add more features like the possibility to have private models and bigger maximum upload sizes
Prepare a model you wish to upload
Click on from the main toolbar in the WebTools
Fill in the fields. Name and API key are mandatory
Click the "Upload" button

Web_BrowserBack.d: Use the Web BrowserBack command to go to the previous page in the list of visited web pages.

Web_BrowserNext.d: Use the Web BrowserNext command to go to the next page in the list of visited web pages.

Web_BrowserRefresh.d: The Web BrowserRefresh command updates the current web page.

Web_BrowserSetURL.d: Use the Web BrowserSetURL command to change the URL of the active Web tab.
u: Make sure a Web tab is active, use the Web OpenWebsite command to create one if required.
A prompt line opens with the current URL.
Edit the URL and press Enter to finish.
The new URL is loaded.

Web_BrowserStop.d: Use the Web BrowserStop command to stop loading the current web page.

Web_BrowserZoomIn.d: Use the Web BrowserZoomIn command to zoom in on the current web page.

Web_BrowserZoomOut.d: Use the Web BrowserZoomOut command to zoom out on the current web page.

Web_OpenWebsite.d: The Web OpenWebsite command opens the FreeCAD website in the current Web tab, or in a new tab if the current one is not a Web tab.

Arch_Floor.d:
The Arch Floor tool is a special type of FreeCAD group object that has a couple of additional properties particularly suited for building floors. Particularly, they have a height property, that its children objects (walls and structures) can use to set their own height automatically. They are mostly used to organize your model.

As of (v0.18) the Arch Floor is derived entirely from the Arch BuildingPart object, which is a general container to organize a building model not limited to floors or storeys. Older Floor objects can be converted to the new type by right clicking on them and choosing Convert to BuildingPart.
u: Optionally, select one or more objects to be included in your new floor.

Assembly_ExportASMT.d: The Assembly ExportASMT tool exports the currently active assembly to an ASMT file.

CAM_Pocket_3D.d: This command inserts a path 3D Pocket object into the Job. This operation takes into account the bottom surface of the pocket, as well as selected walls that are not vertical. In its current state, this operation is used to rough out a pocket with non-vertical walls and/or non-horizontal bottom. A common finishing technique is to use a ball end mill with the experimental 3D Surface operation.
u: From within a Job, select one or more Faces from the Job Model to include as the Base Geometry.
Choose a Tool controller from the pop up selection dialogue window.
Add or subtract Base Geometry elements as needed to configure the Operation.
Check the Depths tab to ensure the Start Depth, Finish Depth, and Step Down percentage are correct. The Final Depth is determined by the Body Geometry selection and is not modifiable.
Check the Heights tab to ensure the Safe and Clearance Heights are appropriate.

Check the Operation tab where the Tool controller can be re-selected, the Cut mode can be configured for Climb or Conventional milling, the Pattern can be set, the Step Over percentage can be adjusted, and Pass…

CfdOF_CFD_Mesh.d: The CFD Mesh dialogue panel is used to build the mesh from the geometry.
u: Select the Geometry that you wish to mesh.
Both the button and theCfdOF → CFD Mesh‏‎ menu option, become available.
Click on either the:
The CFD Mesh dialogue panel will open.
\[Geometry Name\]\_Mesh will be created in the tree.

CfdOF_Fluid_Properties.d: The Fluid Properties dialogue panel is used to input the properties of the fluids to be used in the simulation. These can be manually imputed, or selected from a fluid library. When a Single Phase Physics Model has been selected, only one fluid can be added. In the case of a Multiphase Physics Model, multiple fluids may be added.

CfdOF_Mesh_Refinement.d: The Mesh refinement dialogue panel is used to add surface, volume and extrusion refinements to the background mesh.
u: Select the \[Geometry Name\]\_Mesh within the tree
Both the button and theCfdOF → Mesh refinement‏‎ menu option, become available.
Click on either the:
The Mesh refinement dialogue panel will open.
MeshRefinement will be created in the tree below the \[Geometry Name\]\_Mesh.
Multiple Mesh refinements can be added to the tree. Each additional Mesh refinement will be named MeshRefinementxxx where xxx is an incrementing number from 001.

CfdOF_Physics_Model.d: The Physics Model is used to select the solver that is to be used in the CFD simulation.

FEM_ConstraintElectrostaticPotential.d: Creates a FEM boundary condition for the electrostatic potential. To be used together with the Electrostatic, Electricforce, Magnetodynamic or Magnetodynamic2D equation.
u: Press the Electrostatic potential boundary condition button or use the menu Model → Electromagnetic boundary conditions → Electrostatic potential boundary condition.
In the 3D view select the object the boundary condition should be applied to.
FEM_ConstraintElectrostaticPotential.m: Model → Electromagnetic boundary conditions → Electrostatic potential boundary condition

FEM_SolverCalculixCxxtools.d:
CalculiXccxTools enables usage of the CalculiX solver. It may be used for:

  • Setting analysis parameters
  • Selecting working directory
  • Running the CalculiX solver
u: A CalculiXcxxTools solver object is created automatically with the creation of an Analysis container.
Optionally change the properties of the CalculiXcxxTools solver object in the Property editor.
Double click the CalculiXcxxTools solver object.
Select the Analysis type.
Click the Write.inp file button.
Click the Run CalculiX button.

Materials_Edit.d: The Materials Edit tool provides access to the new material editor implemented as part of the Material handling system improvements made for FreeCAD 1.0. The new materials system can be used in multiple workbenches, also for appearance properties.
u: The new material editor can currently be accessed by either:
Select a material from the multilevel list on the left. The following categories are available:
Use the three tabs on the right side of the editor to edit the properties of the selected material:
In the General tab, press the New button to create a new material with empty properties, Inherit New to create a new material with properties copied from the selected material or to add a…
Press the OK button to confirm, Save to save the changes or Cancel to cancel them.

Movie_MovieCamera.d:
While the page is under construction, add the Template:UnfinishedDocu template at the top of the page by simply typing:

In this first paragraph give a short description of what the command does. The description can refer to other workbenches such as the Sketcher Workbench. (Editor note: The image is 24px, not 16px)

Remember to use Template:Version, Template:VersionMinus, Template:VersionPlus and Template:Obsolete when applicable.
u: Detailed steps as needed. Some steps may need Keyboard presses while others may require using the mouse to click on a Button.
Set options and press OK.
Movie_MovieCamera.m: Menu → Submenu → Menu text for the command

Reinforcement_StirrupRebar.d:
The Reinforcement StirrupRebar tool allows the user to create a set of stirrup reinforcing bars inside an Arch Structure object.

This tool is part of the Reinforcement Workbench, an external workbench that can be installed with the Addon Manager.
u: Select any face of a previously created Arch Structure object.
Then select Stirrup from the rebar tools.
A task panel will pop-out on the left side of the screen as shown below.
Select the desired orientation.
Populate the inputs like 'Left Cover', 'Right Cover', 'Top Cover', 'Bottom Cover', 'Front Cover', 'Bent Angle', 'Bent Factor', 'Rounding' and 'Diameter' of the rebar.
Select the mode of distribution either 'Amount' or 'Spacing'.

Robot_Export.d: Export a robot program file. Export can either be a KUKA compact subroutine or a KUKA full subroutine.
u: Select robot and trajectory in the Tree view.

Std_BoxElementSelection.d:
The Std BoxElementSelection command selects faces from a user defined rectangular area, a box, in the 3D view.

Note that if a whole object falls inside the rectangle, the object itself, instead of its faces, is selected. To avoid this create two box selections for each object (hold down Ctrl while dragging the 2nd rectangle), or use the Part BoxSelection command instead.
u: Do one of the following:

Std_Import.d:
The Std Import command imports geometry from a different file format into the active document. Many file formats are supported and for some formats multiple import options exist. See Import Export for more information.

(v0.21)

: If an image format is selected the command will create an Image Plane.
u: Optionally select the correct file format in the dialog box.
Select a file.
